headline: Punjab news: EC orders FIR against Akali Dal Patiala in-charge over threats to minister
content: Following the directions of the Punjab State Election Commission, the Patiala police have registered an FIR against the Shiromani Akali Dal’s (SAD) Patiala Rural halqa in-charge, Jaspal Singh Bittu Chatha, for allegedly issuing threats to a Cabinet minister and serving officers involved with the polling process. Notably, the model code of conduct is in place ahead of repolling in Patiala municipal wards.According to the information, an FIR has been registered at civil lines police station under section 192 (malignantly giving illegal provocation that is likely to cause rioting), 353(1)(b) (statements conducing to public mischief), 352 (intentional insult) and 351(3) (criminal intimidation) of the BNS.Senior police officers confirmed that though the offences were bailable, if proven, the accused could face a jail term ranging from two to seven years.As per the FIR, a copy of which is with The Tribune, the state election commission brought a video clip to the notice of the district electoral officer. “Please find enclosed a video clip received at the Commission today, wherein a person is seen interacting with the press and allegedly issuing threats to a Minister and government officers who are directly involved in current election process”, says the complaint mentioned in the FIR.The complaint further read, “The Commission desires you to look into and take action as per following: 1. To ascertain genuineness of the video clip; 2. To ascertain identity of the gentlemen in video; 3. To take necessary action, including preventive measures as necessary, and lodging of FIR under the relevant sections of BNS and election laws as may be applicable”.Speaking to The Tribune, Bittu Chatha said the SAD was not afraid of such FIRs and he would continue to raise his voice against the government. “Anyone who highlights the government’s failures is booked in cases on flimsy grounds,” he said.A senior police officer closely monitoring the case said the Deputy Commissioner can order that the accused be kept away from the electoral process till voting is complete.Polling will take place on November 28 from 8 am to 4 pm. The re-elections follow a Supreme Court decision ordering fresh polls in wards where alleged irregularities were reported during the previous municipal elections.

headline: AAP banks on infra upgrade as road link remains Achilles’ heel of Bhoa near Pathankot
content: Cabinet minister Lal Chand Kataruchak is banking on infrastructure upgrade, which he says can steer him to victory in the 2027 Assembly elections.The minister, who is seeking a second term after he first carved out a win in the 2022 elections, has brought in Rs 4.50 crore for development projects in the past five years.Kataruchak, a politically non-controversial figure, has enjoyed unbridled power ever since the AAP assumed office. He is among the handful of ministers who have remained in the cabinet since 2022 without being dropped.Through improved infrastructure, like establishing new link roads, provision of quality education and digital connectivity, this rural Assembly constituency, considered to be the most backward one in Punjab, is now transforming itself into a self-sustaining hub of opportunity.Bhoa is a geographically remote area located in Pathankot district. Heavy, overloaded tippers and trucks, constantly ferrying material extracted from the Ravi and Chakki riverbeds, had broken and degraded village infrastructure, disrupting normal life for residents.“In the last Assembly poll, Kataruchak won after he tailored his campaignto address the socio-economic needs of the voters, including the development of link roads.Link roads are not built to handle the weight of heavy mining trucks and tippers. Hence, the road infrastructure often degrades and breaks. He has focused on issues which make people’s lives better,” said an ex-MLA.Once the minister assumed power, he warned PWD officials and people engaged in mining, both legal and illegal, that they would have to face the music if roads continued to be broken. This had the requisite effect as mining vehicles started avoiding these roads and instead took detours to reach their destinations.Ex-MLA Joginder Pal won in 2017, but failed to retain his seat because he did not focus on the link roads, the Achilles’ heel of Bhoa.“He was a Congress MLA and his party remained in power from 2017 to 2022. However, the issue of roads was never discussed or taken up,” said Tara Devi, a resident of Bamiyal village, located near the International Border (IB).Kataruchak also impressed upon the Cabinet to release Rs 62 crore for the construction of three bridges. One of the bridges has come up on Jalali Nullah, a seasonal rivulet. The bridge now joins three link roads and has considerably shortened the distance between several villages.Link roads, bridges and potable water are the prime issues on which the 2027 polls will be contested. The residents admit that the minister has definitely scored in these three areas.

headline: Congress needs more than an anti-BJP campaign
content: RAHUL GANDHI, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, dubbed as Pappu (incompetent and naïve) in a targeted offensive by the BJP since 2014, when the saffron party launched its successful campaign to capture power in India, has arrived on the centre stage of politics.

headline: BJP slams RJD for tearing PM Modi posters after bridge inauguration in Bihar
content: PATNA Ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders of Bihar on Sunday (November 22, 2026) slammed Opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) supporters for allegedly tearing the posters and banners of Prime Minister Narendra Modi soon after the inauguration of six lane bridge named after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi/ Nitish Kumar | The man who mastered political engineering storyline 1 In several videos going viral on social media platforms, RJD workers allegedly were found tearing down banners, posters, and BJP flags that were put up on the bridge soon after the departure of the Prime Minister. PM Modi inaugurates bridge named after Nitish Kumar in Bihar’s Vaishali PM Modi inaugurates bridge named after Nitish Kumar in Bihar’s Vaishali The bridge connects Kachhi Dargah on National Highway 22 in Patna district with Bidupur on NH-322 in Vaishali. It comprises a 9.76-km main bridge and 10 km of approach roads, officials said PM Modi inaugurates bridge named after Nitish Kumar in Bihar’s Vaishali storyline 1 In the viral video, a large group of young people, including children carrying RJD flags, shouted slogans against the Prime Minister and expressed their support for the leader of the Opposition in the Bihar Legislative Assembly, Tejashwi Yadav, and RJD chief Lalu Prasad. Mr. Yadav was even invited to attend the programme since he represents the Raghopur assembly constituency. After the Prime Minister’s departure, the police barricades were removed, and the bridge was opened to the general public. Following this, RJD supporters drove onto the bridge, waved RJD flags, and began tearing down the BJP’s flags, posters, and banners. Passersby also faced difficulties as the alleged RJD supporters created a ruckus on the bridge for nearly an hour. Reacting to the incident, Bihar BJP spokesperson Niraj Kumar Sharma said, “While all of Bihar is celebrating new connectivity and progress, the RJD remains mired in the old politics of disruption, tearing down posters, and nepotism. Criticism and fights over credit in the name of development have happened before, but this kind of disruption to public property and the bridge after the inauguration exposes an anti-development mindset,” He further said, “The people of Bihar want bridges, roads, and jobs. Not jungle raj and the politics of disruption. The NDA government will keep steadily advancing development work.” Mr. Modi inaugurated the 9.76 km-long Nitish Setu over the River Ganga in Vaishali district on November 21, in the presence of Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. Built at the cost of ₹4,280 crore, the bridge connects Kacchi Dargah in Patna to Bidupur in Vaishali, ending a decades-long wait for the hundreds of thousands of people in Raghopur Diara. Mr. Sharma pointed out that this bridge will make travel between North and South Bihar easier, and it will also ease traffic pressure on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu, and open up new opportunities in agricultural produce, trade, and employment. Senior BJP leader and Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha also attacked RJD, alleging that the people who laid the foundation of the RJD came forward posing as messiahs of the poor, and they went on to loot the poor- to the extent that they even embezzled the fodder meant for animals. “So, what more can you expect from people with such a mentality,”Mr. Sinha said. Another BJP leader and party spokesperson Kuntal Krishna said that RJD has not changed a bit, neither mindset nor the mentality. “RJD was the party of goons and lumpen elements, and it has remained the same even today. On the one hand, when the PM was offering development and giving a message of prosperity, the RJD workers, on the other hand, were busy with hooliganism and creating anarchy. This is the real face of the party and its leaders. Only for this reason, the people of Bihar threw RJD out of power,” Mr. Kuntal said.

headline: BJP targets Congress after traders’ body thanks PM Modi for cautionary advice on buying gold
content: New Delhi The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Sunday (November 22, 2026) targeted the Congress after a traders’ body thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his advice earlier this year to postpone gold purchases. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ “When PM @narendramodi appealed to the people of India to defer the purchase of gold, Congress called it a ‘death warrant’. With gold prices falling globally, traders who followed PM Modi’s advice saved ₹65 lakh per kg of gold! The traders’ body has thanked the Prime Minister today!” BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said. watch: PM Modi: ‘A year ago, I urged people not to buy gold; they followed my advice, and prices fell’ watch: PM Modi: ‘A year ago, I urged people not to buy gold; they followed my advice, and prices fell’ Prime Minister Narendra Modi says people followed his year-old appeal to avoid buying gold unless necessary, claiming that the move helped them save money as gold prices fell. watch: PM Modi: ‘A year ago, I urged people not to buy gold; they followed my advice, and prices fell’ shorts 1 “The Gandhi-Vadra family, which lived a lavish lifestyle when the majority of India’s population was poor, should take a master class in economic management and simple living from PM Modi,” Mr. Bhandari said in a post on social media platform X, demanding that the Congress apologise to traders for “misleading them and creating panic”. His remarks came after the Chamber of Trade and Industry wrote to Mr. Modi, thanking him for his advice to people in May 2026 against purchasing gold. The group said the advice saved lakhs of jewellers, traders, and investors from huge losses as gold prices fell from ₹1.90 crore to ₹1.25 crore, a decline of ₹65 lakh per kg. The dip in gold prices had brought relief to families during the ongoing wedding season, it said. PM’s advisory on gold hasn’t yet made a difference to footfall, say jewellers PM’s advisory on gold hasn’t yet made a difference to footfall, say jewellers However, it has impacted consumer sentiment, pushing some buyers into a cautious or wait-and-watch mode, gold traders say PM’s advisory on gold hasn’t yet made a difference to footfall, say jewellers storyline 1 In another post, Mr. Bhandari cited data to stress that India’s economic transformation under Mr. Modi had been “phenomenal”. He said the country’s GDP was $1.86 trillion in 2013, while it rose to $4.1 trillion in 2026; forex reserves increased from $295 billion to $690 billion; exports from $450 billion to $825 billion; manufacturing output from $280 billion to $500 billion; and defence exports from ₹686 crore to ₹38,622 crore. The BJP leader said salaried employment had expanded, with the number of women in salaried employment rising from one crore to four crores.

headline: Raut alleges BJP offers funds to secure support for Delimitation Bill
content: Mumbai Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut alleged at a conference on November 22 that the Bharatiya Janata Party is offering ₹150 crore to Members of Parliament to gain backing for the Delimitation Bill, while also alleging that the government is delaying the session of the Parliament because it lacks the support of 40 to 45 MPs to pass the legislation and is attempting to pressure parties or buy lawmakers. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/shiv-sena-uddhav-balasaheb-thackeray/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/rajya-sabha-mp-sanjay-raut/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ Editorial | Deservedly dead: On the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/editorial/deservedly-dead-the-hindu-editorial-on-the-defeat-of-the-constitution-131st-amendment-bill-2026/article70875239.ece The Delimitation Bill contains a provision to increase the number of seats in the Lok Sabha to 850, which has resulted in a dispute between the National Democratic Alliance and the INDIA bloc, where the National Democratic Alliance states that carrying out delimitation is required by the Constitution to reflect data from a census and to enable reservation for women, while the Opposition demands implementation of 33% reservation for women within a Lok Sabha that contains 543 members. PM, HM still searching for ‘supertainted’ two-thirds majority for delimitation bill, says Congress PM, HM still searching for ‘supertainted’ two-thirds majority for delimitation bill, says Congress Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented till the Viksit Bharat objective is achieved PM, HM still searching for ‘supertainted’ two-thirds majority for delimitation bill, says Congress storyline 1 Sanjay Raut alleged during the conference that an MP would receive ₹150 crore upon breaking away from a party to support the Delimitation Bill without facing disqualification, and he claimed that a Minister from Maharashtra has taken responsibility for the situation and promised to provide funds for the purpose, further alleging that the government has delayed the session of the Parliament because it does not concern itself with the nation, the Constitution, or the Parliament, adding that if parties do not defect, MPs would be purchased, and he referenced a statement regarding a rate on an exchange of ₹150 crore per MP.

headline: BJP Rajya Sabha MP BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies in Delhi
content: Mumbai BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute, who was elected to the Upper House earlier this year, died following a cardiac arrest at a hospital in New Delhi, family sources said on Sunday (November 22, 2026). https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ He was 72. Mr. Wadkute was admitted to AIIMS in the national capital on November 20 after complaining of a cough. He suffered a heart attack around 6 p.m. on Saturday (November 21, 2026) and died during treatment around 11.45 p.m., they said. Hailing from Parbhani in Maharashtra's Marathwada region, Mr. Wadkute was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April this year and had previously served as a member of the State Legislative Council from June 2014 to October 2019. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/maharashtra/ Condoling the demise of the senior leader, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said his death was the loss of a simple and dedicated personality in politics who was deeply concerned about grassroots welfare. Mr. Fadnavis noted that Mr. Wadkute had held several organisational responsibilities in the BJP in Hingoli district and worked extensively for the Dhangar community. He also served as chairman of the Sheep and Goat Development Corporation and made his mark in the cooperative sector, the Chief Minister added. President, PM condole Wadkute’s passing President Droupadi Murmu mourned the demise Mr. Wadkute and remembered him for making valuable contributions to the development of Maharashtra and the nation. “Deeply saddened by the demise of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute Ji. He was dedicated to the cause of public welfare and made valuable contributions to the development of Maharashtra and the nation. My heartfelt condolences to his family members, admirers and well-wishers,” the President said in a post on X. Also condoling Mr. Wadkute’s death, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that he will be remembered for his contribution to society and service to the poor and downtrodden. “Deeply saddened by the passing of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Wadkute ji. He will be remembered for his contribution to society and emphasis on serving the poor and downtrodden,” Mr. Modi said in a post on ‘X’. The Prime Minister said equally noteworthy were Mr. Wadkute’s efforts to strengthen the BJP in Maharashtra. Deeply saddened by the passing of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Wadkute Ji. He will be remembered for his contribution to society and emphasis on serving the poor and downtrodden. Equally noteworthy were his efforts to strengthen the BJP in Maharashtra. My thoughts are with his family and admirers. Om Shanti. राज्यसभा खासदार श्री रामराव वडकुते जी यांच्या निधनाचे वृत्त ऐकून अतिशय दुःख झाले. समाजसेवेतील त्यांचे योगदान तसेच गरीब आणि वंचित घटकांच्या सेवेसाठी त्यांनी दिलेले प्राधान्य यासाठी त्यांचे सदैव स्मरण केले जाईल. महाराष्ट्रात भाजप पक्ष संघटना बळकट करण्यासाठी त्यांनी केलेले प्रयत्नही तितकेच उल्लेखनीय होते. या दुःखद प्रसंगी त्यांच्या कुटुंबीयांच्या आणि चाहत्यांच्या दुःखात मी सहभागी आहे. ओम शांती.— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 22, 2026 Vice-President and Rajya Sabha Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan expressed grief over Mr. Wadkute's passing, saying his contributions to public life and service to the people will always be remembered. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said, "The passing of Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute ji is deeply saddening. In this hour of grief, my heartfelt condolences are with the bereaved family. May the departed soul rest in peace and may the family find the strength to bear this immense loss." Maharashtra Assembly Speaker Rahul Narwekar, in a post on X, said, "The news of the tragic passing of Hon. Ramraoji Wadkute, Member of the Rajya Sabha, in Delhi following a severe heart attack is deeply painful and heartbreaking. At this difficult time, we share in the grief of the Wadkute family." According to family sources, Mr. Wadkute's body will be kept for last respects in Parbhani on Monday (November 23, 2026), and will be taken to Hingoli, where the last rites will be performed on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
