headline: Congress corruption being exposed by its MLAs: KTR
content: HYDERABAD BRS working president K.T. Rama Rao alleged widespread corruption in the Congress government, and said that its own legislators were exposing the commission-based system, citing the recent statements of Congress MLAs Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy and Anirudh Reddy. Allegations relating to intimidation of industrialists and temple lands, including remarks by former Minister Konda Surekha, also pointed to the state of affairs in the government, he argued. Mr. Rama Rao, who was addressing a public meeting in Warangal on Sunday, declared that the countdown had begun for the Congress government and asserted that BRS president K. Chandrasekhar Rao would return as the Chief Minister in 2028. Questioning the Congress government’s claims of increasing social security pensions, he said it had removed 4.71 lakh existing beneficiaries while adding only 4.63 lakh new beneficiaries. The BRS MLA dismissed Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s claim on empowering women, and reminded that Congress had promised a monthly assistance of ₹2,500 to women but had failed to implement it even after 36 months in office. According to him, the accumulated dues amounted to ₹85,500 for each eligible woman. He also referred to other promises like one tola of gold under Kalyana Lakshmi, scooters for girl students and financial assistance ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹10 lakh for students. “If the promises are fulfilled and women are made financially secure, I will quit politics permanently,” he said. Targeting Mr. Revanth Reddy, he said the Chief Minister was more interested in making personal remarks against KCR than addressing farmers’ problems, unemployment, drought and industrial development. ‘Warangal neglected’ KTR also accused the Congress government of putting Warangal’s development on hold over the last three years. The BRS government had sanctioned six government medical colleges and the 24-storey super-speciality hospital with 2,250 beds and 35 medical departments. Similarly, the BRS government had brought IT companies and the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park, generating employment for local youth, he said. He accused the government of failing to utilise Godavari waters effectively and alleged that poor management of the Devadula pumping stations and Kannepalli motors was affecting irrigation.

headline: Congress will return to power in Telangana for second term with 90 seats and one crore votes: Revanth Reddy
content: Hyderabad Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has expressed confidence that the Congress will return to power in Telangana for a second consecutive term, asserting that the party would win 90 Assembly seats with one crore votes in the next elections. Addressing the Extended Executive Committee meeting of the Telangana Congress on Sunday, he said the party leadership was preparing strategies to strengthen the organisation at the grassroots and take the government’s welfare and development initiatives to the people after Sankranti. Recalling the party’s difficult days when he took over as Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president, Mr. Revanth Reddy said the BRS leadership had allegedly used coercion and police cases to force several Congress MLAs and leaders to join the ruling party. Former Chief Minister K. Chandrashekhar Rao had even declared that there was no Congress in Telangana and that he would not allow the party to revive, he said. However, the Congress undertook a digital membership drive and enrolled 48 lakh members in 90 days, the highest by any party in the country. This resulted in Congress securing 92,35,833 votes and won 64 Assembly seats in the last elections. Mr. Revanth Reddy said the Congress had rewarded those who worked for the organisation citing the examples of Adluri Laxman Kumar, Aadi Srinivas, Medipalli Satyam, Kavvampalli Satyanarayana, Vakiti Srihari and Makkan Singh Raj Thakur. The Chief Minister cautioned party leaders against expecting positions merely by moving around Gandhi Bhavan or visiting Delhi. “The place to go is not Delhi but villages and the homes of the poor,” he said. Warns indiscipline He said the party was closely monitoring the conduct and public statements of its leaders, including what they said in public and behind the scenes. The political balance sheet would be prepared once every five years, at election time, and the contribution of every leader and worker would be assessed. Taking a dig at BRS leaders, he said the party’s claims of returning to power were misplaced. Congress would counter the BRS campaign by taking its achievements to the people. He urged Telangana Congress leaders to take responsibility for making Rahul Gandhi the Prime Minister and said the party would aim to win all 15 Lok Sabha seats in the State. Telangana had stood by the Congress during its difficult periods, including the period following the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, who was representing Medak as an MP at the time, he said.

headline: 50 crore out of poverty, yet some don’t want to talk about that: PM Narendra Modi
content: In an apparent dig at the Opposition, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said some individuals still hesitate to acknowledge that 50 crore people have been pulled out of poverty in the country. Addressing BJP workers virtually during a post-Diwali ‘Sneh Milan’ programme organised by the party across all 182 assembly constituencies in Gujarat, he said the achievement reflected the success of his government's policies and efforts. “All those who sacrificed their lives for independence, all those who dedicated their lives to freedom, all those who spent their youth in jails for independence, wherever their souls may be, today they must be the happiest seeing this World Bank report, thinking, ‘finally, poverty is leaving my country’,” he said. According to a World Bank report, India's extreme poverty rate dropped sharply to 2.6% in 2023 from 27.1% in 2011, with the country lifting an estimated 496 million people out of poverty. “After a thousand years of slavery — which had left us utterly miserable — for the first time, 50 crore people have come out of the poverty line. There can be no greater satisfaction in life, and no greater achievement than this,” Modi said. However, some people were still reluctant to acknowledge the achievement, he said. Taking a swipe at the opposition over the issue, he added that many people do not like to talk about it. “Our intentions are correct, our policies are correct, our direction is correct, and there is no lack of effort on our part. A new era is set to begin in the life of every single citizen of this country. The fact that 50 crore people are emerging from poverty is a sign of this new era. I can foresee that the dreams we speak of — the ‘golden age’ we envision — will be witnessed by the generations to come,” he said. The BJP had organised the event across all 182 Assembly constituencies in Gujarat. CM Bhupendra Patel listened to the PM’s virtual address in his Ghatlodia constituency. Modi said this year’s Diwali was significant for him as it marked 25 years since he became Gujarat’s CM in October 2001. Modi said that they have played an important role in the transformation of Gujarat in the last 25 years and asked them to resolve to strengthen people’s confidence in making Gujarat the biggest contributor in making the country developed. In the over 20-minute speech to the party workers, Modi recollected his older days as Gujarat CM and how the state was transformed through initiatives. He also mentioned that recently he completed 25 years in office; first as Gujarat CM and then as Prime Minister. Acknowledging his indebtedness to party workers, Modi said, “Had it not been for such immense support and cooperation from these workers, we would not have been able to serve Gujarat to this extent; therefore, today I also acknowledge my indebtedness to these workers. It is because of their hard work that we are able to serve Gujarat, the nation, and various other states today.” He said that Gujarat’s identity earlier was only related to ‘business’. But now, the scope of development has been widened greatly to sectors like agriculture, dairy, industries, semiconductor, green energy, modern infrastructure etc. “For the creation of a developed India, Gujarat is set to take a giant leap forward; and we have to strengthen people’s confidence that let us become the state with the largest contribution toward building a developed India.” —With PTI inputs

headline: PM Modi, Balendra Shah meet today: Focus on economic and energy ties
content: An economic vision document, a proposed financial assistance package to tide over post-flood reconstruction in Nepal, connectivity including train service between Ayodhya and Janakpur, new air routes, energy cooperation, training for Nepal's start-ups and cricket team, and an offshore IIT campus — these are some of the issues on the agenda as Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah began his first India visit on Sunday. Shah will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday — their first one-on-one in-person meeting since he assumed office as Nepal Prime Minister in March this year. While this is Shah’s first bilateral visit abroad, the two PMs have had phone interactions in the past. Modi and Shah are scheduled to inaugurate, virtually, several completed initiatives and carry out foundation stone-laying ceremonies for some new projects. A number of forward-looking bilateral documents, across diverse areas, are expected to be concluded, sources said. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar called on Shah on Sunday evening. “Privileged to call on PM Balendra Shah of Nepal on his visit to New Delhi this evening. India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal. Look forward to his engagements with PM Narendra Modi tomorrow,” Jaishankar said in a post on X. According to sources, the major outcomes are likely to be in the domains of development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, connectivity, addressing climate change and disaster resilience, infrastructure and technology. Sources said Shah’s visit comes at a time when there is considerable synergy between the national priorities of both countries in terms of economic growth, social development, expansion of infrastructure, adoption of technology, and addressing issues like natural disasters and climate change. “Discussions between the two leaders will provide a political direction, which is expected to chart the course for the bilateral partnership for the coming years. Both sides are expected to review the entire gamut of bilateral relations apart from exploring new dimensions of cooperation,” a source said. On arrival at the Delhi airport, Shah was received by Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada. “Warm welcome to the Prime Minister of Nepal. The visit provides an opportunity to strengthen the enduring and multifaceted partnership between India and Nepal," the Ministry of External Affairs’ official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in a post on X. Shah's 25-hour visit is one of the shortest visits by a Nepalese PM. Since he is on a state visit, Shah will also pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat, and meet President Droupadi Murmu. The economic vision document on the agenda is expected to talk about economic partnership encompassing all major sectors including energy, financial payment linkages and financial assistance. Nepal, which was struck by the devastating flash floods in August this year, is looking at a financial assistance package of US$ 1-2 billion. While the initial ask was learnt to be $1 billion, in recent weeks, it has risen to $2 billion. There will be discussions on the mode - how much will be grant, loans and line of credit. On connectivity, sources said that a new passenger train service will commence between Ayodhya and Janakpur Dham, connecting two of the “most revered centres of the Ramayana tradition, which will stimulate pilgrimage, religious tourism and people-to-people exchanges”. Railway links connecting Jaynagar in Bihar with Kurtha and Bijalpura in Nepal, and Jogbani in Bihar with Nepal Customs Yard in Biratnagar (Nepal) have been developed with India's support. Both sides have been involved in preparations for further extension of these lines, sources said. The two sides are also discussing new possibilities, like the Raxaul (Bihar)-Kathmandu railway link, which could open new avenues for cross-border passenger and freight connectivity, sources said. Nepal is also asking for new air routes connecting two new airports at Pokhara and Bhairahawa in Nepal through Indian airspace, which would mean a cut in flying hours and fuel, making it more economical. But, there is some discussion going on between aviation authorities since India needs access to Nepalese airspace at the Siliguri corridor. Energy cooperation is also on the agenda, since bilateral cooperation in the power sector has been on an upward trajectory, with developments like the agreement for long term power trade that envisages the import of up to 10,000 MW power from Nepal to India over a period of 10 years. India currently imports about 1200 MW of power from Nepal annually. Both sides are augmenting cross-border transmission capacity through new high-capacity lines, sources said. The two sides are also looking at the start-up ecosystem for Nepalese youth. Since 2025, several start-ups in Nepal have received training through the India-Nepal Start-up Partnership Network (IN-SPAN), in collaboration with IIT-Madras and its incubation centre, Pravartak. This programme offers mentorship and networking opportunities. Several have also got further investment offers from Indian incubators. “This will also be part of the discussions, and how to scale it up,” sources said. To create an education ecosystem in Nepal, they are also exploring setting up an offshore campus of IIT - preferably IIT-Kanpur or IIT-Delhi - in Nepal. And to boost sports ties, there is a possibility of Nepal cricket teams being coached by India, and the two sides playing in each other's countries more regularly. In the last three years, India-Nepal sports cooperation, particularly in cricket, has seen growth. The Indian government and BCCI have collaborated with the Cricket Association of Nepal (CAN) to facilitate training at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru (August 2024, 2025 and 2026), as also practice matches for Nepal's national teams. In fact, the Indian Embassy started a short-term fellowship in 2025, under which three U-19 cricketers from Nepal were sent to Bhopal for a month-long training programme.

headline: Cars and government jobs, yet free rations: What Centre’s study reveals
content: An evaluation study commissioned by the Centre has found a 13.2 per cent “inclusion error” among beneficiaries of its free foodgrain scheme, Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY), under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) 2013. The study, conducted during the financial year 2025-26, has found that several households that do not meet the prescribed eligibility criteria set by states continue to receive free foodgrains. These include households owning assets such as houses with three or more rooms, cars and air conditioners, as well as those with family members employed in government jobs. The study, commissioned by the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD), covered 51,303 beneficiary households across rural and urban areas in all 36 states and Union Territories. It found that the inclusion error rate — or share of those not eligible for free foodgrains — was much higher than the national mark in several states, with West Bengal topping the list (39.5 per cent), followed by Tripura (39.2 per cent) and Tamil Nadu (38.7 per cent). In states with high inclusion errors, the study found that the top contributing factors include households having pucca houses with three or more rooms, air conditioners, motor vehicles and government jobs (see chart). The study does not provide a state-wise break-up of the total sample size of 51,303 beneficiaries, but says that a minimum of 550 beneficiaries per state and Union Territory were selected. It defined “inclusion error” as the “households that do not meet the prescribed eligibility criteria continue to receive subsidised food grains”. The findings are significant as the Centre’s food subsidy stood at Rs 2.28 lakh crore, almost half of the total subsidy bill of Rs 4.69 lakh crore, during the financial year 2025-26. The DFPD functions under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and administers the food security law. The Department did not respond to an emailed questionnaire from The Indian Express on the study’s findings. Under the NFSA, the government provides food security to 75 per cent rural and 50 per cent urban households. In absolute terms, the maximum number of people who can be covered by the Act is about 81.35 crore, with the figure at 78.63 crore as of October 2026. “Under NFSA, an inclusion error occurs when households that do not meet the prescribed eligibility criteria continue to receive subsidised food grains. Assessing inclusion errors is important for understanding the effectiveness of beneficiary identification systems and the extent to which programme benefits reach intended vulnerable households,” the report, which was submitted to the Food Department recently, stated. “The concurrent evaluation estimates the overall inclusion error of 13.2% under NFSA. The analysis indicates rural-urban variation, with inclusion error rates of 12.5% in rural areas and 15.6% in urban areas, suggesting broadly consistent targeting performance across geographies. Across beneficiary categories, AAY households exhibit a slightly lower inclusion error (12.2%) than PHH households (13.4%), with a marginally higher error among PHH households in urban areas (15.7%),” it said. AAY households refer to families covered under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY), which constitute the poorest of the poor and are entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per household per month. Priority Households (PHH) are entitled to 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month. “Overall, while variation remains modest, these findings highlight the importance of strengthening beneficiary identification systems, periodic database validation, and dynamic updating mechanisms to further improve targeting efficiency under the NFSA,” it said. The report's findings show that eastern and northeastern states have the highest intensity of error rates. “Some states, including West Bengal (39.5%), Tamil Nadu (38.7%), Tripura (39.2%), and Meghalaya (28.5%), exhibit very high inclusion errors. These findings suggest the need for continued strengthening of eligibility validation, Aadhaar seeding, and periodic reviews of beneficiary databases,” the report said. “States including Bihar (25.5%), Odisha (22.9%), Sikkim (21.9%), Punjab (20.6%), and Maharashtra (20.3%) show moderate-to-high inclusion errors, indicating partial system inefficiencies. States such as Madhya Pradesh (0.5%), Jammu & Kashmir (0.3%), Haryana (1.0%), Delhi (1.0%), and Rajasthan (1.8%) exhibit low inclusion errors, reflecting stronger targeting frameworks, better digitisation, and more effective beneficiary validation systems,” it said. “A clear regional trend emerges in eastern and north-eastern states, such as West Bengal, Tripura, and Meghalaya, which exhibit higher inclusion errors, while northern and western states (e.g., Haryana, Rajasthan, and Gujarat) perform relatively better, suggesting differences in governance capacity, data systems, and implementation rigour,” it said. According to Section 9 of the food security law, the overall number of beneficiaries is determined by the Centre but under Section 10, the responsibility for identifying households on the ground and preparing guidelines for it lies with the states. The beneficiary identification criteria differ from state to state. “The estimation of inclusion errors in this study is based on the eligibility criteria defined by individual States and Union Territories. While overall NFSA coverage is centrally determined, States are responsible for identifying eligible households using criteria that vary across jurisdictions. These criteria generally include income thresholds, asset ownership, landholding, employment and tax status, and other exclusion filters,” the report states. The report attributes inclusion errors to “variations in the design, scope, and updating of eligibility criteria across States”. “Accordingly, a household is classified as an inclusion error if it does not meet the eligibility criteria specified by the respective State despite being included in the beneficiary list. Variations in the design, scope, and updating of eligibility criteria across States are likely to influence inclusion error rates and targeting outcomes under NFSA. Inclusion errors across rural and urban areas provide additional insights into the spatial dimensions of beneficiary targeting under NFSA,” it said. The NFSA, introduced by the then UPA government in July 2013, entitles 67 per cent of households to food grains at a subsidised price (rice Rs 3/kg, wheat Rs 2/kg) under the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS). The NDA government subsequently waived the subsidised prices under PMGKAY, providing free food grains. Last year, the Centre launched an exercise flagging ration card holders who receive free food grains, but are either taxpayers, car owners or directors in companies.

headline: SCO forum: In statement, Culture Ministry highlights Pakistan minister Musadik Malik’s speech
content: Overcoming their initial hesitation about hosting a Pakistani minister—the first such visit since Operation Sindoor—the Ministry of Culture went the whole hog to signal camaraderie during the two days of the SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum, highlighting Musadik Masood Malik’s speech in their official release, hosting informal interactions over meals, even though no bilateral meeting was held. On his part, Pakistan’s Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination did not make any caustic remarks. He, in fact, thanked the culture ministry for its hospitality and for bringing delegates from the region together. In his ministerial address Saturday, he emphasised that dialogue among civilisations was “essential”. In the culture ministry’s official release later in the day, his appreciation for the description of the event as ‘Tehzeeb Ki Guftagu’, or ‘Dialogue of Civilisations’, also found place. The statement referred to Malik’s conversation with Culture Minister Gajendra Shekhawat on the event’s opening day, Friday, where Malik said how “the layers of history and culture had been an integral part of the region's way of life for thousands of years”. “It was therefore important to recognise that distinct identities have their own significance, while dialogue among diverse identities is equally essential,” the ministry quoted Malik as saying. “He (Malik) said participants had gathered precisely for this purpose—to bring together multiple voices and identities and facilitate the free flow of ideas among them,” said the statement issued on Saturday. Referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at Purana Qila, Malik said the fort where the delegates sat was, in itself, a story, according to the ministry. In his statement in Urdu on Saturday, Malik invoked Ghalib, Taxila, Gandhara and Mohenjodaro to highlight the shared cultural links between South Asia and Central Asia, and invited delegates to visit Harappa and Mohenjodaro sites in Pakistan. Quoting his address, former BJP Rajya Sabha MP Tarun Vijay posted on his X account, “Must welcome his invite and plan a visit to Mohenjo- Daro. Good move. Surprisingly, however, we did not show them Rakhigarhi, which is twice the size of Mohenjo-Daro.” “I met him there (at the Purana Qila SCO venue) with his wife; we spoke in fluent Punjabi, and found him to be someone one can talk to,” said Vijay. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Forum on November 20. Alok Dimri, Additional Secretary, Ministry of External Affairs, and National Coordinator for the SCO, said that the organisation now needed to move beyond its security-centric approach. The ministry’s statement made a passing reference to other “dignitaries and representatives” who shared their perspectives, including Azerbaijan’s Minister of Culture, Adil Karimli; Nepal’s Minister for Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Khadak Raj Poudel; and Tajikistan’s Minister of Culture, Matlubakhon Amonzoda Sattoriyon. While the proceedings over the weekend largely remained out of bounds for Indian media, a couple of Pakistani journalists posted videos of their conversations with Malik at Purana Qila.

headline: In Goa, CJP’s Dipke slams CM: ‘You are the one selling state to friends from outside’
content: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday took potshots at Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant, accusing him of “selling” the coastal state to “friends from outside”. Speaking at the event 'Challa Kitem, Goa' or 'What's happening, Goa?' in Panaji, Dipke said that Sawant, while referring to a CJP-led protest last month to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, had claimed before the media that the protesters were from “outside the state.” “I want to tell Pramod Sawant.'Bhivpachi Garaj na' [There is no need to be afraid]. Tell me, who destroyed Goa's forests?” Dipke asked at the event organised by the CJP . The CJP founder said that when he first visited Goa a decade ago, he saw the backwaters, a pristine view of the ocean and the palm trees. “But, now when I land at the airport, it does not feel like I have come to Goa,” he said. “It feels like I have landed in any other metropolitan city. And I think that is the biggest loss of Goa. the loss of its identity, the loss of its culture, the loss of its beautiful architecture. We see big houses of concrete now. But, they don't look like Goan houses. This is not the Goa that I remember when I first visited this state,” he added. “This is all being ruined. How does it all start? It starts.when they take away your land. First, they take away your land. Then, they take away your tradition, your culture. and at the end, they take away your identity. This is what these corrupt politicians, with the help of 'land mafias' are doing. They are here just to make money by stealing away your identity. And that is what we have to protect,” Dipke said. The CJP announced that it will draft a 'Citizen's Manifesto' over the next two months as the state goes to polls in early 2027, adding the first demand of the manifesto will be to “scrap” Section 39 A of the Town and Country Planning Act. The contentious provision, notified in 2024, allows changes to the zoning of land parcels and modifications to the Regional Plan and Outline Development Plans at the direction of the government. Critics have argued that such changes can undermine the state’s planning framework and protections for ecologically sensitive areas, and allege that they can be influenced by real estate interests and individual demands. Section 39 A “has to be scrapped”, Dipke said. “Section 39 A is a way to ensure that Goans don't get their own houses,” he said, adding that builders, in connivance with local politicians, are “stealing away the lands of the people”. “And when people are fighting to save their lands, they are being called thieves,” he said. “There is a great scarcity of water. I got to know that the villagers [in Karapur Sarvan] are already struggling for water. Meanwhile, a township project is using so much water that the groundwater level is decreasing day by day,” said Dipke. 'Does Goa need colleges or township projects?' “Now, imagine a township project in 130 acres. They want to create. an artificial beach. It almost feels like they are not running a government, they are running a parody show, a comedy show. People come here to enjoy the experience of the beach and the forest, and you are going to give them an artificial experience,” he added. “What is the youth of Goa getting through this? Does Goa need colleges and universities or township projects? Does Goa need hospitals in the most remote areas or townships and luxurious apartments for people who are not from Goa?” he asked. Dipke said the youth of Goa have to migrate to other states, and often to other countries, because of lack of adequate educational infrastructure or job opportunities in the state. “Does the youth in Goa own a majority of the businesses [in the tourism sector]? Do they get a majority of the profit? Despite being the biggest tourist hub in India, Goa's youth is deprived of the benefit of the tourism industry,” he said. “Shouldn't Goa's youth be given the foremost priority when it comes to tourism? But, they are clearly not the first beneficiary. Who are the beneficiaries? We can ask Pramod Sawant, who always claims that people are coming from outside. You [Sawant] are the one who is selling Goa to your friends from outside [the state],” Dipke added. “And that is why it is necessary for all of us to unite. CJP will stand with each and every Goan who wants to save Goa. We need to ensure that we save our land,” he added.

headline: BJP to dispel top-down image, senior leaders to fan out, meet workers in UP
content: Marking a shift from the top-down process that has characterised much of the BJP’s approach over the last decade in Uttar Pradesh, the party has started its preparations for the coming Assembly elections by sending senior leaders to hear out workers on the ground. Steered by the BJP’s UP in-charge Vinod Tawde and joint in-charges Medha Kulkarni, Jagdish Patel, Pradeep Verma and Anant Ojha, along with state BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary, several teams of senior leaders will be visiting every district and meet local leaders to discuss their concerns besides organisational gaps and ground realities. The process got underway with the recent two-day chintan baithak of the party held in Mathura, attended by about 50 BJP leaders, including party president Nitin Nabin and national general secretary (organisation) B L Santhosh, where each participant was allocated time to put forward their views. Sources said that the idea that senior leaders tour the districts was discussed at a meeting in Gorakhpur earlier this month, which was also attended by Nabin. At the meeting, Jagdish Patel said that during a recent visit to Bundelkhand, he had been approached by villagers with complaints regarding implementation of the Har Ghar Jal Yojana. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said an inquiry had been ordered in that matter. Sources said a senior minister then urged all the leaders present to listen to Patel’s views, holding that they should all speak freely or else such internal meetings would be futile. The minister also remarked that a major grievance of the workers has been that their voices were not heard, sources said. With the message going out, “an atmosphere of patient listening” marked the Mathura meeting, as per sources present. Leaders said that B L Santhosh went on to ask a pointed question as to who among the participants had not met CM Adityanath personally since 2017 (when he first became CM). Pushkar Mishra, Ranjana Upadhyay and Tryambak Tripathi – all leaders from the Brahmin community, which believes the Adityanath regime is “Thakur-focused” – raised their hands. They were asked to meet the CM after the session. Gonda, Mishra and Tripathi, who have been former office-bearers in the UP BJP, later shared photographs of their meeting with Adityanath on social media. When contacted, one of the three leaders confirmed they met the CM, without sharing any more details. Incidentally, while former state BJP presidents and current general secretaries were invited for the Mathura session, ex-state chiefs Kalraj Mishra, Vinay Katiyar and Om Prakash Singh, who have not been very active in the party, did not attend. Katiyar said he was not informed about the meeting. BJP’s challenges Immediately after the Mathura meeting, Adityanath travelled to Delhi to hold discussions with Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Nabin and Santhosh, which was seen as an effort to also realign leaders at the highest levels in the BJP. Shah was expected to be present at the Mathura meeting but did not attend. Incidentally, the party meeting was originally to be held in Vrindavan in October, but was postponed, with one reason cited by sources being the unavailability of Shah. As per sources, the state BJP is also feeling the absence of national general secretary Sunil Bansal. As the UP general secretary (organisation) for several years, Bansal played a significant role in the party’s successive wins, but later distanced himself due to differences with the state leadership. Bansal shifted to the Centre in August 2022 as national general secretary of the BJP and is now the party’s in-charge of West Bengal and Telangana. One of the reasons for the setback to the BJP in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, particularly in Uttar Pradesh, was seen to be the lack of involvement of the RSS in the campaign. With the Samajwadi Party getting a new lease of life from the 2024 results, and its chief Akhilesh Yadav on the offensive, the BJP does not want to take any chances. Hindutva as the message The choice of Mathura as the venue of the meeting was also deliberate, coinciding with a renewed focus by the BJP on the Krishna Janmabhoomi dispute. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said during the meeting that a grand Krishna temple at the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Eidgah mosque site in Mathura was very much a part of the BJP’s poll agenda. Over a dozen petitions in the Mathura case are pending before the Allahabad High Court. Sources said the BJP feels that Akhilesh’s ‘PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak)’ narrative cannot be effectively countered by the BJP’s social justice slogans alone, and that a stronger Hindutva message is required. Along with the call for a Krishna Janmabhoomi temple, the slogan Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De emerged from the Mathura conclave. This push may also help the BJP make inroads in the Yadav vote bank, which claims kinship to Lord Krishna – though, as an insider pointed out, no delegate from the Yadav community found representation at the meeting. The BJP is aware that whenever a party has been able to cash in on the social justice theme in UP – as Akhilesh is trying to do – it has found the going tough. The late Sushma Swaraj once observed that a cheque can be encashed only once, in response to questions about whether the campaign for a Ram temple in Ayodhya alone would sustain political advantage for the BJP. In another change from 2024, the BJP is likely to avoid slogans such as “Abki Baar, Chaar Sau Paar”, setting for itself a 400-plus seat target in the general elections. The Opposition projected it as a sign of the BJP’s arrogance, and played on fears that a dominant party like it would “alter” the Constitution and remove provisions such as reservations once in power.

headline: Why has BJP inducted cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal in its OBC Morcha?
content: Ahead of major elections, parties often parade celebrities who join their ranks, most of the time to contest polls. But not Yuzvendra Chahal. The Indian cricketer — who retired from first-class, red-ball cricket last year but is still available for one-day cricket and Twenty20 internationals — joined the BJP on Saturday and was appointed a special invitee to the national executive of the party’s Other Backward Classes (OBC) Morcha from Delhi, where no major election is scheduled to be held in the next few years. Chahal recently met BJP OBC Morcha’s national president and Rajya Sabha MP Amar Pal Maurya in Delhi. On Saturday, Maurya announced the new national office-bearers and members of the Morcha’s executive panel. Chahal is among the three special invitees. A BJP leader said Chahal is from the OBC Jat community and was named from Delhi because he provided the party with an address. As there are no elections around in Delhi, the party intends to invite Chahal to Morcha meetings and use him for youth outreach. In the coming Uttar Pradesh election, Jats are expected to play a crucial role in the western part of the state where they are numerically strong. In states such as UP, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Delhi, Jats are already categorised as OBC. The Jats of Rajasthan, except those in Dholpur and Bharatpur, are also OBC in the central list. They are, however, considered to be in the general category in Haryana, Chahal's home state. Jats are a politically powerful community and are estimated to influence the results of nearly 40 Lok Sabha seats and around 160 Assembly seats in UP, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Delhi. In UP, they are concentrated in the western districts, mainly cultivate sugarcane, and are the state’s richest farming community. भाजपा परिवार में मुझे स्थान व मान-सम्मान देने के लिए आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री नरेंद्र मोदी जी, आदरणीय गृहमंत्री श्री अमित शाह जी, भाजपा राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष श्री नितिन नवीन जी व ओबीसी मोर्चा के राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष श्री अमरपाल मौर्य जी का हार्दिक आभार प्रकट करता हूँ।🙏🏻 — Yuzvendra Chahal (@yuzi_chahal) November 21, 2026   “Celebrities have their own fan following and are important for optics. The party may also end up getting a new set of voters from a different age group or social group. It is good that a prominent sportsperson like Chahal, who has excelled in cricket, has joined the BJP. His presence in the party’s poll campaigns will draw the crowd of youths,” said another BJP leader. “Chahal was in touch with me and I decided to bring him in. He had shown an interest in politics and expressed a wish to work with the BJP. The induction of Chahal, Seema Samridhi Kushwaha, and Adwaita Charan Gadanayak will inspire OBC youths to connect with the BJP,” Maurya told The Indian Express. Gadanayak is a renowned sculptor from Odisha who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2025. Kushwaha, meanwhile, was the lawyer of the 2012 Delhi rape-murder victim. She had joined the BJP in March 2024 ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, and has been named to the Morcha from UP. “Yuzvendra has been inducted into the OBC team so that people know that youths from OBC communities see how successful people from the community have been on the global stage,” said a BJP leader. In a post on X on Saturday, Chahal expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin, and Maurya for giving him “space and respect” in the party. Other cricketer-politicians Chahal is not the first cricketer to join politics. In recent years, many from the Indian cricket team have found their way into politics, including two-time World Cup winner Yusuf Pathan, who was elected to the Lok Sabha on a Trinamool Congress (TMC) ticket in 2024 and is now part of a rebel group of party MPs. Another former cricketer and TMC MP is Kirti Azad, who has sided with Mamata Banerjee. Current India men’s team coach Gautam Gambhir was the BJP MP from East Delhi from 2019 to 2024, while former India cricket captain Mohammad Azharuddin is a former Congress MP and currently a minister in Telangana. Former cricketer Navjot Singh Sidhu, an opening batsman, was a minister in the Congress-led Punjab government but has since fallen out with the party.

headline: As Parliament’s adjournment without prorogation breaches 100-day mark, why it matters
content: The longest period of sine adjournment of Parliament has breached the 100-day mark amid speculation around a special session for yet another push to the BJP-led NDA government’s “delimitation package”, which includes the implementation of 33% reservation for women. Sunday marked the 101st day since the Monsoon Session was adjourned sine die on August 13. With the customary year-end window for announcing the Winter Session approaching, questions have emerged over whether the government will convene a special sitting before the regular session. The previous two longest periods of adjournment sine die without prorogation were recorded during Congress governments in the 1980s. The current spell is the longest since the BJP-led NDA first came to power in 2014 and, indeed, the longest in Parliament’s history. Interestingly, both the earlier instances and the current one occurred during the respective Eighth Session — the Eighth Lok Sabha under the Congress government and the 18th Lok Sabha under the BJP-led NDA government. In 2025, the Winter Session was held from December 1 to 19, with 15 sittings. Parliament passed eight Bills and held special discussions on the 150th anniversary of the national song Vande Mataram and electoral reforms. Government sources have indicated that the Winter Session is on track and that the government has the support of more than the required number of Lok Sabha MPs to meet the two-thirds majority needed to pass a Constitutional amendment for the proposed delimitation package. There has also been speculation about a three-day sitting, possibly as the second part of the Monsoon Session, which has not yet been prorogued. Such a sitting could be held ahead of the Winter Session. Under Article 85 of the Constitution, the President is empowered to summon Parliament. The convention is to provide around 15 days notice for a regular session. The Constitution also requires that no more than six months elapse between two consecutive sittings of Parliament. A special sitting, however, can be convened at shorter notice. If a session has been adjourned sine die but not prorogued, it technically remains in existence. Under Rule 15 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, the Speaker can reconvene the House after it has been adjourned sine die. The distinction between adjournment and prorogation is significant. An adjournment ends a sitting of the House, while an adjournment sine die ends its sittings without specifying a date for the next one. Neither, by itself, brings the session to an end. Prorogation, on the other hand, formally terminates a session through an order issued by the President under Article 85(2) of the Constitution. It ordinarily follows an adjournment sine die, although the two are legally distinct. The President exercises the power to prorogue Parliament on the advice of the Prime Minister. Prorogation can technically take place at any time, including while the House is sitting, though the usual practice is to prorogue it after an adjournment sine die. The Monsoon Session of the 18th Lok Sabha began on July 20 and was adjourned sine die on August 13. By comparison, the 2023 Monsoon Session, which ran from July 21 to August 21 and had 21 sittings, was prorogued the following day. According to Practice and Procedure of Parliament, authored by M N Kaul and S L Shakdher, a House may be adjourned from day to day, for more than a day, or sine die during a session. The Speaker can also summon a sitting of the Lok Sabha before the date to which it has been adjourned or at any time after it has been adjourned sine die. Thus, an adjournment sine die does not, by itself, prevent the House from meeting again. The 1987 and 1989 precedents The longest previous period of adjournment sine die without prorogation in Lok Sabha history lasted 76 days, in 1987, during the Eighth Session of the Eighth Lok Sabha. The second-longest, lasting 61 days, was recorded in 1989 during the 14th Session of the same Lok Sabha. The 1987 episode unfolded against the backdrop of the Bofors controversy, following allegations of kickbacks in connection with India's 1986 agreement with Swedish arms manufacturer Bofors AB for the supply of Howitzer guns. The Eighth Session began on February 23, 1987, and was adjourned sine die on May 12 amid disruptions over the controversy. The Speaker subsequently exercised the power available under the proviso to Rule 15 to reconvene the House. The Lok Sabha met again from July 27 to August 28.

headline: Congress won 2 seats in UP in 2022. Does its 181-seat demand add up?
content: Even before the two parties formally sit down to discuss seat-sharing for the coming Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls, the tug-of-war between the Congress and its ally, the Samajwadi Party (SP) over the issue has seemingly begun. The two parties are likely to have a meeting over seat-sharing for the Uttar Pradesh polls on Monday in Delhi. While the Congress has submitted a list of 181 seats, or 45%, the SP is reluctant to concede such a large share, citing its ally’s past performance in the state, The Indian Express has learnt. Uttar Pradesh has a total of 403 Assembly seats. An analysis of the past six Assembly elections in the state shows that the Congress has contested 298 seats on average, winning 19 with an average vote share of 7.69%. Congress’s past record The party’s best performance came in 1996, when it contested with the Mayawati-led Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) in a bid to consolidate Muslim and Dalit votes. It contested 126 seats, winning 33 while securing an 8.35% vote share. The BSP, which by then had already made inroads into the Congress’s Dalit vote share, contested 296 seats, winning 67 with a 19.64% vote share. In 2002, the Congress decided to go it alone, contesting 402 seats in the state. However, its tally fell to 25 seats despite its vote share seeing a marginal improvement to 8.96%. Five years later, the Congress’s tally further declined. Contesting the polls alone in 393 seats, it managed to win only 22 with an 8.61% vote share. The BSP, also contesting independently, won an absolute majority and formed the government under Mayawati. The 2012 elections saw the Congress recording an improvement in its electoral performance. Contesting 355 seats in alliance with the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), the party won 28 seats with a vote share of 11.65%. The RLD contested 46 seats, winning nine and securing 2.33% of the votes. The SP went on to win a majority, paving the way for Akhilesh Yadav to become Chief Minister. Despite completing a full term, Akhilesh agreed to ally with the Congress for the 2017 polls following a bitter power struggle with his uncle. The SP-Congress alliance campaigned together with slogans like “UP ko ye saath pasand hai (UP likes this duo)” and while projecting Akhilesh and Rahul Gandhi as “UP ke ladke (UP’s sons of the soil)”. The SP contested 311 seats in alliance with the Congress, which fielded candidates in 114. However, the alliance collectively won only 54 seats – SP’s 47 and seven for the Congress, which saw its vote share drop to 6.25%. The BJP stormed to power, winning over 300 seats. Following the loss, the Congress and SP parted ways for the 2022 polls. The Congress’s campaign was led by AICC general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and revolved around the slogan “Ladki hoon, ladh sakti hoon (I am a woman and I can fight)”. The Congress fielded 399 candidates but won only two. The party also saw its vote share plummet to its lowest ever – 2.33%. The Lok Sabha polls of 2024, however, offered the two parties a more successful template for Uttar Pradesh. Under their seat-sharing arrangement, the SP contested 62 of the state's 80 Lok Sabha seats and the Congress 17. The SP won 37 seats and the Congress six, taking their combined tally to 43. The BJP, which had won 62 seats in the state in 2019, was reduced to 33. The 181 calculation Explaining the rationale behind the Congress's demand for 181 Assembly seats despite its relatively poor record in state elections, a senior party leader said the 2024 Lok Sabha results had changed the political equation. “Past Assembly election performances are one consideration. But we are looking at the outcome of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The Congress won six Lok Sabha seats, but secured a substantial number of votes in the other 11 seats it contested. The party has workers in every district of Uttar Pradesh. To maintain its presence across the state, it wants to contest at least one seat in every district and keep its cadre engaged in the campaign,” the leader said. “If the Congress leaves an entire district to the SP and asks its workers to campaign for the ally's candidates, they may eventually feel it is better to join the SP. Why would they continue working for the Congress for five years only to campaign for the SP during elections?” the leader added. The leader also cited the 2017 seat-sharing agreement. “If the SP could give the Congress 114 seats in 2017, after having run a majority government for five years, why can't it give us 181 in 2027, when it has been out of power for 10 years?” a Congress leader said. Another Congress leader said the party was firm on contesting more than 100 seats. “There will be no compromise below 100 seats. The political atmosphere in Uttar Pradesh is favourable for the Congress-SP alliance,” the leader said. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress had secured a lead in 40 Assembly segments. Party sources said it was keen to contest these Assembly segments, along with constituencies where its candidates had finished runners-up by narrow margins. “For instance, we lost the Bansgaon Lok Sabha seat to the BJP by just 3,150 votes, despite leading in three Assembly segments falling under the constituency,” a party leader said. The Congress is also seeking an “equitable distribution” of around 90 weak seats, constituencies that the BJP has won in the last two or three Assembly elections.

headline: After Congress’s rural gains, Ashok Gehlot makes his move: ‘Can be CM again if needed’
content: Following the Congress’s decisive win in the Panchayati Raj elections in Rajasthan this week, former three-term Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot has made the first move for the top job, saying he does not hunger for a fourth term but making it clear that he was still open to doing the job if the party desired. The Assembly elections in Rajasthan are scheduled for late 2028. Asked about his possible role in Delhi amid his frequent visits to the national Capital, Gehlot told PTI in an interview on Saturday, “I have said already; I haven’t been given a hint by anyone, nor has there been any discussion. I keep going to Delhi because of meetings and work. I have been going to Delhi for 50 years, even longer. I am very happy here (in Jaipur), irrespective of whether I get a post or not. I have been given so much by Sonia ji, and when Rahul Gandhi became Congress president, I again became (the CM); I have been CM thrice.” “Indira Gandhi made me Deputy Minister (at the Centre), Rajiv Gandhi ji promoted me; during Narasimha Rao’s tenure (as Prime Minister), I became the Textiles Minister. I have sat in the AICC (All India Congress Committee) twice and have been the PCC (Pradesh Congress Committee) president thrice, hadd hoti hai. Teen baar mukhyamantri banna kum hota hai kya? (There is a limit. Isn’t being a CM thrice a lot?). Chauthi baar Gehlot sarkar (Gehlot as CM a fourth time), when such slogans are raised, I have to tell them to stop. And I say it with heart, although in politics no one believes it, whether you are speaking from your heart or not.” In the past, Gehlot has taken on his rival and former Deputy CM Sachin Pilot over the top job, highlighting that the party gave Pilot important posts at a young age. “But I say it with heart that I am satisfied. But despite that, if it is felt that it is necessary for me to become CM in the interest of the party, and the high command takes a decision in my favour, then I am not a hypocrite either. Theek hai, alag baat hai, ban jaayenge Mukhyamantri (Then it is fine, I can be the CM). But it isn’t that I have to be the CM again and again. The high command will decide — when the time comes — what is in the party’s interest and what the public wants,” Gehlot said. Gehlot’s careful emphasis on the high command comes in the backdrop of his apology to then party chief Sonia Gandhi in September 2022 following his camp’s boycott of a Congress Legislature Party (CLP) meeting in Jaipur, which was apparently called to choose a new CM, said to be Sachin Pilot. A month earlier, Gehlot had emerged as the Gandhis’ choice to take over as Congress president. But that would have meant giving up the Rajasthan CM’s chair, which Gehlot did not want to do. Gehlot stayed on as CM as the boycott of the CLP meeting by legislators allied to him ensured that the high command could not carry out the leadership change in the state. He eventually lost power in the 2023 Assembly elections. A recurring theme The fight between Gehlot and Pilot over leadership has defined the party in Rajasthan over the past half a decade. In July 2020, the leak of audio tapes allegedly involving a BJP leader, a middleman, and some Congress MLAs led to a political crisis in Rajasthan as then Deputy CM Pilot unsuccessfully led a rebellion along with 18 Congress MLAs against Gehlot’s government while staying in Manesar in BJP-ruled Haryana. At the heart of the rebellion was said to be Pilot’s ambition for the CM post, which he believed should have been his after leading the state Congress back to power in 2018. The high command managed to broker a shaky truce between the two, but the matter has continued to resurface from time to time. Ahead of the 2023 elections — which the Congress ultimately lost — Gehlot said amid a tussle over the candidate list that it would be a mistake to rule him out of the CM race if the party was voted back to power. At the time, Gehlot said that while he “wants to leave the top post”, “the post was not leaving me and may not do so in the future”. With the next Assembly polls in the state in 2028, Gehlot’s latest statement sends a clear signal to the high command and Pilot, who may once again have to navigate machinations within the party over the next two years.

headline: Rumblings in UDF: Why CM Satheesan faces Congress discontent
content: Barely six months into office, Keralam Chief Minister V D Satheesan is facing criticism from within his Cabinet and the Congress over what party leaders claim was a row related to “unilateral decision-making and lack of consultation”. The differences have come to the fore over political appointments and key government decisions, exposing a growing faultline within the Congress, which rules the state along with its United Democratic Front (UDF) allies. The dissent, particularly expressed by Congress ministers, suggests that Satheesan has yet to secure the political and administrative confidence of a significant section of his Cabinet, which largely comprises leaders seen as close to AICC general secretary (organisation) K C Venugopal, who had lost the race for the chief minister's post to him in May. Making the differences with the CM public, Keralam Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president and Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph said on Thursday, “There are certain issues on which deliberations are not complete. Discussions are not complete. There is a situation in which deliberations have to take place. We want decisions not to be unilateral, and we are trying to ensure that.” The remarks came a day after the weekly Cabinet meeting in which a few Congress ministers reportedly locked horns with Satheesan. The KPCC chief’s public outburst came after he had expressed displeasure over Satheesan's intervention in the state's power purchase deal, particularly his decision to suspend an earlier decision on the matter. Sunny's remarks came close on the heels of Satheesan acknowledging differences within the Cabinet, albeit in a different context. “Debate is the beauty of democracy. This is not a Cabinet of loyalists. There will be arguments in the Cabinet. Different opinions from the Congress and the UDF will not be rejected, but will be heard and examined to see whether they matter,” the CM told the media. As the debate raged, senior Congress leader and Minister K Muraleedharan sought to play down the controversy on Saturday, suggesting that some leaders were “behaving like Opposition leaders”. “The Satheesan government has the support of the people, who have high expectations of its performance. The government will complete five years. The Chief Minister will move ahead robustly,” he said. What sparked dissent? The immediate trigger for the flare-up was the appointment of Congress nominees to the State Public Service Commission and the Guruvayur Devaswom Board. Ministers considered close to Venugopal reportedly questioned Satheesan's decision to push through the names without adequate consultations within the party. However, leaders close to Satheesan alleged that the controversy was part of a concerted attempt by the rival camp to undermine the government's image. “All decisions are taken with the consent of Congress leaders, including Venugopal. However, Venugopal has not so far contradicted the reports attributed to his camp. We suspect a double game behind the latest controversy. The Chief Minister has limitations when it comes to speaking out. Certain quarters are exploiting this to take the sheen off the government and create the impression that it is already in trouble,” a leader close to Satheesan said. Key appointments stalled The lack of consensus within the Congress has also stalled hundreds of political appointments to government-run corporations and welfare boards. With Satheesan and Venugopal yet to reach an understanding on the distribution of positions, the appointments remain pending, frustrating party workers who had expected to be accommodated after the UDF's return to power. The issue has also surfaced within the UDF. RSP leader and Forest Minister Shibu Baby John has openly expressed anguish over the CPI(M) leaders appointed during the previous LDF regime continuing in government positions. He has argued that these posts should have gone to the Congress and UDF nominees who worked for the alliance's return to power. Ironically, the composition of the Cabinet should have made political and administrative coordination easier for Satheesan. It comprises the KPCC president, two party vice-presidents and the Youth Congress chief. Former KPCC presidents Ramesh Chennithala and Muraleedharan are also part of the Cabinet. Both have backed Satheesan in the power struggle. ‘CM taking party for granted’ However, a section of the rival Congress faction believes that the CM was taking the party organisation for granted, apparently relying on the presence of senior leaders in his Cabinet. Satheesan has also faced criticism from outside the Cabinet, particularly from UDF convener and Congress MP Adoor Prakash, who has also complained that he was not consulted on several key decisions and appointments. Early last month, Prakash reportedly met the AICC leadership to raise his grievances against Satheesan, particularly over the decision to give the chairmanship of the Administrative Reforms Committee to the IUML. Party sources, however, said the decision had been taken with the consent of the AICC leadership, which explained its silence on Prakash's complaint. Past troubles The Congress had faced similar challenges during the tenure of the party-led UDF government that came to power after the 2001 elections. The then A K Antony-led government had won 99 of the 140 Assembly seats, but its tenure was marked by persistent differences within the Cabinet and between the government and the party organisation. Factionalism and anti-incumbency contributed to the UDF's poor performance in the 2004 Lok Sabha elections in Kerala, even as the Congress returned to power at the Centre. The Congress had then failed to win any of the state's 20 Lok Sabha seats, while its UDF ally IUML secured just one seat.

headline: BJP, Sena spar over appointment of ‘tainted’ health official Ashok Thorat
content: The BJP and the Shiv Sena, which are allies in Maharashtra’s ruling coalition, have crossed paths once again, this time over the continuation of the appointment of the medical director of the Employees' State Insurance Society (ESIS). BJP MLA Namita Mundada has questioned the appointment of Dr Ashok Thorat, who was suspended over irregularities related to COVID-19 relief work in Beed district and faced allegations of a similar nature in Nashik district as well as a criminal case. While the health minister is Sena leader Prakash Abitkar, Mundada has flagged the matter in a letter written to Minister of State Meghana Bordikar, who is from the BJP. The MLA has also demanded Thorat's suspension in the Assembly. In response, Dr Thorat has reportedly written to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and his department. He has said he is being unfairly targeted and is ready for an inquiry by a senior IAS official. Dr Thorat's wife is a Sena leader in Beed. In March 2025, it was Sena leader Abitkar who announced Dr Thorat's suspension in the legislature over the allegations of financial irregularities during COVID-19 in Beed. However, the suspension was revoked and Dr Thorat was given a deputation post in the ESIS. Mundada, in letters sent in September 2025 and in August 2026 to Bordikar, has levelled allegations regarding an alleged Rs 3.37-crore COVID ICU scam in Nashik, an inquiry into financial irregularities in Beed, and an abortion case in Kaij in the same district. According to sources in the health department, more than an administrative affair, the issue is turning into a political one. When contacted, Mundada said she had mentioned all these cases on the floor of the House several times. "We believe that the inquiry is being held and it will reveal everything," she said. Asked whether the issue is about the administrative tussle between the BJP and the Sena, she did not comment. The chief minister’s office is also probing a similar complaint submitted against Thorat filed by a Kaji-based doctor, Dr Chandrkant Lamture. Both ministers have chosen to be tight-lipped about the complaint. Dr Thorat said he would not comment on any allegations against him.

headline: BJP MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute dies of cardiac arrest, PM Modi offers condolences
content: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute died after suffering a cardiac arrest at a hospital in New Delhi late on Saturday night. The 72-year-old leader had been elected to the Rajya Sabha earlier this year. Wadkute was admitted to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in New Delhi on Saturday night after complaining of a cough, according to news agency PTI. Condoling the demise of the senior leader, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, "Deeply saddened by the passing of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Wadkute Ji. He will be remembered for his contribution to society and emphasis on serving the poor and downtrodden. Equally noteworthy were his efforts to strengthen the BJP in Maharashtra. My thoughts are with his family and admirers. Om Shanti." Deeply saddened by the passing of Rajya Sabha MP Shri Ramrao Wadkute Ji. He will be remembered for his contribution to society and emphasis on serving the poor and downtrodden. Equally noteworthy were his efforts to strengthen the BJP in Maharashtra. My thoughts are with his family and admirers. Om Shanti. राज्यसभा खासदार श्री रामराव वडकुते जी यांच्या निधनाचे वृत्त ऐकून अतिशय दुःख झाले. समाजसेवेतील त्यांचे योगदान तसेच गरीब आणि वंचित घटकांच्या सेवेसाठी त्यांनी दिलेले प्राधान्य यासाठी त्यांचे सदैव स्मरण केले जाईल. महाराष्ट्रात भाजप पक्ष संघटना बळकट करण्यासाठी त्यांनी केलेले प्रयत्नही तितकेच उल्लेखनीय होते. या दुःखद प्रसंगी त्यांच्या कुटुंबीयांच्या आणि चाहत्यांच्या दुःखात मी सहभागी आहे. ओम शांती. — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 22, 2026 Hailing from Hingoli district in Maharashtra's Marathwada region, Wadkute was known for his simplicity and commitment to the Dhangar (shepherd) community. Wadkute was associated with the undivided NCP from its formation in 1999 till 2019. In 2004, the party led by Sharad Pawar fielded him from the Kalamnuri Assembly constituency. But he lost that election. Later, he was appointed a member of the state Legislative Council. In 2019, Wadkute quit the NCP to join the BJP. He was also made Hingoli BJP president and prabhari. His work during the 2024 Lok Sabha and Assembly elections earned him applause within the party. He also headed Maharashtra Sheli and Mendi Vikas Mahamandal (Goat and Sheep Development Corporation). "To me, this was unexpected. I am grateful to central and state leadership for considering my candidature for the Rajya Sabha. I am pleasantly surprised," he had said of his nomination to the Upper House of Parliament. He would also frequent the Maharashtra Vidhan Bhawan to take up issues related to the Dhangar community with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and others. Fadnavis expressed grief, describing Wadkute as a simple and dedicated political leader committed to grassroots welfare. He also recalled Wadkute's organisational responsibilities in the BJP's Hingoli unit and his work for the Dhangar community. Vice-President and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan expressed grief over Wadkute's passing, saying his contributions to public life and service to the people would always be remembered. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said, "The passing of Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute ji is deeply saddening. In this hour of grief, my heartfelt condolences are with the bereaved family. May the departed soul rest in peace and may the family find the strength to bear this immense loss." Maharashtra Assembly Speaker Rahul Narwekar, in a post on X, said, "The news of the tragic passing of Hon. Ramraoji Wadkute, Member of the Rajya Sabha, in Delhi following a severe heart attack is deeply painful and heartbreaking. At this difficult time, we share in the grief of the Wadkute family." (With inputs from Shubhangi Khapre in Mumbai)

headline: Aaditya Thackeray says BJP lacks courage to stop work at Adani project site
content: Accusing Adani Green Energy Limited of continuing work at its hydropower project in Maharashtra’s Satara district, Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Aaditya Thackeray on Saturday said the BJP-led government lacked the courage to enforce its order to stop the work. "Adani is the boss of the BJP. The party doesn't have the courage to speak in front of them. When ordinary citizens hold protests, police are sent to lathi-charge them. When work is going on at Adani's project site despite a stay, why aren’t police sent there? Why is the government not arresting those continuing the work?" Aaditya said at a party event at Mundhwa, Pune. “The BJP has taken politics to a new low,'' he added. The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board issued a letter to Adani Green Energy’s Tarali Pump Storage Project on Friday, directing it to stop the work at Sawarghar in Patan taluka. Aaditya also spoke about the drought situation in the state and said the central government should use the PM CARES fund to help drought victims if necessary. "A drought has been declared in nearly 40 per cent of Maharashtra's area. The drought that usually starts around April–May began in September–October itself. There is talk that even in Pune, water supply will be limited to once a day. In such a situation, the central government is expected to help Maharashtra. Just as aid was given to Gujarat, give aid to Maharashtra too. If needed, use money from the 'PM CARES' fund and help the drought victims," he said. Centre neglects Maharashtra: Aaditya Thackeray Emphasising that aid should directly reach drought victims, he said. “The government is ensuring water to the industrial sector while neglecting agriculture. Water must be given properly for agriculture as well as drinking. Due to urbanisation and construction, natural sources are being encroached upon. Therefore, taking stock of the situation is necessary.'' Aaditya alleged that while the Centre gave huge amounts of aid to Gujarat to deal with the aftermath of Cyclones Nisarga and Tauktae, Maharashtra was neglected. ''Now there is a BJP government in the state and at the Centre as well. Then what is the obstacle in giving aid to Maharashtra?" he said. Regarding the speculation about a possible merger between the ruling NCP and the Opposition NCP (SP), Aaditya said, "Politics in the state has currently fallen to a lower level. However, there is currently a serious water crisis everywhere in Maharashtra—be it Pune, Mumbai, or anywhere else. In such a situation, people must be helped by stopping politics over water."

headline: 'PM Modi's advice saved Rs 65L per kg of gold': BJP demands Congress' apology for 'misleading' traders
content: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Sunday demanded an apology from the Congress for criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal to defer gold purchases, saying traders who followed his advice avoided losses of Rs 65 lakh per kg as prices fell. The party cited a letter from the chamber of trade and industry (CTI) thanking PM Modi for his advice and said the Congress had misled traders by calling it a "death warrant".BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said the Congress had created panic when Modi asked people to postpone gold purchases earlier this year. He said traders who followed the advice were spared losses as gold prices declined globally."With gold prices falling globally, traders following PM Modi's advice saved Rs 65 lakh per kg of gold. The trader bodies have thanked the prime minister today," Bhandari said in a post on X."The Congress should apologise to the traders for misleading them and creating panic," he added.Bhandari also criticised the Congress leadership over its response to Modi's appeal."Gandhi-Vadra family, which lived a lavish lifestyle when India's majority was poor, should take a master class in economic management and simple living from PM Modi," he wrote.The BJP's remarks came after the CTI wrote to PM Modi, thanking him for advising people against buying gold.The chamber said the advice had saved lakhs of jewellers, traders and investors from substantial losses. It cited a fall in gold prices from Rs 1.90 crore to Rs 1.25 crore per kg, amounting to a decline of Rs 65 lakh per kg.The CTI also said the fall in prices had brought relief to families during the ongoing wedding season.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Watch: Hours after PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu, RJD workers tear down NDA banners
content: NEW DELHI: A political showdown erupted on Bihar’s newly inaugurated Nitish Setu on Saturday, with Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) workers pulling down banners and posters put up by the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the bridge in Vaishali.Videos circulating on social media showed a large group of RJD supporters, tearing down the displays and shouting slogans in support of party supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav and leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav. Police personnel were seen moving alongside the crowd but appeared unable to control the gathering.The disruption has triggered a fresh exchange between the BJP and RJD, turning the inauguration of a major infrastructure project into a political flashpoint.BJP has accused the RJD of trying to politicise a development project rather than acknowledge its benefits. The bridge, named Nitish Setu, was inaugurated by PM Modi on November 21. The six-lane structure has been built at an estimated cost of Rs 4,280 crore and connects Kacchi Dargah with Bidupur. It is expected to improve connectivity between north and south Bihar and reduce pressure on Mahatma Gandhi Setu.Row over the bridge’s nameThe naming of a bridge in Bihar has triggered a political row, with the Congress and RJD questioning the decision to christen it Nitish Setu instead of naming it after Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.Congress leader Pawan Khera accused the BJP-led Bihar government of hurting Sikh sentiments through the decision. In a post on X, he questioned why a bridge proposed to be named after Guru Gobind Singh was now being named after Nitish Kumar, and whether the move was aimed at pushing the former chief minister out of the political mainstream. "Why is this being done in a way that tramples on the sentiments of the Sikh community?" he asked.Khera also questioned the timing, saying it raised concerns about whether the JD(U) leader was being sidelined while still alive. He shared a Bihar Road Construction Department document containing a note on a non-official resolution moved by RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav regarding the proposed name.Tejashwi had earlier said he moved a private member's resolution in the Bihar Assembly proposing the bridge be named after Guru Gobind Singh. He accused the government of changing its position and said the decision was politically motivated. The Bihar Assembly later said no decision had been taken in the House to name the bridge after Guru Gobind Singh.The controversy has also drawn criticism from AAP leaders in Punjab. Finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema, Assembly speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and MLA Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal urged the Bihar government to reconsider, saying the bridge's proximity to Takht Sri Patna Sahib made the issue particularly sensitive. Cheema said the government could honour Nitish Kumar in other ways, but going back on a proposal to honour Guru Gobind Singh was unacceptable. Dhaliwal called the decision an insult to Sikh sentiments.Tejashwi also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's inauguration of the bridge, claiming Nitish Kumar had opened it around 17 months earlier and that the project was already in use. He challenged the BJP to identify its contribution to the construction.The inauguration also brought back a familiar election-season image: PM Modi waved his gamcha during the event, recalling his appearance at the BJP office in Patna after the NDA’s victory in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections. The gesture had gone viral at the time, with “Modi Ka Gamcha” trending online after the alliance won 202 of the state’s 243 seats.The bridge inauguration was attended by Bihar governor Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (retd), Union minister Chirag Paswan, chief minister Samrat Choudhary and other dignitaries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: BJP leader, Shiv Sena MLA clash at public event in Palghar; minister steps in
content: NEW DELHI: An argument broke out between a Bharatiya Janata Party leader and a Shiv Sena MLA on Sunday during a public programme in Palghar district.According to news agency PTI, the incident took place during a sporting event where BJP district president Bharat Rajput and Shiv Sena MLA Rajendra Gavit were seated on either side of Naik, who is also Palghar's guardian minister.Local sources told PTI that Rajput questioned Gavit's presence at a BJP event. Gavit responded that he had been invited by Naik along with the Palghar MP, leading to a heated exchange between the two leaders.The video shows Naik stepping in to defuse the situation and pacify the two leaders. The BJP, Shiv Sena and NCP are partners in the ruling Mahayuti coalition in Maharashtra.Speaking to the media later, Gavit accused Rajput of using abusive language during the argument. He also brought up the September attack at a Palghar hospital, in which Rajput's son, Rohit Gavit, is an accused.The Sena MLA alleged that Rajput had contacted the doctor involved in the case 18 times and claimed that his son had been deliberately implicated.Rohit Gavit and 10 others are currently in judicial custody for allegedly assaulting staff members at a private hospital. The accused had claimed that the hospital was charging exorbitant fees for treating injured 'Govindas' who had taken part in the Dahi Handi celebrations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: ‘Opposed to development’: BJP targets RJD after youths tear PM Modi posters on Bihar bridge
content: PATNA: A day after PM Narendra Modi inaugurated the Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge across the river Ganga that links north and south Bihar, a video showing a group of around 100 irate youths going amok and tearing his posters and cutout on the bridge went viral on Sunday.The incident happened around half an hour after the inauguration of the bridge, which, earlier this month, was given the name Nitish Setu to recognise the contribution of former CM Nitish Kumar by present CM Samrat Choudhary, who leads the BJP-led NDA govt in which the JD(U), headed by Nitish, is a junior partner.As the video shows, youths in the age group of 19-25 years run amok on the bridge and tear the posters of PM Modi and also leave his cutout half knocked down. They shout slogans in favour of RJD chief Lalu Prasad and its working president Tejashwi Prasad Yadav.One of them carries an RJD flag tied to a stick. No other individual carries an RJD flag. Some of them had arrived on motor cycles, left parked by the side on the bridge.Half a dozen policemen are seen telling them to stop what they were doing, and also trying to wave them away. They did not carry any baton, nor a rifle.The incident involving youths running amok on the bridge after its inauguration by PM immediately led to a war of words between BJP and RJD functionaries.A state BJP spokesman Neeraj Kumar Sharma assailed RJD and its workers, saying that they have not changed a bit from “being what they have been, the goondas and ruffians.”Yet another BJP spokesman and former MLA Prem Ranjan Patel said that he had seen the video on YouTube, and added: “PM Modi, by commissioning the bridge, had given a gift to the people of flood-affected Raghopur constituency (represented by Tejashwi in the assembly) and surrounding areas, but his party and its workers have shown that they are opposed to development. The people of the area will defeat Tejashwi in the next election.”In contrast, state RJD spokesman Chitranjan Gagan denied that the youths were RJD workers. “They, in fact, were local youths who were angry with PM Modi and the central government for various reasons. The PM, standing on the bridge, had waved his ‘gamchha’ towards them.”That apart, as the reports said, the controversy surrounding the change in the name of the bridge from Guru Gobind Singh Setu to Nitish Setu has spiralled into a controversy with a bearing on the election-bound Punjab.Following the reaction that Congress Rajya Sabha member Pawan Khera made on Saturday, the Punjab AAP leadership has also taken exception to the change in the name of the bridge.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Patna | Silver Rate in Patna | Bank Holidays in Patna | Public Holidays in Patna | Patna AQI | Weather in Patna | Petrol Price in Patna | Diesel Price in Patna | CNG Price in Patna | LPG Price in PatnaStay updated with the latest Patna news.
