headline: ‘I Have Never Torn A Book Or Opposed PM’s Decisions’: Minister Ashish Shelar Hits Out At Opposition Over
content: Pune: Maharashtra Minister, Ashish Shelar on Sunday in Pune, said he had never torn a book or opposed any decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while dismissing allegations raised by the Opposition over the electoral process as hypocrisy. Referring to the controversy surrounding the tearing of a book, Shelar said he did not support such acts and maintained that the Opposition was selectively questioning the electoral system despite remaining silent over irregularities in earlier elections.Shelar Denies Tearing Book, Reiterates Support For PM Modi’s DecisionsShelar said, “I have never torn any book. I have never torn a book, nor have I opposed any decision taken by the Prime Minister. I do not agree with the act of tearing books.”Speaking about the book and the debate surrounding India’s electoral system, Shelar said it was necessary to examine the developments concerning voters, the electoral machinery and election results over the past 75 years.Shelar Credits Earlier Political Leadership For Building Electoral MachineryHe said the country had successfully established a massive election machinery, crediting earlier political leadership for building the system. He also questioned why the Opposition had not raised similar concerns when irregularities were reported in previous elections.He said, “When we were in the Opposition, we never questioned the election management system. We continued to contest elections. The fact that such a massive electoral machinery was established in this country is an achievement of the political leadership of that time.”‘Even 300 MPs Cannot Get An Appointment With Election Commission’: Maharashtra Congress Chief Harshwardhan SapkalCalling the Opposition’s current stand hypocritical, Shelar said voters were intelligent and had confidence in Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He also pointed out that several surveys in recent days had projected more than 100 seats for the BJP.Questioning the arguments surrounding party ownership and election symbols, Shelar cited the split in the Congress during Indira Gandhi’s tenure. He said the Congress faction led by Indira Gandhi was recognised as the party and received the hand symbol.He said, “If this principle was accepted in Indira Gandhi’s time, why should the same yardstick not apply to Eknath Shinde and Ajit Pawar? The issue of claiming a party and its symbol was prevalent even then.”Level up your brain the fun way. Play daily games and quizzes on FPJ Smart!

headline: 500 mn lifted out of poverty, but some still hesitate to acknowledge it: PM
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday said some individuals still hesitate to acknowledge that 50 crore people have been pulled out of poverty in the country, in an apparent dig at the Opposition. Addressing BJP workers virtually during a post-Diwali 'Sneh Milan' programme organised across all 182 assembly constituencies in Gujarat, he said the achievement reflected the success of his government's policies and efforts. "All those who sacrificed their lives for independence, all those who dedicated their lives to freedom, all those who spent their youth in jails for independence, wherever their souls may be, today they must be the happiest seeing this World Bank report, thinking, 'finally, poverty is leaving my country'," he said. According to a World Bank report, India's extreme poverty rate dropped sharply to 2.6 per cent in 2023 from 27.1 per cent in 2011, with the country lifting an estimated 496 million people out of poverty. "A thousand years of slavery had impoverished us; for the first time after a thousand years of slavery, 50 crore people are coming out of poverty. There can be no greater satisfaction in life than this, no greater achievement than this," Modi said. However, he said some people were still reluctant to acknowledge the achievement. "I know many people still hesitate to say this aloud, because all of this happened during this period (BJP rule). They don't like it. Whether they like it or not, we have the satisfaction that our efforts have borne fruit," Modi said. Terming the development the beginning of a new chapter in the lives of citizens, he said coming generations would witness the country's "golden era". "Our intention is true, our policy is right, our direction is right, and there is no shortcoming in our hard work," he said. The BJP had organised the programme across all 182 assembly constituencies in Gujarat. Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel listened to the PM's virtual address in his Ghatlodia constituency. Modi said this year's Diwali was significant for him as it marked 25 years since he became Gujarat's chief minister in October 2001. He credited generations of BJP workers for supporting him in his political journey and said their hard work had enabled him to serve his home state and the country. Recalling the devastating 2001 Gujarat earthquake, Modi said his first Diwali as chief minister was spent with affected families. "That day, my belief became very strong that the true happiness of festivals, the true joy of festivals, lies in lighting a lamp of hope in someone else's life," he said. Modi said the spirit of public participation had helped Gujarat overcome the devastation and transform Kutch into a new centre of hope. The reconstruction efforts subsequently spread across the state, leading to a wider transformation, he said. Recalling Gujarat's development journey, Modi said the state, once largely associated with trade, had expanded its presence in sectors such as agriculture, dairy, industries, semiconductors, petrochemicals, automobiles and green energy. He said Gujarat's economic progress had contributed significantly to the country's development and reiterated his earlier slogan of achieving national development through Gujarat's development. Recalling the difficult years around 2001, he said party workers had gone door-to-door collecting 'sukhdi' (a traditional sweet) for poor families to provide them with essential nutrition. They had also arranged cattle fodder from different parts of the country during droughts and organised cattle camps, he said. The PM said public participation had helped Gujarat overcome droughts and water shortages. "Campaigns to conserve water and construct check dams had gradually turned into mass movements, changing the situation in the state," he said. The prime minister also referred to the Garib Kalyan Melas launched during his tenure as chief minister in 2001, saying they helped build confidence among poor families and encouraged them to come out of poverty. "The experience gained from launching such programmes helped me create welfare schemes introduced by my government at the Centre after 2014," Modi said. Modi recalled that when his government started opening bank accounts for the poor, critics questioned their utility, while similar doubts were raised over the provision of LPG connections to households that could not afford cylinder refills. "We kept making scheme after scheme and taking them to the last person in the queue. We proved what social justice means for those who are rightful claimants and in need. And who were the ones without bank accounts? Our Dalit families, tribal families, the oppressed and downtrodden, as well as the women," the PM said. While bank accounts were opened, gas stoves arrived in homes, and electricity connections and Ayushman cards were distributed to the needy, he said. "As a result of all these schemes, 50 crore people have come out of poverty," the PM added. Modi urged BJP workers to keep national interest above party interests. He said the social harmony and unity developed in Gujarat would help the state and the country progress. He expressed confidence that Gujarat would achieve much more in the next 20 years than it had accomplished over the previous 25 years.

headline: West Bengal govt in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres in Singur: CM
content: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said his government was in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres of land in Singur in Hooghly district, a day after Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar announced Ashok Leyland would set up a truck manufacturing plant there.Singur was the site of Tata Motors' Nano small-car factory, for which the then Left Front government acquired around 997 acres in 2006. The acquisition triggered a prolonged farmers' agitation led by Mamata Banerjee, following which Tata Motors moved the project to Sanand in Gujarat in 2008.In August 2016, the Supreme Court quashed the land acquisition and ordered that the land be returned to the farmers."The West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) had been tasked with acquiring the 997 acres, and negotiations with farmers were underway to purchase the land at a reasonable rate," Adhikari told reporters.He said the government would "do something" with the land, without mentioning Ashok Leyland or its proposed truck factory at the site.Describing Singur as a symbol of West Bengal's industrial decline, Adhikari claimed farmers were unable to grow paddy, potato or mustard on the land returned to them."An earlier attempt by the previous government to promote fish farming there had also failed," he said."The farmers had received compensation twice -- first when the land was acquired during the Left Front regime and again in 2016-17 following the Supreme Court verdict," he added.Speaking to reporters after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's programme at IIT-Kharagpur on Saturday, Majumdar had said the BJP government was committed to bringing industry to Singur."We want to bring industry back to Singur. Our chief minister has also said so. I am reiterating today that Ashok Leyland is coming to Singur. It will set up a truck manufacturing plant, and work will begin soon," the Union Minister of State for Education had said.Adhikari said the government had accepted the 2013 land acquisition policy and the concept of land pooling, but did not elaborate."The state was also exploring the possibility of setting up solar power projects, which is environment-friendly, and substantial land is available in Purulia," he said.The government was separately purchasing land from owners of closed jute mills in the Barrackpore industrial belt as part of a major acquisition drive, he said, adding that 8,000-10,000 acres will be acquired over the next three months."The government is also interested in purchasing land in Bhangar, near New Town, from owners willing to sell at prices fixed by them," he added.

headline: Cloud over Parliament's Winter Session as uncertainty over dates persists
content: Uncertainty over the dates of Parliament’s Winter Session has persisted as the Monsoon Session remained unprorogued for 101 days after it was adjourned, setting a new record. The Winter Session traditionally runs from the last week of November to the third week of December. Both Houses were adjourned sine die (indefinitely) on August 13 but were not formally prorogued until Sunday evening.

headline: PM Modi's criticism of industry calls for a two-way reform dialogue
content: The next leap for India must begin with honest self-reflection, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi last Thursday underlined in his address at the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (Ficci). Stressing that industry must reflect on its performance, the PM sent a strong message to captains of India Inc, rebuking them for having failed to do enough on job creation, wage increases, investment, and building capabilities to ramp up competitiveness and lowering import dependence. Mr Modi took on India Inc’s preoccupation with short-term growth riding on a captive domestic market, and what he termed an insatiable “appetite” of companies for the government doing the heavy lifting for them, be it in the form of cuts in corporation tax and tariff protections, or demand creation through reduction in personal income tax and goods and services tax, and new trade deals. For good measure, the PM reminded the members of Ficci, which is entering its 100th year, that Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi had delivered them a similar message in 1930, and rhetorically asked if his need to reiterate the need for self-reliance reflected industry’s success or failure.

headline: PM Modi expresses happiness over people buying less gold after his appeal
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday expressed happiness over people buying less gold following an appeal made by him last year, claiming gold prices fell due to this.Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan here, Modi said, "Today, you must have seen that there is a lot of discussion in the media and on social media. In that discussion, everyone is saying today that Modi ji said in Parliament in 2023 that you should invest your money in bonds issued by the Government of India's PSUs. You will make a fortune. People mocked me at the time, but today history bears witness that those who invested made a fortune." Referring to the fall in prices of gold, Modi said, "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it, and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell." He went on to say, "Today, I'm going to say something else. Mark my words: Times are changing, and people with skills will be valued more than those who go around with paper certificates, wearing suits and ties. Demand for those with skills, those with talent, will increase." PM further said, "I am happy because just as people once followed Lal Bahadur Shastri ji's request to skip one meal for the nation, our citizens listened. Such is the character of this nation.

headline: Thanks to PM Modi, gold price drops ₹65 lakh per kg: CTI writes open letter, ‘Your advice helped protect savings’
content: On November 22, the Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) formally thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The trade body credited his appeal to limit gold purchases with helping traders avoid losses. In its letter, CTI said jewellers and investors who held off had protected their money.PM Modi made the appeal in May, asking people to avoid unnecessary gold purchases. He urged consumers to limit purchases for a year to conserve India’s foreign exchange reserves.The government also raised the import duty on gold from 6% to 15%. PM Modi later repeated his appeal in a video message on X. He said people told him that they had saved money after following his May appeal.CTI said gold was priced at ₹1.90 crore per kg when the prime minister gave the advice. The chamber put the price at ₹1.25 crore per kg on November 22.That works out to a drop of ₹65 lakh per kg using CTI’s figures. According to the chamber, jewellers often hold several months of stock. Those buying at the earlier price could have faced heavy losses, it argued.CTI said the appeal helped small traders who would buy and sell gold online or offline. It said stock market investors also avoided losses. According to CTI, some jewellers and traders who initially opposed the advice later supported it. The chamber thanked Modi on behalf of the trading community.“Mr Prime Minister, your advice helped protect the savings of lakhs of families. On behalf of CTI and the entire trading community, we thank you from the heart,” CTI wrote in its open letter.Goodreturns reported Delhi’s 24-carat gold price at ₹15,250 per gram on May 9. That was a day before Modi’s appeal. The rate later fell to ₹12,523 per gram, down ₹2,727 from the May figure.The chamber said cheaper gold was helping families buy jewellery during the wedding season. CTI put the number of weddings this season at 52 lakh.Jeweller Ashish Gupta told Nikkei Asia that visits had fallen about 30% from last year. He said some customers who had previously bought 10-gram pieces were choosing 5-gram pieces instead.Gold importIndia’s gold imports fell 81% in September, according to Commerce and Industry Ministry data. Their value dropped to $1.8 billion from $9.6 billion in September last year. Between April and September, the value of gold imports fell 27.3% to $19.27 billion.Economist NR Bhanumurthy pointed to higher import duty and a jump in international gold prices. He identified both as possible reasons for weaker demand.CTI asked the government to continue guiding traders in the gold and silver markets. It said regular guidance could help protect these markets from speculation and hoarding. Chairman Brijesh Goyal and other CTI office bearers signed the letter.

headline: Yuzvendra Chahal joins BJP: Indian cricketer appointed special invitee to National OBC Morcha executive committee
content: Indian cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and been appointed as a special invitee to the party's National Other Backward Classes (OBC) Morcha executive committee. The appointment was announced on Saturday as part of the BJP's latest organisational reshuffle.Chahal has been included among three special invitees to the OBC Morcha's national executive committee. He has been appointed from Delhi, while the other two special invitees are Professor Advait Charan Gananayak from Odisha and advocate Seema Samriddhi Kushwaha from Uttar Pradesh.The appointments were made on the directions of BJP national president Nitin Nabin. OBC Morcha national president and Rajya Sabha MP Amarpal Maurya announced the new appointments, which also included changes to several key organisational positions. Chahal thanks senior BJP leadershipIn a post on X, the leg-spinner thanked the senior BJP leadership for giving him a place and respect within the party. “I sincerely thank respected Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi ji, respected Home Minister Shri Amit Shah ji, BJP National President Shri Nitin Naveen ji, and OBC Morcha National President Shri Amarpal Maurya ji for giving me a place and respect within the BJP family,” he wrote. Chahal’s cricketing careerThe Haryana spinner kickstarted his international career with an ODI against Zimbabwe in June 2016, and also made his T20I debut against the same opponents a week later. He has, however, fallen out of favour in recent times and last played for India in a T20I against West Indies in August 2023. The 36-year-old has played 72 ODIs and 80 T20Is, and has taken 121 and 96 wickets in the two formats respectively. Chahal was part of the India squad for the 2019 ODI World Cup, where the Men in Blue reached the semifinals before losing to New Zealand.Chahal, who hasn't played Tests for India, retired from First-Class cricket in October this year. Iin the IPL, the right-arm leg-break bowler has played for several teams, including Mumbai Indians, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals and most recently Punjab Kings. He has played 188 IPL matches since making his debut in 2013 and has taken 233 wickets. Chahal is currently the all-time leading wicket-taker in the IPL, with Bhuvneshwar Kumar in second place with 226 scalps.

headline: ‘No one can take away livelihood of a skilled person’: PM Modi on AI, calls for equal respect for ITI, IIT students
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday addressed growing anxieties around artificial intelligence (AI) and job security, asserting that while AI is widely discussed, it cannot threaten the livelihood of someone who possesses real skills. Speaking at the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow, Modi said that times are changing and India is steadily moving towards becoming the skill capital of the world. AI, skills, and moving beyond ‘paper certificates’ Addressing concerns that artificial intelligence could displace workers, the Prime Minister stressed that practical talent will outlast mere academic credentials. "There is a lot of discussion about AI, but remember that no one can take away the livelihood of a person who possesses skills," Modi said. "Times are changing. Skilled individuals will command greater respect than those who merely hold certificates," he added. Modi also praised citizens for heeding his earlier appeal to curb unnecessary gold purchases, drawing a parallel to former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri's famous call to the nation. "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens to not buy gold if they don't need it. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell," he said. "I am happy because just as people once followed Lal Bahadur Shastri ji's request to skip one meal for the nation, our citizens listened. Such is the character of this nation," he added. Making a fresh prediction for the country's workforce, he said, "Today, I'm going to say something else. Mark my words: Times are changing and people with skills will be valued more than those who go around with paper certificates, wearing suits and ties. Demand for those with skills, those with talent, will increase." From invaders to Macaulay: How traditional skills were undermined Tracing the historical decline of India's traditional craftsmanship, Modi said foreign invaders deliberately damaged the country's skill infrastructure, while British colonial rule later reshaped education to serve its own manufacturing interests. "When invaders came to India, their first attack was on our skills. They knew that the craftsmanship of Indians was making the country great and prosperous, and sought to destroy it by cutting off the thumbs of artisans," Modi told the gathering. "The British were more sophisticated. They changed their methods. (British politician Thomas Babington) Macaulay imposed an education system that reduced our skill-based system to producing clerks," he said. He noted that even after independence, clerical roles continued to be prioritised while traditional craftsmanship took a back seat. "Over time, being a paper clerk came to be seen as a matter of prestige," he added. Highlighting India's rich artisanal heritage, Modi said, "India has always been a country that respects skills. Look at the chikankari work here in Lucknow. For a long time, India's identity in the world was built around such skills. From fine muslin, Banarasi and Kanchipuram silk, Kashmiri pashmina and cotton textiles to kalamkari, and from steel used to make some of the world's finest swords to bronze and panchdhatu (five-metal alloy) sculptures, there were countless such crafts." Equal respect for IIT and ITI students Stressing that India can progress in the 21st century only by respecting its skilled workforce, Modi pointed to government efforts such as the 'Shramev Jayate' initiative and the creation of a dedicated Ministry of Skill Development. He called for a shift in societal attitudes towards vocational education, highlighting the backbone role played by Industrial Training Institute (ITI) graduates. "Just as IIT students are respected, my ITI students should receive the same respect. Even the biggest companies may have two or three people carrying paper certificates, but they need 200 to 300 ITI-trained people to provide strength and run the company," he said. "Be it IIT or ITI, for me, students are the treasure, strength and future of the country," he added. Recalling the COVID-19 pandemic, Modi noted that the migration of workers from cities back to villages demonstrated how vital skilled manpower is to daily life. "People realised that no matter how wealthy one is, it is impossible to lead a normal life without skilled manpower. These skilled workers are the ones who kept things running and sustained the nation," he said. Linking skill development directly to India's manufacturing boom, the Prime Minister noted that nearly 5,000 new ITIs have been built over the last decade. "There was a time when India used to import mobile phones. Today, the daughters of our country are manufacturing them. Mobile phones made in India are now being exported across the globe. It is because of you that the country's manufacturing capacity is growing. This is why ITIs are being given such great importance today," he said. "The number of those studying in ITIs has also increased by over 5 lakh, with the number of girls increasing more than two and a half times," he added. UP's industrial push and 2027 WorldSkills Competition Modi highlighted Uttar Pradesh's expanding industrial and infrastructure base—citing upcoming large mobile manufacturing hubs, a semiconductor manufacturing facility, and the production of BrahMos missiles in the state—as key drivers of new opportunities for the youth. He also announced that India will host the 2027 WorldSkills Competition in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh. Lauding the Yogi Adityanath government for improving law and order, Modi recalled a factory inauguration in his parliamentary constituency of Varanasi where a woman told him she could safely return home even after working until 11 pm. "This is not an ordinary thing. Under the leadership of Yogi ji, the BJP government has created an environment of security in Uttar Pradesh," he said. Concluding his address with a message to the youth, the Prime Minister said, "Security and confidence in prosperity will build a developed India. I tell every young person in the country that the entire sky is open before you. Dream big, develop your skills and work with all your strength to fulfil your dreams. Never feel that you are alone. Whenever you feel so, remember that I stand with you."

headline: RJD supporters tear PM Modi, NDA posters at newly opened Nitish Setu
content: The newly inaugurated Nitish Setu in Vaishali district, Bihar, witnessed bedlam as scores of youths, reportedly owing allegiance to Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), ran amok, tearing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and NDA banners and posters. The incident, which lasted about 40 minutes, occurred hours after Modi inaugurated the six-lane bridge on river Ganga on Saturday.Videos posted on social media show some youth tearing down posters and banners of the Prime Minister and the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), waving RJD flags and raising slogans in support of party leaders Lalu Prasad and Tejashwi Prasad Yadav.The disruption, which lasted nearly 40 minutes according to accounts, unfolded after the formal ceremony. Footage circulating widely shows young men pulling down large hoardings featuring Modi, some trampling banners under foot, and moving about on motorcycles while police personnel stood nearby. The bridge was thrown open to the public shortly after Modi’s departure.The police said it detained three youths, hailing from Jafrabad tola of Rurstanmpur area, for creating ruckus and obstructing the administrative works.The 9.76-km main span of the cable-stayed structure, part of a roughly 19.7-km project including approach roads, connects Kacchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali. Built at an estimated cost of Rs 4,280 crore, it is expected to ease pressure on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and improve links between north and south Bihar.Modi dedicated the bridge as a tribute to former chief minister Nitish Kumar’s contribution to the state. The visit also marked one year of the NDA government under chief minister Samrat Choudhary.A political slugfest ensued after the incident. BJP spokesperson Neeraj Kumar Sharma accused the RJD of preferring disruption over development.Meanwhile. RJD MP Sudhakar Singh defended the action as a legitimate protest. He argued that the bridge had already been inaugurated earlier and that large sums had been spent on a second ceremony essentially to rename it. The posters and banners, he claimed, had been put up “in a fraudulent manner.”Earlier, leader of the opposition Tejashwi Yadav had questioned the repeated inauguration of the same project and the decision to name it Nitish Setu, suggesting it sent a message that the JD(U) leader’s political career was being closed.He had also claimed the project originated during the previous Mahagathbandhan government when he held the road construction portfolio.The Nitish Setu is one of several major infrastructure projects the NDA has sought to highlight. Its opening was accompanied by the inauguration or foundation-laying of other schemes worth tens of thousands of crores.

headline: Odisha government orders inquiry into Patnaik, Pandian's overseas visits
content: HYDERABAD: The Odisha government has ordered an inquiry into the foreign visits undertaken by former chief minister Naveen Patnaik, retired IAS officer VK Pandian and IPS officer Ravi Kant during 2022-23 and 2023-24, following allegations of irregularities in travel expenditure.Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has assigned the inquiry to the Principal Secretary of the General Administration Department. According to a statement issued by the Chief Minister's Office, the investigation will examine the overseas visits, particularly those to Japan and Italy..The decision follows complaints by social activists who, citing information obtained through Right to Information (RTI) applications, questioned the expenditure records of the trips. They alleged that the available details were incomplete, inconsistent and lacked transparency. The CMO also said allegations had been raised that information about the visits was deliberately withheld.Reacting to the decision, the opposition Biju Janata Dal (BJD) welcomed the inquiry, saying people had the right to know the facts. However, party media coordinator Lenin Mohanty described the move as an attempt to divert public attention from other issues..Mohanty said Patnaik had officially travelled abroad only twice during his 24-year tenure as chief minister. He said the Italy visit in 2022 was linked to an engagement with the World Food Programme, while the 2023 Japan visit was aimed at attracting investment to Odisha.The BJD also called for similar inquiries into the foreign visits of Majhi, his cabinet colleagues and senior government officials, arguing that transparency and accountability should apply equally to all governments.Patnaik served as Odisha chief minister from 2000 to 2024. Pandian, who was his close aide and private secretary for over a decade, took voluntary retirement from the IAS in 2023 before joining the BJD. He withdrew from active politics after the party's defeat in the 2024 elections.

headline: BJP protests in Latur over Amit Deshmukh’s Tipu Sultan remarks
content: LATUR: BJP leaders protested in Latur on Sunday, November 22, criticising Maharashtra Congress MLA Amit Deshmukh’s remarks about Tipu Sultan at a birth anniversary event held in the city.The programme was organised by the Sher-e-Hind Shaheed Hazrat Tipu Sultan Public Birth Anniversary Celebration Committee.Congress MLA Amit Deshmukh, along with Latur MP Dr Shivaji Kalge, attended the event.The Congress leader paid tribute to Tipu Sultan’s portrait and spoke about making information and books about the ruler available to younger generations..He also said that younger generations should understand who Tipu Sultan was and that he would extend assistance towards the initiative. He added that the Latur Municipal Corporation would act on recommendations to preserve Tipu Sultan’s memory in the city..Following Deshmukh’s remarks, the BJP criticised the Congress MLA and staged a protest to express its displeasure.Maharashtra BJP minister Nitesh Rane strongly opposed the remarks, describing them as the glorification of Tipu Sultan. He also warned those who praised the ruler or supported distributing books about him.Amit Deshmukh’s younger brother and former Congress MLA, Dheeraj Deshmukh, defended him, alleging that political opponents were circulating selected portions of Amit’s speech to create controversy and distort its context.He added that the event was intended to promote awareness of historical personalities and their contributions and should be viewed in the context of art, music and social harmony.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: Shah raps Congress for neglecting Arunachal
content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Sunday that the Congress did not focus enough on development and gave too little financial help during its time in Arunachal Pradesh. He said the Centre, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has now increased support for the State’s progress.At an event held by the State Cooperation Department, Shah said the Centre gave Arunachal Pradesh Rs 33,530 crore during the UPA Government from 2004 to 2014. He said this amount rose to Rs 1,64,664crore from 2014 to 2024 under the NDA government. Shah also said tax devolution to the state rose fourfold and grants increased 18 times.Shah said these numbers show the Modi Government’s commitment to developing Arunachal Pradesh and the Northeast. He pointed to the rise in Arunachal Pradesh’s budget from Rs 12,000 crore to Rs 36,000 crore over the past 12 years as a sign of progress.Shah talked about the Vibrant Villages Programme and said the prime minister calls border villages the country’s first villages. He said development should start at the borders and that people living there should have basic facilities and job opportunities. Shah said the programme has helped bring people back to almost 40 villages in Arunachal Pradesh. He added that the Government is working on issues like electricity, schools, basic services, and jobs in these areas.Shah said the Northeast has seen big improvements in connectivity and development over the past 12 years under Prime Minister Modi. He said the gap between the region and the national capital has become smaller.The home minister said all state capitals in the Northeast now have better road, rail, and air connections. He said the region has seen a lot of new infrastructure and called improved connectivity a major NDA achievement.Shah said the Centre has made the Northeast a priority in its development plans, focusing on education, economic growth, jobs for young people, and industrial growth. He credited Prime Minister Modi for promoting the region’s tourism and natural resources.“PM Modi has also become a key ambassador for promoting Northeast tourism across the country and has started efforts to boost industry while protecting the region’s natural beauty,” Shah said.Shah said the Centre has made the region’s development a priority, focusing on education, skill training, and jobs for young people.Shah said development in the Northeast means building infrastructure, growing the economy, improving people’s lives, keeping cultural traditions, and creating chances for local communities. He said the region’s natural resources and tourism could support India’s development if used well.Shah, who is also the cooperation minister, said village cooperatives are now buying farm produce, milk, eggs, and vegetables from local communities instead of getting them from Tezpur or Guwahati. He said this is making the rural economy stronger and helping security personnel and villagers work more closely together. Shah called for self-reliance and urged Arunachal Pradesh to grow its dairy, meat, and fish production. He said Amul and the National DairyDevelopment Board (NDDB) would buy all the milk produced in the State.Shah asked the Arunachal Pradesh Government to make the state self-reliant in producing milk, eggs, meat, and fish. He said the goal should be to stop depending on supplies from outside the State.Shah said reaching self-sufficiency in these areas could help at least 32,000 families become financially independent. He asked the state government to create a full self-reliance plan, using cooperatives to support dairy and fisheries and improve rural livelihoods.Shah said more than 50,000 people are part of 185 primary agricultural credit societies, 52 dairy cooperatives, and 43 fish farms. He suggested starting fish farming in hydropower reservoirs to create rural jobs.On infrastructure in the State, he mentioned the 2,880-MW Dibang hydropower project, which is being built at a cost of about Rs 32,000 crore. He also spoke about the Balipara-Charduar-Tawang road, the Nechiphu tunnel, and a bridge over the Sisi River in Dibang Valley. Shah mentioned the double-decker road-and-rail bridge connecting Pasighat and Dibrugarh, as well as start of coal mining in the State.

headline: South Korea education minister resigns after AI-assisted exam cheating scandal
content: South Korea: South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday, November 22, taking responsibility for the government's inadequate preparation to prevent AI-assisted cheating ahead of the country's highly competitive university entrance examination.President Lee Jae Myung accepted his resignation, the presidential office said.According to The Guardian, the controversy broke out after the top scorer in a national tax accountant examination admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to cheat and obtain a near-perfect score. The incident came into light just four days before South Korea's annual College Scholastic Ability Test, commonly known as Suneung..The confession led the authorities to introduce extra security measures shortly before the university entrance examination, held on November 19. These included requiring candidates to surrender electronic devices, inspecting clothing and accessories for concealed cameras and blocking public Wi-Fi near examination areas. However, these last-minute changes drew criticism from students, teachers and parents, who said the measures added to the pressure surrounding an already stressful examination..In a statement announcing his resignation, Choi acknowledged that the government had failed to prepare adequately in advance. He said the examination had concluded without any major incidents but that he could not avoid criticism over the confusion caused by the changes.Yonhap News Agency reported that President Lee accepted the resignation about an hour after Choi announced his decision.The 72-year-old minister had also faced criticism over remarks made during a parliamentary hearing on November 16. He had been asked whether authorities could detect all attempts at AI-assisted cheating, to which he reportedly said he was not confident because of his age. The response triggered a public backlash..Authorities recorded 111 cases involving electronic-device violations during Thursday's examination, according to the Education Ministry. Nearly half were detected through emergency alerts sent to mobile phones across the country, The Guardian reported.The alerts were designed to expose candidates who had failed to surrender their phones. They sounded at full volume and could not be silenced, allowing examination officials to identify devices that remained switched on..The Suneung is one of South Korea's most important examinations, with university admissions playing a significant role in students' future academic and career prospects. The country makes extensive arrangements to ensure the test runs smoothly, including rescheduling aircraft movements during the English listening section and suspending certain military exercises.The resignation comes amid growing concerns over the use of artificial intelligence to cheat in competitive examinations. President Lee has called for a review of examination procedures, stressing that fairness in assessments must be protected as technology advances.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: CM Revanth Reddy demands OBC count in 2027 Census, Rs 30,000 crore aid for El Niño
content: Hyderabad: Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday, November 22 demanded the inclusion of OBC enumeration in the 2027 Population Census and sought Rs 30,000 crore in central assistance to tackle the impact of El Niño in the state.Addressing the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee’s (TPCC) Political Affairs Committee (PAC) meeting at Gandhi Bhavan, the Chief Minister said Telangana had conducted a caste census for the first time in 100 years. The PAC adopted a resolution demanding OBC enumeration in the national census and asked TPCC president B Mahesh Kumar Goud to write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi regarding the issue..Revanth Reddy announced a five-month ‘Praja Balam’ programme after Sankranti, instructing party leaders to visit every village and take on assigned responsibilities. He assured that there would be no shortage of funds and said the government would soon launch a major initiative to provide employment opportunities for all.Citing inadequate rainfall due to El Niño, he appealed to farmers to cultivate dry crops and sought Rs 30,000 crore from the Centre for relief measures. He mentioned that Telangana was not facing a foodgrain shortage. With neighbouring Maharashtra and Karnataka also experiencing drought conditions, he said available water in projects would be reserved for drinking water needs over the next eight months.He added that the state was meeting a power demand of 20,000 MW without interruptions, while also protecting agricultural crops..Launching a sharp attack on the BJP-led Centre over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Revanth Reddy alleged that 71 lakh votes had been set aside in Telangana and 13 crore votes removed nationwide. He warned that the number could reach 20 crore, claiming that Dalits, Adivasis, tribal communities, and women were particularly vulnerable to exclusion.Urging Congress workers and Booth Level Officers to remain vigilant against deletions due to migration and discrepancies in surnames, he called for a ‘Gyanesh Kumar Go Back’ campaign on the lines of the historic ‘Simon Go Back’ movement.The Chief Minister also welcomed the new Telangana Congress in-charge, BM Sandeep, and thanked Sonia Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, and Rahul Gandhi for the appointment. Crediting outgoing in-charge Meenakshi Natarajan, he highlighted that Congress secured 66 percent of panchayat seats and an 85 percent success rate in municipal elections during her tenure.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: Assam Congress to hold ‘Save Constitution’ march in Guwahati on November 26
content: Guwahati, Nov 22: The Assam Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) will organise a ‘Save Constitution Padayatra’ in Guwahati on November 26, joining a nationwide programme led by the Congress to mark Constitution Day.APCC Co-in-charge Manoj Chauhan announced the programme at a press conference at Rajiv Bhawan in Guwahati on Sunday, as part of the Congress’s ongoing “Save Vote, Save Country” campaign led by Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi. Chauhan said the Congress and its INDIA bloc allies have been organising protest programmes over the past several months to protect the Constitution and raise awareness about what it calls threats to democracy and the electoral process. "Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah, in collusion with the country's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, have formed the government through vote theft and have plundered the nation's democracy,” he said. Chauhan also criticised the Centre over the appointment process for Election Commissioners. Referring to a 2023 Supreme Court judgment, he alleged that the government subsequently replaced the Chief Justice of India in the selection panel with a Cabinet minister through legislation passed by Parliament. The “Save Constitution Padayatra” will be held in state capitals across the country on November 26, which marks Constitution Day. "We appeal to all those who believe in the country's democracy and Constitution to participate in the Save Constitution Padayatra on November 26 and save the nation's democracy,” Chuahan added. The Congress reiterated three demands: the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, cancellation of the entire SIR process, which the party claims deleted 13.30 crore voter names nationwide and a return to ballot papers for all future Lok Sabha and Assembly elections. The Assam programme will be held at the Manabendra Sarma Complex in Guwahati from 11 am on November 26, APCC Media Department chairman Bedabrat Bora said. APCC Social Media Department chairman Rituparna Konwar and secretary Ghana Chutia were also present at the press conference.

headline: Gaurav Gogoi accuses BJP of funding party machinery with drug syndicate money
content: Guwahati, Nov 22: Assam Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) president Gaurav Gogoi on Saturday accused the ruling BJP of running its organisational machinery with money collected from drug syndicates. Addressing a press conference here, Gogoi alleged that there is an alarming proliferation and trafficking of drugs in the State. “While Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma are putting on a show of taking a tough stand against drugs, the BJP is actually running its organisational machinery with money collected from drug syndicates. The government is carrying out a few arrests through the police merely for publicity and electoral gains. However, instead of declining, the drug menace in the State is increasing day by day,” he said. He said that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had warned about the alarming drug problem in Punjab and across the country long ago, but instead of taking the issue seriously, the BJP had chosen to criticize him. “Had the Central and State governments taken stringent measures at that time, we would not have been witnessing the present situation,” he added. Referring to allegations surrounding the donation money collected for the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, Gogoi said, “A party capable of stealing even donations made to the Ram Temple would have little hesitation in running its organisation with money generated from drug syndicates.” He said that the younger generation, particularly Gen Z, and their parents in Assam were deeply concerned about the growing drug menace. “Instead of criticizing our younger generation, it is important that we listen to them. In the coming days, NSUI (Congress party’s student wing) will launch a social campaign among young people across Assam to create awareness with the objective of building a drug-free Assam. We will extend our full support to this initiative,” Gogoi said. He asserted that the Congress will continue its fight against alleged government “irregularities and conspiracies” carried out in the name of delimitation in Assam and will never withdraw from the electoral battlefield under any circumstances. “If the Congress party refuses to contest elections and withdraws from the battlefield, will the BJP stop stealing votes, imposing the National Security Act, or running syndicates? Only by fighting elections can we expose their corruption and make citizens aware that the power of the people is always greater than that of any political party,” Gogoi said.

headline: Bengal BJP MLA Rekha Patra critical after suspected pesticide poisoning
content: Kolkata Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from Hingalganj in West Bengal’s North 24 Parganas, Rekha Patra, was on Sunday (November 22, 2026) admitted to a private hospital in the city after falling ill from suspected pesticide poisoning. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ The MLA was admitted to Basirhat Subdivision Hospital, from where she was shifted to the private facility. West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya calls for protest over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya calls for protest over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh State BJP chief claims Bangladesh was created on the basis of religion, not language, as Bengali-speaking Hindus are now being persecuted and bearing the consequences of Partition West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya calls for protest over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh storyline 1 The referral card of the State-run hospital stated that a poisonous ‘herbal larvicide’ had entered her stomach. The medical report from the hospital in Kolkata, accessed by The Hindu, points to an “alleged history of poisoning (agricultural) on the home premises”. According to reports, the MLA was unconscious and was on ventilation. She remains unresponsive and has not opened her eyes. West Bengal Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee, along with other senior BJP leaders, met the family members of Ms. Patra at the hospital. The Minister, who is also a medical practitioner, said that the MLA fell ill after having food and that it could be a suspected case of “food poisoning”. Dr. Mukherjee said that Ms. Patra’s condition has improved. West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party “BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” alleged Bongaon MP Santanu Thakur West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party storyline 1 Ms. Patra came to prominence during the resistance led by women against former Trinamool leader Sheikh Shahjahan in early 2024. The BJP had fielded her from the Basirhat constituency in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, which she lost. She was elected to the West Bengal Assembly in May 2026. Over the past few weeks, the BJP MLA had expressed dissatisfaction with the party’s district leadership. She had publicly spoken about her political position and internal issues within the party.

headline: Akash Anand targets SP over Dalit outreach, slams BJP govt
content: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national convenor Akash Anand on Sunday accused the Samajwadi Party (SP) of remembering Dalits only during elections, while criticising the BJP government over its record on development, law and order, healthcare and education. He also slammed the Congress over its claims of concern for the Dalit community.Addressing a public meeting in Agra, a week after the SP organised a Dalit Sammelan in the city, Anand urged people to bring BSP chief Mayawati back as Uttar Pradesh chief minister for a fifth term.The meeting was organised in support of BSP candidate Sarvesh Baghel from the Etmadpur assembly constituency. Anand also urged party supporters to reach Lucknow on December 6, when Mayawati is scheduled to address a rally on the death anniversary of Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar.“I have come with a message from BSP national president Behenji (Mayawati), who has appealed to us all not to be misled by the false propaganda of Opposition leaders. A full ‘baraat’ (group) of leaders will come to you, some from Gujarat, others from Saifai, but they remember Dalits only when elections are around. We need not ask for directions to Agra because we ourselves belong here,” he said, asserting the BSP’s close association with the city, often referred to as the Dalit capital.Anand accused SP president Akhilesh Yadav of adopting an Ambedkarite stance for political gains and mocked the party’s PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) formulation.“I am unable to understand what Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav is up to. Until recently, the ‘P’ in PDA stood for Pichhda (backward), but when Brahmins began moving towards the BSP, Yadav termed it as Pandit. By the time elections come, this ‘P’ will stand for ‘pata nahin’ (not known),” he said, accusing the SP of changing its stand according to political convenience.Anand also demanded an apology from Akhilesh Yadav and senior SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav over an incident at the November 15 Dalit Sammelan. He alleged that Ram Gopal Yadav had insulted a Dalit community member in the audience by calling him ‘moorkh’ (fool) during his address.Drawing a comparison between the political significance of different regions for parties, Anand said Agra held the same place for the BSP as Ayodhya did for the BJP and Saifai and Etawah did for the SP.“Agra was once the capital of the Mughal Empire but is now the capital of Dalits. If Shah Jahan gave the Taj Mahal to Agra, Behenji gave the Yamuna Expressway to the city. Since the BSP lost power in the state, Agra has lost its priority. To restore its past status, Dalits should make Behenji the chief minister for a fifth time,” he said.Anand also criticised Akhilesh Yadav for his ‘chavanni’ remark against Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) president Jayant Chaudhary, who was an SP ally until recently.“Jayant Chaudhary is the grandson of Chaudhary Charan Singh, whom Mulayam Singh Yadav regarded as his ‘guru’. Yet Akhilesh Yadav did not hesitate to insult his grandson. He should apologise,” Anand said.Anand alleged that the SP and Congress, rather than the BSP, were the BJP’s “B teams”, echoing Mayawati’s charge that the BJP and Congress were two sides of the same coin.Targeting the BJP government, Anand questioned its claims of development, alleging that it had spent crores on publicity while neglecting essential services.“The BJP has been in power in the state for a decade, but what has it given the people of UP apart from advertisements costing crores? It claims UP is number one, but not in development. The state is number one in murders and crimes against women. The government has money for publicity but not for health services at medical colleges, and innocent infants lost their lives at Jhansi Hospital,” he alleged.He also criticised the government’s law-and-order claims, saying it appeared more interested in filming criminals during encounters than addressing the underlying problems.“This BJP regime claims itself to be a regime of encounters, but they seem more interested in filming criminals, and it appears as if the shooting of some serial is on. Schools are closing, teacher posts are vacant and examination papers are leaked. The BJP does not want us to be educated and wants us to continue standing in queues,” he alleged.Anand also accused the Congress of hypocrisy over its claims of concern for Dalits. He said Congress leader Rahul Gandhi invoked Babasaheb Ambedkar but did not acknowledge how the party had opposed Ambedkar’s election and how he was forced to resign from the Union cabinet after being harassed.

headline: ‘Haven’t invited me to discuss Indus waters’: Pak minister Musadik Malik evades questions on IWT, ‘cut off hands’ remark | India News
content: Pakistan minister Musadik Masood Malik said that Pakistan would discuss the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) only when formally invited to do so, deflecting questions on the issue from reporters in Delhi. Malik also dodged questions about his earlier controversial “cut off hands” remark, avoiding a direct response to the matter.“When you invite me to discuss the Indus Waters Treaty, we will certainly talk about it. You haven't invited me to discuss the Indus Waters Treaty at this moment,” Malik, who is attending the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, told reporters on Sunday.In June, Malik warned that Pakistan would "cut off that hand" which attempted to take away its share of water, accusing New Delhi of using water as a tool of pressure against Islamabad.‘Evidence can be presented bilaterally’: Pakistan minister on terrorismResponding to questions on terrorism, Malik called for discussions based on evidence, claiming that Islamabad was willing to engage with India on the issue through both bilateral and multilateral forums.“I assure you, such discussions will certainly happen...We have stated on many occasions - in various forums that evidence can be presented bilaterally; we have also suggested that this could be handled multilaterally, you bring your evidence, and we will bring ours,” he said.He said Pakistan was prepared to present its evidence and examine evidence presented by India, while accusing those raising the issue of merely seeking to provoke rather than finding a lasting solution."If you are seeking a lasting solution to the issue, rather than merely looking to provoke, then that is how we should proceed...I am offering you a stable, consistent response: whenever discussions take place, they will be based on evidence,” he added.ALSO READ: ‘Umeed hai aana jaana rahega’: Pakistan minister after attending SCO meet in DelhiPakistan minister gets approval for Taj Mahal visit, but Nizamuddin Dargah request rejectedMeanwhile, Malik's request to visit Taj Mahal in Agra has been approved, while the request to visit Nizamuddin Dargah in Delhi has been rejected, the ministry of external affairs said on Saturday, news agency ANI reported.The proposed visit to Nizamuddin Dargah has reportedly not been cleared by the security agencies and the ministry of external affairs.First time in 3 years that a Pak minister has visited IndiaMalik is in India from November 20 to 22. This is for the first time in three years that a Pakistani minister has visited India.On Friday, Malik said that Pakistan will fully support all efforts to take forward peace and security in the region. “Whenever you talk of peace and when different countries come together and they sit together and make efforts to take forward peace and security, then we will also participate fully,” Malik said on the sidelines on SCO event in Delhi, shortly after the event got underway with a speech by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.ALSO READ: ‘No change on Indus Waters Treaty stance’: MEA as Pak minister, who warned India, visits DelhiSpeaking about his visit being the first by the country's leader in three years, Malik said he hoped that such visits would continue in the future.“Mujhe ummeed hai ki dobara aap gila nahi karenge aur hamara aana jaana rahega...(I hope you won’t have any more complaints, and that we’ll continue to visit each other),” Malik told news agency ANI.

headline: 'Anti-Hindu, anti-Sanatan Dharma': BJP slams TN govt over Karthigai Deepam review plea
content: <p>New Delhi: The BJP on Sunday said the <a href="https://deccanherald.com/tags/tamil-nadu">Tamil Nadu</a> government's move to seek a review of a Supreme Court order permitting the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp on November 24 as a one-time measure at Deepathoon reflects an "anti-Hindu and anti-Sanatan Dharma" mindset of the Congress and its allies.</p>.<p>Deepathoon is a stone pillar atop the Thiruparankundram hill in <a href="https://deccanherald.com/tags/madurai">Madurai</a>.</p>.<p>The commissioner of Tamil Nadu's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department filed the review petition in the Supreme Court on Saturday, a day after the top court permitted the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp on November 24 as a one-time measure at Deepathoon.</p>.Tamil Nadu moves Supreme Court seeking review of order allowing Karthigai Deepam lighting at Thiruparankundram hill.<p>Reacting to the move, BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi told reporters, "It is very unfortunate that the INDI Alliance government of Tamil Nadu is hell-bent on not implementing the Supreme Court's judgment.</p>.<p>"This reflects the anti-constitutional mindset of the Congress and its ally parties. It also reflects their anti-Hindu and anti-Sanatan Dharma mindset," he charged.</p>.<p>The Tamil Nadu government's move also reflects the Congress and its allies' "hatred against Hindu Dharma," the BJP Rajya Sabha MP said, demanding that the Supreme Court's Friday judgment be implemented "immediately".</p>.<p>The Congress is an alliance partner in the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government in Tamil Nadu, headed by Chief Minister<a href="https://deccanherald.com/tags/joseph-vijay"> C Joseph Vijay</a>. </p>

headline: Pak minister seeks India's invitation for talks on Indus Waters Treaty, avoids questions on past threat
content: Pakistan's Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Minister Musadik Masood Malik on Sunday said he would discuss the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) with India if New Delhi extended a formal invitation for bilateral talks, when questioned about his earlier remarks threatening action over the suspension of the water-sharing agreement.Malik, who is leading Pakistan's delegation at the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, was asked about the treaty, which India placed in abeyance following the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack."When you invite me to discuss the Indus Water Treaty, we will certainly talk about it. You haven't invited me to discuss the Indus Water Treaty at this moment," he said.Asked about his earlier statements on the issue, Malik said he would respond to questions on specific bilateral matters if India initiated a formal dialogue."When you invite me to discuss those specific issues, I shall be there. But first, you must extend that invitation. Tell me that you wish to engage in a bilateral dialogue; when you invite me for such a discussion, I will be present, and I will then answer all the bilateral questions you choose to ask," he said..Malik's remarks came months after he criticised India's decision to place the 1960 treaty in abeyance. In June, he had warned that Pakistan would "cut off that hand" which attempted to take away its share of water, while accusing New Delhi of using water as a means of exerting pressure on Islamabad.India has maintained that its position on the treaty remains unchanged. On Friday, Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated New Delhi's stand when asked about Malik's visit and his earlier remarks."As far as the IWT is concerned, we have made our position very clear and that is where it remains. There is absolutely no change," Jaiswal said.India placed the treaty in abeyance after the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people were killed. New Delhi has said the decision will remain in force until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism.The suspension followed Operation Sindoor, launched by India in response to the Pahalgam attack. The operation targeted terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Military exchanges between the two countries continued until a ceasefire understanding was reached on May 10, 2025.The Indus Waters Treaty, signed in 1960, governs the sharing of the Indus river system between India and Pakistan. The river system is crucial to Pakistan's agriculture and water supply, with a large share of its agricultural land and water use dependent on its waters.Malik's visit to New Delhi for the November 20-22 SCO forum marks a rare visit by a Pakistani federal minister to India amid strained bilateral relations. India had invited all SCO member countries, including Pakistan, to participate in the multilateral event.(With inputs from ANI).Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: ‘We Are Servants, Not Rulers’: Tripura Minister Sudhangshu Das Highlights BJP’s Governance Philosophy & Questions CPI(M)’s 25-Year Record
content:
Addressing a large election rally at the Old Town Hall premises in Belonia, in the presence of BJP National General Secretary and Lok Sabha MP Biplab Kumar Deb, Das appealed to voters to support BJP candidates contesting all 17 wards of the Belonia Municipal Council in the November 27 elections.

Expressing confidence in the party’s electoral prospects, Das said the enthusiasm of supporters at the rally indicated strong public participation. He claimed that BJP candidates would secure victories by substantial margins when the results are declared on December 2.

Explaining the BJP’s governance approach, the minister identified three guiding principles — Seva (service), Garib Kalyan (welfare of the poor) and Sushasan (good governance). He said the party, under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership and the guidance of former Chief Minister Biplab Kumar Deb and incumbent Chief Minister Dr Manik Saha, was committed to working for the people rather than exercising power over them.

Referring to Modi’s description of himself as the ‘Pradhan Sevak’, Das said the BJP’s political philosophy revolved around public service. He cited the party’s organisational slogans, ‘Seva Hi Sangathan’ and ‘Seva Hi Sankalp’, to underline its emphasis on serving people.

The minister devoted a significant part of his address to housing and other welfare programmes. Claiming that approximately 4.5 lakh houses had been provided to beneficiaries in Tripura under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana since 2018, he said another one lakh houses were expected to be taken up in the coming year.

Comparing the figures with the previous Left Front government, Das referred to a response given by former Deputy Chief Minister Jishnu Dev Varma in the Assembly during his tenure as an MLA. According to Das, around 52,000 houses had been sanctioned during the CPM’s 25-year rule, but funds for 2,240 houses were returned due to beneficiaries being excluded from the list. He contrasted this with the housing figures achieved under the BJP government.

headline: Former Chief Minister Manik Sarkar Slams State Government Over Governance And Public Issues At Dharmanagar.
content:
Dharmanagar, Tripura, 22nd of November 2026 : Braving the rain, a massive public rally was organised at the grounds of Dinanath Narayani Vidyamandir in Dharmanagar in support of the Left Front candidates ahead of the upcoming Dharmanagar Municipal Council elections.Former Tripura Chief Minister and senior CPI(M) leader Manik Sarkar attended the rally as the chief speaker.

During his address, he launched a series of sharp political attacks against the present state government.Also present at the rally were Politburo/State Committee member Amitabha Datta, several Left Front leaders from the Dharmanagar subdivision and district levels, CPI(M) candidates nominated by the Left Front for the municipal elections, and a large number of party workers and supporters.

Addressing the gathering, Manik Sarkar described the present government’s claims of development as misleading and far removed from reality. He alleged that the rule of law in the state had virtually collapsed. According to him, repeated attacks on opposition political parties, the curtailment of democratic rights, and an atmosphere of political vendetta have created growing concern among ordinary citizens.

He further alleged that uncontrolled price rise has made life increasingly difficult for common people. Unemployment, he said, has reached alarming proportions, while the government has failed to provide any effective roadmap for generating employment. He also claimed that rural people were not receiving adequate work under the MGNREGA scheme, which remains an important source of livelihood for rural households. He accused the ruling establishment of misleading people with various promises ahead of the elections.

Manik Sarkar’s speech made it clear that he sought to portray the municipal election not merely as a contest for control of the Municipal Council, but also as a platform for protesting against the prevailing political situation in the state.Highlighting the presence of party workers and supporters despite the rain, Left Front leaders expressed confidence in their electoral campaign while drawing attention to what they described as the challenging political circumstances under the present government.

In this backdrop, Manik Sarkar appealed to the people of Dharmanagar to support the Left Front-nominated CPI(M) candidates to form a transparent, accountable and development- oriented Dharmanagar Municipal Council. It now remains to be seen how far the political message delivered from the rally platform will influence the voters of Dharmanagar and whether it will translate into electoral gains for the Left Front in the upcoming municipal elections.

headline: 'Called Sanatan dengue, malaria': BJP slams Rahul Gandhi over his 'Ardhanareshwar' post
content: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Sunday hit out at Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the BJP and RSS accompanying an 'Ardhanareshwar' post, accusing him of having an "inherent hate for Sanatan". BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said Rahul had earlier referred to Sanatan Dharma as "dengue, malaria", while actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut accused the Congress of opposing women's reservation."India does not need lectures from Rahul Gandhi who called Hindus as Violent & gave clean chit to Pakistan because of vote bank politics! The more I listen to Rahul Gandhi, more I realise he has inherent hate for Sanatan! Do not forget they called Sanatan Dengue Malaria!" Bhandari said in a post on X.Reacting to the Rahul's remarks, Kangana accused the Congress of opposing the Women's Reservation Bill and preventing its implementation."If the BJP is male-dominated, why is it fighting for the Women's Reservation Bill? It is the Congress that is opposing the bill and preventing its implementation. The anti-women mindset is that of the Congress," she said.What Rahul Gandhi saidThe Congress leader called BJP and RSS "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists" with "no understanding of our spiritual and religious traditions" as he shared a Shiva-Parvati sculpture picture.Rahul's post came days after he faced criticism over his remarks about the relationship between his parents, Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi, during the launch of his mother's memoir, Belonging: A Journey Of Love.Speaking at the event, he had recalled how his parents would sit together during meals, saying, "there would be Papa, and on Papa's lap, there would be Mama."He later shared a photograph of a 12th-century temple sculpture depicting Goddess Parvati sitting on Lord Shiva's lap. Gandhi said fear, anger and hatred had created a barrier among BJP and RSS supporters and that he wanted them to experience love and belonging."As a true Hindu, it is my duty to free them from this web, so that they too can start to experience the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging in their lives. Satyam Shivam Sundaram," he had said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Ram Temple theft: Congress questions 21-day delay in FIR, alleges senior trust officials shielded
content: Questioning why senior Ram Temple trust officials were made witnesses rather than accused despite receiving evidence of alleged theft, the Congress on Sunday demanded a Supreme Court-monitored probe into the theft of offerings at Ayodhya's Ram Temple, asking why it took 21 days to register an FIR and why the investigation was confined to just eight employees despite 304 alleged instances of theft.Congress general secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Jairam Ramesh raised five questions over the 74,000-page charge sheet, alleging that the investigation had failed to examine the accountability of senior trust officials, allegations of irregularities in land deals and a complaint involving alleged misappropriation of over Rs 200 crore."Does this charge sheet contain a complete account of the thefts, or has it merely named eight employees as accused, shielding prominent figures and sidestepping serious questions?" Ramesh asked.Citing the charge sheet, he said Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai received a video of the alleged theft on WhatsApp on June 4. The footage reportedly showed Rs 2.25 lakh in cash bundles kept inside a bathroom. The following day, Anil Mishra and others allegedly watched the video at Rai's residence. However, the FIR was registered only on June 25.Ramesh questioned the delay, pointing out that the Uttar Pradesh government had constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) on June 13, three complaints were submitted between June 16 and 18, and eight suspects were identified in the SIT's preliminary report on June 23.He further alleged that the accused had returned stolen cash and jewellery in the presence of senior trust officials. However, Champat Rai, Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao were listed as witnesses numbered 18, 17 and 19, respectively."To what extent was the role of the senior officials to whom evidence of the theft reached, and in whose presence the recovery was made, investigated?" he asked.Reviving the controversy surrounding the 2021 Ram Temple land deals, Ramesh said allegations had surfaced that land purchased for Rs 2 crore was sold to the trust for Rs 18.5 crore within 10 minutes.He questioned why the report of the government-appointed inquiry committee had not been made public despite repeated demands for an investigation.The Congress also sought details of the reported reopening of the land deal investigation in July 2026 and questioned why the complete date-wise CCTV timeline of 304 alleged thefts had not been disclosed.Ramesh asked why no FIR was registered on Santosh Dubey's complaint alleging misappropriation of more than Rs 200 crore and who had determined the scope of the investigation into senior trust officials.Demanding an independent investigation reporting directly to the Supreme Court, he said the probe must examine the trust's functioning, the role of senior officials and the SIT's methods."The Ram Temple is a symbol of faith for hundreds of millions of people across the country. There must be an accounting of every rupee offered in Ram's name. No one can be allowed to escape accountability," Ramesh said.
