headline: BJP appoints Yuzvendra Chahal as special invitee to OBC Morcha executive committee
content: New Delhi Indian cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has been appointed as a Special Invitee to the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) National Other Backwards Classes (OBC) Morcha executive committee. Also read | Nitin Nabin announces his team; Smriti Irani, Ram Madhav make a comeback, Amit Malviya out https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/bjp-reshuffle-vasundhara-raje-ram-madhav-smriti-irani-vice-presidents-general-secretaries-organisational-overhaul/article71355824.ece BJP national president Nitin Nabin on Saturday (November 21, 2026) announced fresh appointments of national office-bearers, national executive members, and department heads for its OBC Morcha with immediate effect. According to the official communication issued by the party’s central office, the list includes seven national vice presidents, three national general secretaries, and seven national secretaries representing various states across the country. The new BJP team’s piecemeal reset The new BJP team’s piecemeal reset Apart from the usual distribution of organisational berths to poll-going States, caste groups, and other demographics of sex and age, the new BJP team reflects the party’s attempts at a reset. Nistula Hebbar reports on how three terms in power have brought both the pieties of the past and anxieties of the future into focus Spotlight The new BJP team’s piecemeal reset storyline 1 The seven newly appointed national vice presidents of the BJP OBC Morcha are Jogen Mohan (Assam), Mamata Mohanta (Odisha), Sangam Lal Gupta (Uttar Pradesh), Babanrao Ravji Choudhary (Maharashtra), Sat Prakash Rana (Delhi), Arjun Sahani (Bihar), and Sangeeta Balwant Bind (Uttar Pradesh). Gajendra Yadav (Delhi), Pramod Madhwaraj (Karnataka), and Lalit Chandrakar (Chhattisgarh) have been named as national general secretaries. The party also appointed seven national secretaries: Dashrathji Thakor (Gujarat), T Varatharajan (Tamil Nadu), Sanjeev Kumar alias Bablu Bhagat (Jharkhand), Sarita Jangid (Haryana), Kadaganchi Ramesh (Telangana), Vaibhav Panwar (Madhya Pradesh), and Bhim Kumar Sahu (Bihar). Under the organisational appointments, Radheshyam Yadav from Uttar Pradesh has been given charge as the national treasurer. Sanjay Kumar Gurjar and Dr Arun Yadav (both from Delhi) have been appointed as national office secretary and co-office secretary, respectively. Ajay Gupta from Bihar has been named the media coordinator for the Morcha. For digital communication, Parikshit Dagar (Delhi) has been appointed social media coordinator, with Pradeep Mahaur Soni (Madhya Pradesh) named co-coordinator. Prof. Pankaj Choudhary (Delhi) will head the policy and research wing as coordinator, assisted by co-coordinators Ashutosh Behera (Odisha) and Rahul Yadav (Uttar Pradesh). The party also notified the initial names of the national executive committee members, including Sanjeev Rangaiya (Andaman & Nicobar), Srinivas Rao Kantubukta (Andhra Pradesh), Rajiv Ranjan alias Vishal Yadav (Bihar), and Sanjeev Verma (Chandigarh).

headline: BJP Sounds Poll Bugle in Chandigarh; Nitin Nabin Calls for United Fight to Win Municipal Elections
content:
Chandigarh, November 22, 2026- BJP National President Shri Nitin Nabin today sounded the poll bugle for the upcoming Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections, calling upon party workers to set aside differences, strengthen the organisation at the booth level and ensure a decisive victory across the city.

Addressing a massive Booth Workers’ Conference at Ramlila Ground, Sector 27, amid enthusiastic slogans and a grand welcome by thousands of party workers, Shri Nabin said the BJP’s greatest strength was its dedicated cadre, which remained committed to public service throughout the year, not merely during elections.Describing Chandigarh as a “Mini India,” he said the enthusiastic participation of people from different communities reflected the city’s spirit of unity and social harmony. Referring to his association with Patna, the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, he said Chandigarh presented a remarkable example of India’s cultural diversity.Launching a sharp attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Shri Nabin alleged that certain opposition leaders enjoyed the benefits of this country but travelled abroad to malign India’s image.Taking a dig at Rahul Gandhi’s challenge to debate Prime Minister Narendra Modi, he remarked that even a BJP mandal president was capable of countering his arguments.Rejecting allegations of “vote theft,” Shri Nabin said the opposition had lost its political ground and was resorting to baseless accusations to conceal its failures.Targeting the Aam Aadmi Party, he said that after its defeat in Delhi, the BJP would work towards defeating AAP in Chandigarh and subsequently in Punjab. He also cautioned against what he described as the threat of urban Naxalism to society and democratic institutions.Highlighting the achievements of the Narendra Modi Government, Shri Nabin said India had emerged as the world’s third-largest economic power under the Prime Minister’s leadership. He cited Direct Benefit Transfer, the growth of over two lakh startups and India’s indigenous COVID-19 vaccines as examples of the government’s achievements.He said the government was committed to women’s empowerment through initiatives such as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.Announcing that the BJP’s manifesto for the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections would be prepared with public participation, Shri Nabin said suggestions from residents would be incorporated to address the needs and aspirations of every section of society.He urged workers to learn from the experiences of the 2024 elections, overcome internal differences and work unitedly to ensure the lotus blooms across Chandigarh.Earlier, Chandigarh BJP President Shri Jatinder Pal Malhotra welcomed the National President and said that winning elections through dedicated public service was the foremost responsibility of every party worker.Highlighting the BJP’s development initiatives, Shri Malhotra described the decision to provide ownership rights to approximately 50,000 families in Chandigarh as a historic achievement that would bring long-awaited relief and security to thousands of residents.He said the BJP had consistently worked for the welfare of economically weaker sections, traders, middle-class families and other residents while prioritising the city’s overall development.Expressing confidence in the party’s organisational strength, he called upon workers to reach every household with the achievements of the Central Government and the Chandigarh Administration.The conference was attended by Election In-charge Shri Satish Upadhyay, Chandigarh BJP In-charge Shri Mohinder Pandey, former BJP Presidents Shri Sanjay Tandon and Shri Arun Sood, former MP Shri Satya Pal Jain, Mayor Shri Saurabh Joshi, Senior Deputy Mayor Shri Jasmanpreet Singh, Deputy Mayor Shri Suman, district and morcha presidents, senior party leaders and thousands of booth-level workers.The conference concluded with workers resolving to strengthen the party at every booth and secure a decisive victory in the forthcoming Municipal Corporation

headline: Akalis play hardball with BJP, Mayawati seeks Amritpal pact
content: CHANDIGARH: As winter sets in, the Punjab assembly poll scene is hotting up, with talks for alliances gathering momentum. Even as bargaining for seats has delayed announcement of a re-alliance between the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the BSP is exploring a tie-up with the Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De) led by jailed Khadoor Sahib MP Amritpal Singh.Sources in both the BJP and SAD said an alliance has been formalised barring differences on the number of seats each party will contest. The BJP wants to contest around 55 seats but the SAD is likely to give them around 45.“The BJP has made it known that it will not play the role of a junior partner. The party wants a larger share in rural and reserved seats to move beyond its urban-centric image. The SAD, however, wants to protect its traditional strongholds,” a source privy to the matter said, adding that both the parties are staking claim to around a dozen seats.BJP sources said state party chief Kewal Singh Dhillon, and general secretary (organisation) Manthri Srinivasulu, among others, are not in favour of an alliance. But former Punjab BJP chief Sunil Jakhar, national vice president Manpreet Singh Badal and former CM Capt Amarinder Singh pitch for a tie-up..The BSP is exploring an alliance with Amritpal’s party, subject to approval from BSP supremo Mayawati. A BSP leader said, “An alliance with a regional party in Punjab will help the BSP regain its political relevance in the state and bolster its poll prospects. An alliance can offer a route to reclaim lost ground among the scheduled caste vote bank, which accounts for nearly 32% of the state’s population.”The proposed alliance could mark a departure from Mayawati’s announcement in August that the BSP would contest Punjab polls on its own. It is learnt that last week, BSP’s Punjab president Avtar Singh Karimpuri met Mayawati to seek her approval for an alliance with Amritpal’s party.Waris Punjab De leader Manpreet Singh Ayali shared, “Talks are currently under way on seat-sharing with the BSP. We are hopeful of finalising the arrangement within the next two weeks.”.Punjab MP Amritpal Singh gets parole to attend grandmother’s cremation

headline: Indian-origin Navdeep Bains elected as Ontario Liberal party leader; pledges to rebuild for next election
content: CHANDIGARH: Former Canadian minister of Indian origin hailing from Punjab, Navdeep Singh Bain, has been elected as the new leader of the Liberal Party in Ontario, pledging to focus on getting the party in shape for the next election. By winning the Liberal party leadership, Bains has become only the second turbaned Sikh to lead any federal or provincial party in Canada. Before him, Jagmeet Singh headed the New Democratic Party from 2017 to 2025.The 49-year-old Bains was born in Toronto in June 1977, but his family hailed from Mahilpur in Hoshiarpur district of Punjab got 50.3 percent of the vote on the third and final ballot at the party's leadership convention.Bains defeated Lee Fairclough in the third round of the election as leader of the Ontario Liberal Party by getting 50.3 percent of the votes against 49.7 percent votes by Lee out of 20, 510 cast votes. In the first round, he got 44.1 percent of the votes against 33.7 percent for Fairclough and in the second ballot he got 46.1 percent against 38.2 percent of Fairclough."This may be the end of a leadership race, ladies and gentlemen, but this is just the beginning of our campaign to replace Doug Ford and the (Progressive) Conservative Party of Ontario," he said.Bains has been one of the biggest supporters of former Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. The Conservative Party has been in power in the province since 2018. He was elected yesterday evening and replaced Bonnie Crombie, who had left the party leadership earlier this year.Before entering politics, Bains was a senior financial analyst at Ford Motor Company. After leaving parliament in 2021, he became an executive who remained one of the longest serving ministers of innovation, science and industry in Justin Trudeau-led the federal government of Canada from 2015 to 2021 and introduced the most comprehensive innovation and skills plan in over three decades. He had started his political career by winning the first election from Mississauga-Brampton South in 2004.Bains has been elected as party leader only a day after two Punjab-origin lawmakers were made ministers in the British Columbia provincial government, apart from four other Punjab-origin members as parliamentary secretaries..The provincial Liberal Party has been without a long-term leader since Bonnie Crombie's resignation in January. Bains becomes the party's third leader since former premier Kathleen Wynne resigned following the party's sweeping 2018 election defeat.The province's premier (Ford) congratulated Bains on the win in a post to social media platform X. "Ontario families are counting on us to work collaboratively and put the province over party so we can stand up to tariffs, protect workers and make life more affordable," Ford said."I look forward to continuing that work," Bains said. He is likely to face several hurdles, including not having a seat in the legislature. He suggested on Saturday that he would seek a seat, but did not say where or when. "I'll definitely be running, and the determination around the exact location will be made at the appropriate time," he said.Bains is now expected to shepherd the party into the next election, which may not come until 2030. He spoke in his victory speech about his family, in particular his parents, who moved to Ontario 50 years ago.His dad learned cabinet-making as a trade and his mother worked the night shift at a factory, he said. This province provided opportunities for his parents and for himself, Bains said, and he worries that those same opportunities are no longer available."One in four people in my community of Mississauga visit the food bank, who have a job, who have multiple jobs, who play by the rules and are falling further and further behind. The reason why that is, is because Doug Ford and the Conservatives have abandoned the fight, they are not in it for the people," he said..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: 2027 Punjab Polls: Congress first list of 45 names likely by December first week
content: CHANDIGARH: The first list of Congress for the 2027 Punjab Assembly Elections is likely to be released by the first week of December is which tentatively they might be names of around 45 prospective candidates, it is likely to be a mix of first timers, youth, women and experienced leaders with only one condition. "winnability’’.Sources privy to the developments in the grand old party said that the first list of the candidates to be released is under consideration and is likely tobe announced by the first week of December and in that youth have been given representation in infuses fresh blood into the party and not only that, it is also new. faces is likely to figure as first time candidates. "The number of women candidates contesting these upcoming elections on the party ticket are likely to be double then last time, as it is thought to give more tickets to ladies this time," said a senior party leader.On the issue of the one-family-one ticket norm, the party has been following the past polls are likely to stick to it and, in the rarest case, only two members from one family might be given a ticket. At the same time, experienced candidates are likely to be given preference. "After the first list is declared the remaining candidates are likely to be declared by the end of December," said the party.leader.It is learnt that the party is considering the names of 40 to 50 potential candidates. particularly in assembly segments where the leadership wants to identify strong contenders, as the party is conducting surveys across the state to assess the political standing and public support of prospective candidates. The team of leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, is reportedly involved in this. exercise collecting feedback about the prospective candidates and their prospects.This time, instead of rushing into ticket distribution, the Congress is focusing on identifying strong candidates in advance and preparing for the election.Thus surveys are being conducted at two levels in all the 117 assemblies.constituencies and seeking feedback from voters, local workers and otherstakeholders to assess the prospects of potential candidates. One by Rahul Gandhi's team and the other by the Punjab Congress on its own. .Most of the work on both surveys has been completed. Their findings could also be a key factor in candidate selection. as this exercise will provide the leadership with constituency-wise inputs before it takes a final call on nominations.A party leader said that most of the leaders whose names were likely to be cleared in the first list wanted the announcement to be delayed, as an early announcement would stretch their campaign period.Punjab Congress President Pargat Singh said the criteria for party tickets would not be limited to winnability alone, as the party has conducted more than 2000 sample surveys and this process is still going on. The candidates with a good public image, strong character and commitment to society should be given opportunities strictly on merit."Leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has a clear vision for candidates with a clean image, a strong character. and commitment towards society should be given opportunities strictly on merit," he said.The first meeting of the 42-member State Election Committee, headed by the State Congress President Pargat Singh, is scheduled for November 24 in which it will discuss potential candidates from various assembly constituencies, their political activism, regional influence, organizational affiliations, and election winning prospects.Then an attempt will be made to reach a consensus on the names of strong contenders which will be sent to the three-member screening committee headed by Dr Sirivella Prasad, AICC in-charge for Maharashtra, with Sachin Sawant, AICC national secretary, and Nivedith Alva, in-charge of Tamil Nadu, as its members, where the final decision will be made after shortlisting by the Congress high command.The AICC general secretary in charge of Punjab, Sachin Pilot; Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee president Pargat Singh; Leader of the Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa; and AICC secretaries attached to the general secretary in charge will be its ex officio members.While Pargat Singh had earlier questioned the rigid application of the ‘one family, One ticket’ formula, saying a candidate’s winnability should matter more than family background.He pointed out that a situation could arise where one family member was already an MP while another sought an Assembly ticket. Such cases, he said, should not face a blanket restriction. Every candidate should be assessed individually, as there is no fixed yardstick.The debate gained momentum after former PPCC chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring backed the rule, arguing that ordinary party workers also deserved opportunities instead of senior leaders seeking tickets for relatives..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: NEWS RECEIVED FROM PB BJP PRINT MEDIA AT CHANDIGARH
content:
BJP to Seek Public Suggestions for Election Manifesto Through 3 Helplines

Chandigarh, November 22:The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Punjab has launched an extensive public suggestion campaign to prepare its vision document for the 2027 Assembly elections. Punjab BJP State President Kewal Singh Dhillon formally launched the campaign by unveiling three phone numbers and a QR code in the presence of Punjab BJP affairs in-charge Dr Satish Poonia, Manifesto Committee Chairman Avinash Rai Khanna and other committee members.

Addressing the media at the party’s state office, Kewal Singh Dhillon said that the only solution to Punjab’s crisis of drugs, gangsterism, corruption and debt is a BJP double-engine government. When the Central and State governments work with the same vision, the state will progress at a pace of doubling its growth by the day. He said that with this vision, Punjab BJP is releasing helpline numbers and a QR code for its website so that every citizen of Punjab could directly connect with the party and share their suggestions and views. BJP Punjab will contest the elections on the issues of de-addiction and development. Our sole agenda is the development of Punjab, making the state drug-free, securing the future of its youth and ensuring prosperity for Punjab.

Manifesto Committee member and National Vice-President Manpreet Singh Badal, Advocate HS Phoolka, Rajya Sabha MP Rajinder Gupta, former state president Manoranjan Kalia, former MLA Ashwani Sekhri, former Union Minister Som Parkash, Rana Gurmeet Singh Sodhi, Parampal Kaur and State Media Head Vineet Joshi were also present On the occasion .

Three Phone Numbers and QR Code Issued for Public SuggestionsAddressing the media, Avinash Rai Khanna said that the party have issued three phone numbers and a QR code to collect suggestions from the public. The first number, 0797-194-3333, can be called directly to submit suggestions. The second number, 991-300-2027, is meant for missed calls, following which the party office will call the person back to collect their suggestions. The third number, 750-856-0065, can be used to send suggestions through WhatsApp messages. People can also submit their suggestions through the QR code.

Avinash Rai Khanna said that vans would be deployed across Punjab to collect suggestions from the public. These vans will carry information about the achievements of the Modi government and will also have suggestion boxes where people can submit their ideas. A committee headed by Manpreet Singh Badal will examine these suggestions and incorporate them into the vision document.

headline: Young skaters of AKSIPS-41 Smart School, Chandigarh, deliver impressive performances
content: Young skaters of AKSIPS-41 Smart School, Chandigarh, delivered impressive performances at various skating championships. Harjap Singh and Garv Rai won gold, silver and bronze medals at the Chandigarh State-Level and Chandigarh 2 State-Level Skating Championships. They also secured a silver medal at the inter-state school skating championship. Adiraj Rai of Class II won silver in the 100-metre event and bronze in the 1,000-metre event at the CBSE North Zone Skating Championship held in Gurugram. Adding to the school's medal tally, Rihansh Sharma of Class II-C clinched bronze medals at the 48th Chandigarh State Roller Skating Championship 2026. The school management congratulated the young achievers, their parents and coaches for their dedication and hard work, wishing them continued success in future competitions.

headline: Have a say in 2027 Punjab Assembly polls? BJP launches phone lines, QR code to seek ideas
content: <p>Chandigarh: The <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/bjp">Punjab BJP</a> on Sunday launched three phone numbers to invite suggestions from people across the state for preparing what it described as a “people’s manifesto” for the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/assembly-elections">2027 Assembly elections</a>.</p>.<p>Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon said the numbers were 07971943333, 9913002027 and 7508560065.</p>.<p>A QR code has also been launched to seek suggestions from people for the party’s manifesto, he said.</p>.<p>“We will welcome suggestions from every section and thereafter the poll manifesto will be prepared. It will be a people’s manifesto,” Dhillon told reporters here.</p>.<p>“We have only one agenda, which is Punjab’s progress and development. It will be a manifesto for every Punjabi,” he said.</p>.<p>The party will also send vans to villages and cities to collect suggestions from people for the manifesto, Dhillon said.</p>.Setback to Punjab Congress as ex-MLA, 2027 manifesto panel co-head Hardial Singh Kamboj joins BJP.<p>Targeting the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/aap">AAP government</a> over issues such as law and order, drug menace, gangsterism and rising debt, he accused it of having “destroyed Punjab” during its tenure.</p>.<p>He claimed that Punjab had lagged behind in terms of development and that the AAP government had failed to ensure that funds sent by the Centre reached the people of the state.</p>.<p>The Punjab BJP chief also claimed that the state’s outstanding debt had nearly doubled from Rs 2.82 lakh crore under the AAP government.</p>.<p>Party’s Punjab in-charge Satish Poonia and senior leaders Manpreet Singh Badal, Som Parkash, H S Phoolka, Manoranjan Kalia, Ashwani Sekhri, Parampal Kaur and Rana Gurmit Singh Sodhi were present on the occasion. </p>

headline: Delhi meets air quality targets but lags on waste processing, parking infrastructure: CAQM
content: Delhi has met its targets for installing continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations and expanding construction and demolition (C&D) waste processing capacity, but its performance remains uneven across several pollution-control measures, according to the State Action Plan 2026 report card, which assesses progress up to October 31.The report card from CAQM presents a mixed picture of pollution-control efforts across Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, with significant gaps in waste management, industrial inspections, road dust mitigation and transport infrastructure.Delhi has achieved its target of 19 continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations and established 1,000 tonnes per day of C&D waste processing capacity against the annual target. However, the utilisation of processed construction waste remains poor. Government agencies have taken up only 21 per cent of their targeted offtake, while private agencies have achieved 26 per cent.The city's performance on municipal solid waste management is particularly concerning. Against a target of augmenting two processing plants, Delhi reported no achievement by October-end. It also recorded zero progress against its targeted addition of 650 tonnes per day in processing capacity.Legacy waste clearance at the three major landfill sites remains incomplete. Okhla has achieved 67 per cent of its target, Bhalswa 57 per cent and Ghazipur 42 per cent, leaving substantial quantities of waste to be processed.The gaps are equally visible in transport infrastructure. Delhi has completed only 15 of the targeted 266 parking lots, an achievement of just 6 per cent. It has also added only one medium-sized mechanised road sweeping machine against a target of 57.On public transport, the city has added 1,703 buses against a target of 2,395, achieving 71 per cent. However, it has exceeded its target for electric vehicle charging stations, reporting 6,000 against the planned 5,000.The report also records 1,609 industrial inspections against a target of 979, while installations of online continuous emission monitoring systems and air pollution control devices have reached their respective targets.Across the four states, the report highlights broader implementation failures. None has commissioned a green crematorium against a combined target of 421. Industrial inspections in Haryana and Rajasthan stand at just 5 per cent and 2 per cent of their respective targets.The figures underline a wider challenge: meeting infrastructure targets in selected categories has not translated into comparable progress across the range of measures required to address pollution.

headline: Data gives clearer picture as government claims Delhi just saw cleanest air in 10 years
content: Even as the Delhi government has claimed that the Capital recorded its cleanest air in a decade for the months of October and November, the official data presents a clearer picture. While October indeed registered the best air quality index (AQI) in 10 years, an analysis of daily AQI data shows that pollution levels in the run-up to and during Diwali were among the highest in the period before a sharp improvement around mid-November, aided by favourable weather. The seven days preceding Diwali averaged an AQI of 347.4, the third-highest for the corresponding period in a decade, behind 2020 (399 AQI) and 2023 (375.7). Six of those seven days recorded AQI levels above 300. November 8, when Diwali was celebrated, and the next seven days averaged an AQI of 346, making it the sixth most polluted Diwali week in the 10-year period. Earlier years such as 2021 (410.7 AQI), 2019 (402.4) and 2018 (386.9) recorded higher averages, while 2020 (290.1) and 2025 (318.6) were cleaner, an analysis of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data shows. Six of the seven days during the Diwali week this year recorded AQI levels above 300. Air quality improved markedly in the following week, which averaged an AQI of 259.4, the lowest post-Diwali weekly average in the ten-year period. Daily AQI values stayed between 204 and 290, making 2026 the only year in the dataset in which AQI on every day of the post-Diwali week remained below 300. This was in sharp contrast to previous years when post-Diwali pollution remained considerably higher. The corresponding seven-day averages stood at 401.3 in 2022, 397.1 in 2021 and 372.7 in 2023. Favourable weather The sharp mid-November improvement coincided with favourable meteorological conditions, including sustained strong winds of up to around 15 kmph. Data from the India Meteorological Department and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology showed an increased role of weather conditions in the improvement, including a higher ventilation index coupled with better wind speed in mid-November. Ventilation index refers to the potential of the atmosphere to disperse airborne pollutants, depending on average wind speed and mixing depth — vertical height of the lowest layer of the atmosphere where the pollutants can disperse freely. Meanwhile, October this year recorded an average AQI of 165.6, the lowest average for the month over the last 10 years. Earlier, it was in 2021 that the city had recorded a lower October average. September, however, was not the cleanest on record. With an average AQI of 101.5, this year saw the third-cleanest September in the 10-year period after 2021 (78.4) and 2019 (98.1). Together, AQI in September and October this year averaged at 134.1, making this the second-cleanest start to the post-monsoon season after 2021 when the corresponding average was 126.6. This month, however, AQI data up to Saturday shows an average AQI of 317.6, the lowest for the corresponding period in the available 10-year record. But this average masks considerable fluctuations in pollution levels through the month. Daily AQI values ranged between 204 and 382, with the city recording levels between 369 and 382 from November 4 to 8, reflecting several days of severe and near-severe pollution.

headline: Opposition questions US policy after report flags China’s support to Pakistan during Op Sindoor
content: NEW DELHI: Political reactions have poured in after a US congressional commission flagged China’s military support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor.The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission said China’s military support for Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict complicated India’s operational planning and tied down its military resources, without Beijing directly entering the fighting.The commission, established by the US Congress in 2000, said China views India as a potential competitor and is working to constrain its rise. It warned that Beijing’s growing military partnership with Pakistan has made a possible two-front conflict a greater concern for New Delhi.“China understands this, and it is actively working to suppress India’s rise across multiple domains,” the report said.“May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without Beijing entering the fighting directly, adding to India’s concerns about how a future conflict with Pakistan could develop,” the report added.The assessment by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC) has drawn reactions from political leaders, with Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi saying the findings were unsurprising, while Congress leader Shama Mohamed questioned Washington’s own policy towards India and Pakistan.Reacting to the report, Chaturvedi said China had itself acknowledged that Pakistan was using Chinese-supplied equipment and defence systems during the operation.She said successive Indian governments, regardless of political affiliation, had sought to manage national security concerns in their dealings with China, and that the report served as another reminder for India to remain cautious.Chaturvedi said India-China trade ties were important, but warned that the money generated through trade could also be used by Beijing in ways that ran counter to India’s national interests.Congress leader Shama Mohamed said China’s support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor was already known and pointed to unresolved tensions along the India-China border, saying the two countries had not returned to the pre-2020 status quo.Mohamed also questioned the US approach towards India, citing the tariff dispute, pressure over Russian oil purchases and President Donald Trump’s meeting with Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir at the White House.“If the US needs India, it has to work with India and keep Pakistan at a distance,” she said, adding that Washington should take India’s security concerns into account while dealing with the region.She also accused the Indian government of failing to prevent China’s growing presence along the border, including in areas near Arunachal Pradesh.Defence expert says report raises questions for WashingtonBrigadier Hemant Mahajan (retd) said the report was not a major revelation but raised questions about what Washington knew, what it would do in response and how its claims could be independently verified.Mahajan alleged that Chinese support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor extended beyond supplying weapons and included intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, repairs and technical assistance. He claimed that Chinese satellite capabilities and equipment had been used to support Pakistan’s military preparedness.He also alleged that China had provided Pakistan with substantial military equipment and helped repair platforms that had been out of service before the operation. Mahajan said the support had stopped short of China directly joining the conflict.However, he argued that the performance of Chinese-made weapons during the conflict had raised questions about their effectiveness, and said Indian-made systems had performed better. These assessments were his own.Mahajan further questioned whether the US report would lead to any change in Washington’s policy towards China and Pakistan, saying the broader strategic implications of Beijing’s military assistance extended beyond South Asia.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Infrastructure push has narrowed Northeast-Delhi gap, says Amit Shah | India News
content: The Northeast, particularly Arunachal Pradesh, witnessed a major transformation in connectivity, infrastructure and economic development over the past 12 years under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, significantly narrowing the gap between the region and the national capital, Union home minister Amit Shah said on Sunday.Addressing the ‘Sahakarita Samaroh’ at the Dorjee Khandu Convention Hall here, Shah said the region had witnessed unprecedented infrastructure expansion, with improved road, rail and air connectivity bringing northeastern states closer to the country’s development mainstream.He asserted that the Modi government placed the Northeast at the forefront of its development agenda, focusing on infrastructure, education, employment, industrial growth and tourism.Taking a swipe at the Congress, Shah accused the previous UPA government of neglecting Arunachal Pradesh and providing inadequate financial assistance during its tenure. Also Read | 'No local terrorist in Kashmir anymore': Amit Shah reiterates days after LeT's Lateef Bhat killedHe claimed that central assistance to the state had increased from ₹33,530 crore during 2004-2014 under the UPA government to ₹1,64,664 crore between 2014 and 2024 under the NDA. Tax devolution to Arunachal had increased fourfold, while grants had risen 18-fold, he added. The state’s annual budget had also expanded from ₹12,000 crore to ₹36,000 crore, reflecting accelerated development.Highlighting the Vibrant Villages Programme, Shah said Modi had transformed the perception of border settlements by describing them as the country’s “first villages” rather than the last. Improved infrastructure, electricity, schools and livelihood opportunities had encouraged reverse migration, with residents returning to nearly 40 border villages in Arunachal Pradesh, he claimed.Referring to major infrastructure projects, Shah highlighted the 2,880-MW Dibang hydropower project, involving an investment of approximately ₹32,000 crore, the Balipara-Charduar-Tawang road, the Nechiphu tunnel and other strategic connectivity initiatives.He also said he had discussed the possibility of introducing a second daily flight between Itanagar and New Delhi with an airline following a request from chief minister Pema Khandu.During the programme, Shah launched development projects worth approximately ₹5,610 crore. These included Mission Shikshit Arunachal Phase II, with an allocation of ₹1,500 crore; power and rural road development programmes worth ₹2,000 crore each; and 199 projects under the Vibrant Villages Programme worth ₹110.95 crore across 11 border districts.He also unveiled the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision Document 2047, aimed at strengthening rural livelihoods and promoting economic self-reliance.Describing cooperatives as crucial to Arunachal’s economic future, Shah said the state was poised for a new era of rural prosperity, particularly benefiting farmers, youth and women.He said more than 50,000 people were associated with 185 primary agricultural credit societies, 52 dairy cooperatives and 43 fish farms.Shah urged the state government to prepare a comprehensive dairy development roadmap in collaboration with the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), assuring procurement support from Amul and NDDB.He also highlighted women-led cooperatives supplying locally produced vegetables, milk, eggs and agricultural commodities to the Army and Indo-Tibetan Border Police, reducing dependence on supplies from neighbouring Assam.The minister suggested promoting fisheries in hydropower reservoirs to generate additional employment and strengthen the rural economy.Listing achievements under central welfare schemes, Shah said 1.28 lakh farmers had benefited from PM-KISAN, 2.30 lakh households had received tap water connections, 1.90 lakh people had obtained health coverage of up to ₹5 lakh, and around 45,000 beneficiaries had received housing assistance.Chief minister Pema Khandu said around 1,100 cooperative societies were contributing to the state’s rural economy and that the newly launched projects would accelerate inclusive and balanced development.Union minister Kiren Rijiju stressed technological advancement and investment, while deputy chief minister Chowna Mein called for strengthening cooperative institutions to make them financially sustainable.On the occasion, Shah inaugurated a foodgrain warehouse at Raga LAMPS, launched an e-commerce platform for Arunachal State Rural Livelihoods Mission products and flagged off a mobile medical unit for remote areas. He also inaugurated the SARAS Mela and felicitated four outstanding cooperative institutions for their contributions to rural development.Shah, who arrived in Arunachal on Friday for a three-day visit, had earlier reviewed development projects and security-related matters in the state.

headline: CAQM sets 15-20% pollution reduction target for Delhi-NCR in 2027, seeks district-wise action plans | Latest News Delhi
content: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has told Delhi and NCR states to cut annual average air pollution by 15-20% in 2027 from 2026 levels. For the first time, it has asked for action plans at the district level, with an officer listed by name for carrying out and monitoring every measure.The commission has not clarified in the statement how a district’s pollution will be measured, how it will separate the effect of weather from the effect of the measures, or what happens to an officer whose district misses its target.In a letter to the governments of Delhi and NCR states on November 20, CAQM asked for district-level plans in addition to the existing state and municipal plans. The plans must set measurable targets, timelines and monitoring parameters for vehicular emissions, road dust, industrial pollution, construction and demolition, municipal waste, crop residue burning, diesel generator sets, crematoria and other local sources.Also read: Delhi air quality remains poor at AQI 278 as calm winds hamper pollutant dispersalStates asked to submit plans by December 5States must name, for every measure, the department or agency responsible, along with the name, designation and contact details of the officer in charge of carrying it out and monitoring it.The commission has set a minimum target of a 15% cut in annual average AQI, PM2.5 and PM10 levels from 2026, and asked states and agencies to aim for up to 20%. The plans must be submitted through CAQM’s online portal by December 5. The commission said it would send more action points for the plans, and that measures by urban development authorities would go into municipal corporation plans.A senior Delhi government official said the government expects more clarity on preparing the plan after CAQM holds a meeting with district magistrates on November 23. “The communication was issued on Friday, and we will follow the directions issued by CAQM,” the official said, asking not to be named.Also read: Report links cloud-seeding to AQI gain in Delhi; but western disturbance may have had a roleThe official said district-level plans were more relevant for the other NCR states, because pollution sources are largely similar across Delhi’s districts, including stubble burning, road dust and vehicle emissions.“However, pollution sources vary across districts in other states. While one district may be grappling with industrial pollution, another may face dust pollution as a major challenge,” the official said.CAQM said it had regularly reviewed the 2026 plans to monitor implementation and identify gaps. It said the 2027 effort would follow an “airshed approach”, with measures coordinated across administrative boundaries and pollution sources.Unclear how district-wise pollution reductions will be measuredA district’s annual average depends on how many monitoring stations it has and where they are, and a single station records the air at only one location. CAQM has not said which readings it will use to judge whether a district met its target.Pollution also moves across district lines. Officers can act only on emissions within their own district, but the target is set on pollution in the air, and those also depend on what blows in from elsewhere. CAQM describes its approach as covering the whole airshed, yet it has fixed accountability district by district. Annual averages also change with wind, rain and how high pollution can mix into the atmosphere, all of which vary from year to year. The commission has not said how it will tell a cut that came from the measures apart from one that came from cleaner weather.District officials would need to know how much their district emits, and from which sources, to work out how much any measure would cut. The 15% minimum applies to every district whatever its starting level or mix of sources, and CAQM has not said how it arrived at the 15% and 21% figures.Experts flag need for emission data and public monitoringSunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at the think tank Envirocatalysts, called the direction a significant step because it is the first time plans will be drawn up at the district level as well as the state and municipal levels. “Every action will need measurable targets, timelines and a named nodal officer. That sets out clearly where each action applies, which sector it covers and who is responsible for it. The focus on cutting emissions at the source is exactly what NCR and the country needs,” he said.He said the plan would have to work in practice, and district authorities would need up-to-date emission inventories and “the skills and resources to update those inventories every quarter.” He said making the data public would matter just as much: “That means current emission loads, district-wise inventories by sector, and progress towards the 15–20% reduction target. Public data is what will ensure these steps are carried out on the ground.”Also read: 4th day of ‘poor’ air, Delhi CM says negligence won’t be toleratedWeather on SaturdayDelhi’s air quality stayed “poor” for a seventh day Saturday, with 24-hour average AQI at 265—five points better than Friday, as per CPCB. Thirteen of 57 monitoring stations reported “very poor” air. Vehicles contributed 33.1% of the pollution, followed by secondary organic aerosols (16.5%) and biomass burning (13.9%). According to AQEWS forecast, Delhi will continue to see “poor” air.The maximum temperature was 27.6°C on Saturday while minimum was at 12.2°C, according to IMD.

headline: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies of cardiac arrest in Delhi
content: <p>Mumbai: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute, who was elected to the Upper House earlier this year, died following a cardiac arrest at a hospital in New Delhi, family sources said on Sunday.</p>.<p>He was 72.</p>.<p>Wadkute was admitted to AIIMS in New Delhi on November 20 after complaining of a cough. He suffered a heart attack around 6 pm on Saturday and died during treatment around 11.45 pm, they said.</p>.Maharashtra FDA suspends licences of Amazon, BigBasket dark stores in Pune over food safety violations.<p>Hailing from Parbhani in <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/maharashtra">Maharashtra</a>'s Marathwada region, Wadkute was elected to the Rajya Sabha in April this year and had previously served as a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) from June 2014 to October 2019.</p>.<p>Condoling the demise of the senior leader, Maharashtra Chief Minister <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/devendra-fadnavis">Devendra Fadnavis</a> said his death was the loss of a simple and dedicated personality in politics who was deeply concerned about grassroots welfare.</p>.<p>Fadnavis noted that Wadkute had held several organisational responsibilities in the BJP in Hingoli district and worked extensively for the Dhangar community.</p>.<p>He also served as chairman of the Sheep and Goat Development Corporation and made his mark in the cooperative sector, the chief minister added.</p>.Maharashtra government forms CM-led panel to suggest names of metro stations in Mumbai, Pune and Nagpur.<p>Vice President and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan expressed grief over Wadkute's passing, saying his contributions to public life and service to the people will always be remembered.</p>.<p>Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said, "The passing of Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute ji is deeply saddening. In this hour of grief, my heartfelt condolences are with the bereaved family. May the departed soul rest in peace and may the family find the strength to bear this immense loss."</p>.<p>Maharashtra Assembly Speaker Rahul Narwekar, in a post on X, said, "The news of the tragic passing of Hon. Ramraoji Vadkute, Member of the Rajya Sabha, in Delhi following a severe heart attack is deeply painful and heartbreaking. At this difficult time, we share in the grief of the Vadkute family." </p>

headline: Delhi air pollution: CAQM directs district-level action plans for 2027 to reduce AQI by 15-20%
content: <p>Amid rising <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/air-pollution">air pollution</a> in Delhi, the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has asked the capital city and NCR states to prepare district-level action plans for 2027. </p>.<p>The action plan for 2027 will focus on the overall reduction of annual air <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/opinion/editorial/aqi-gaps-raise-public-health-concerns-4217832">pollution levels</a> (AQI, PM2.5 and PM10) by 15 per cent and 20 per cent as compared to 2026, the Commission mentioned in its order.</p>.<p>This is the first time that CAQM has asked the Delhi government to include district-level action plans in measures to tackle air pollution in the city. The district-level attention to the situation will help facilitate focused implementation and effective monitoring of pollution measures at the grassroots. </p>.Govt extends pollution certificate renewal intervals for newer BS-VI vehicles.<p>The order released on November 20, will also help identify implementation gaps and enable timely corrective action, with defined accountability, officials said.</p>.<p>"Dealing with air pollution requires sustained and concerted efforts based on the airshed approach. For 2027, annual action plans shall also be prepared at the district level, in addition to the state and municipal corporation levels," the CAQM said.</p>.<p>The action plan for next year will have defined sector-wise actions with achievable targets, the CAQM order stated, with timelines and monitoring parameters.</p>.<p>A focused approach will be in place across the major pollution sources including a list of strong probable's like vehicles, road dust, industrial emissions, construction and demolition drives, solid waste, crop residues, diesel generator sets, crematoria, and other local sources.</p>.50 years of air pollution studies show need for multi-pollutant approach.<p>Officials responsible for achieving the prescribed targets will be specifically identified by their names and designations, thereby establishing clear ownership, responsibility and accountability for implementation and outcomes, the CAQM said.</p>.<p>"These significant additions to the state action plans are of critical importance in advancing the Commission's mandate of ensuring sustained improvement in air quality and making the air breathable for citizens across Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas," the CAQM said.</p><p>(With inputs from agencies)</p>

headline: 'Two rulers, one fort': Pakistan minister finds a shared history in Delhi's Purana Qila
content: Pakistan Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik on Saturday invoked Mughal Emperor Humayun and Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri while describing Delhi's Purana Qila as a symbol of the multiple layers of history and civilisational connections.Addressing the thematic session on 'Civilisational and Cultural Expressions' at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, Malik said the fort, associated with both rulers, represented the coming together of different historical identities."This Qila, where we are sitting, is in itself a story. A fort whose foundation was laid by Humayun, who had a descent from the Timurid dynasty linkage and came from Central Asia. Sher Shah Suri further built on it, who was an Afghan. One wall, two rivals, meaning two rulers and one fort, meaning two layers and one trench," he said.Malik's office shared a video of his remarks on X, describing the Qila as a "story".. India is hosting the three-day forum at the historic Purana Qila from November 20 to 22. The event was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday in the presence of delegates from various Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member countries, including Pakistan.Malik, who is visiting India for the first time since the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, said dialogue was possible only between distinct identities and diverse civilisations."Dialogue is between distinct identities, and between diversity, and we have come here for that dialogue only," he said, emphasising the importance of the free exchange of ideas and cultural identities.Referring to the meaning of the word 'dialogue' in Greek, Malik said 'dia' meant through and 'logos' meant ideas. He described dialogue as the free flow of ideas across civilisations and said embracing diversity required both wisdom and courage..‘All of our relationships will improve’: Pakistan minister signals hope for better ties with India.The session was chaired by Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, who said shared cultural heritage was a strong bridge connecting SCO nations. Historical links, he said, had helped bring countries closer and offered significant scope for cultural cooperation, mutual understanding and friendship."Our civilisations are not merely legacies of the past, but living traditions whose knowledge continues to illuminate our present and inspire future generations," Shekhawat said.He expressed confidence that the forum would serve as a platform for strengthening cultural ties and fostering civilisational understanding among SCO member states.India is using the historic site to showcase its civilisational heritage and the multiple layers of history spanning thousands of years. A special exhibition, 'Astitva -- The Essence of our Existence', traces Delhi's history through archaeological evidence dating from 1,200 BC to 1200 CE, including excavated remains, artefacts and architectural fragments.Delegates also visited the exhibition 'The Light and the Lotus: Relics of the Awakened One' at the Qila Rai Pithora cultural complex in south Delhi on Saturday.In his address on Friday, Modi described Purana Qila as an extraordinary heritage site, noting that scholars traced its history to the Mahabharata era.The fort, built on the site traditionally identified with Indraprastha, was developed by Humayun as part of his new capital, Dinpanah. Sher Shah Suri, who displaced Humayun, subsequently continued the construction.On Friday, Malik had said his visit to India was for discussions in a multilateral context. Asked whether the forum could help improve India-Pakistan relations, he said the discussions were taking place in a multilateral setting and stressed the role of culture in facilitating dialogue between the two countries.(With inputs from PTI).MEA says Indus Waters Treaty stance unchanged as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Punjab seeks refrigerated wagons on Vande Bharat, Shatabdi for farm, dairy produce | Hindustan Times
content: To take Punjab’s farm and dairy produce to markets across the country, the state government has proposed that the Railways introduce refrigerated wagons on Vande Bharat and other high-speed trains, enabling the faster, time-bound transport of perishable commodities.Ajit Balaji Joshi, secretary, taxation and cooperation department, Punjab, said, “Railways should bring special refrigerated wagons for transportation of perishable goods like milk, vegetables, and other crops to tap pan-India market. Punjab has unique milk products from Verka, like ‘rabri’ and ‘kheer’and Markfed ready-to-eat products, which are highly in demand in the country, but the state needs time-bound transportation of such items. Railways should bring wagons in high-speed trains like Vande Bharat and Shatabdi for time-bound deliveries, so that consumers get fresh vegetables, fruits, and milk items at far-away places.”He asked the Railways to introduce a mechanism and suitable wagons so that potato producers can use railway wagons to send their produce to different parts of the country.He was speaking at the ‘’Trade Meet 2026’ organised in Chandigarh by the Ahmedabad, Ambala, and Ferozepur Railway Divisions in association with the Central Warehousing Corporation to boost rail freight transportation and trade between Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana.He said there is an Agricultural Infrastructure Fund under the Union Agriculture Ministry, and the Railways and the Punjab government should bring projects for transporting produce from Punjab and Haryana to different parts of the country.He said that the Railways can help the state government curb tax evasion by directly transporting steel scrap from different seaports to Mandi Gobindgarh and Ludhiana.Rabindra Kumar Agarwal, chairman, Central Warehousing Corporation; Ved Prakash, divisional railway manager (DRM), Ahmedabad; Vinod Bhatia, DRM, Ambala; and Annu Tyagi, senior divisional commercial manager, Ahmedabad along with senior officials of Indian Railways and CWC, and representatives from the freight transportation and industrial sectors were present at the event.The officials said the main goal is to speed up trade between Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, promote rail-based freight transport, and lower logistics costs. Farmers, traders, rice mill operators, industrialists, exporters, importers, transporters, and logistics service providers were urged to use the railway freight corridors.Ved Prakash, DRM, Ahmedabad Division, said, “Railways is playing a crucial role in driving economic growth, supporting industrial expansion, creating new markets for agricultural products, and enhancing the global competitiveness of goods. Our objective is to reduce transportation costs for traders, provide farmers with access to larger markets, improve connectivity for industries, and ensure reliable logistics facilities for exporters”.He added, “We need two-way freight movement to reduce costs and improve railway efficiency. If freight trains transport rice, potatoes, foodgrains, and export containers from Punjab and Haryana to Gujarat, our endeavour should be to ensure that these trains carry imported timber, salt, fertilisers, industrial products, and import containers from Gujarat to North India on their return journey. This will reduce empty rake movement, improve wagon utilisation, and make freight transportation more cost competitive.”

headline: 'Acting like frustrated cat': Kangana Ranaut slams Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Indian economy
content: <p>BJP MP <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/kangana-ranaut">Kangana Ranaut </a>on Sunday slammed Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi saying he was acting like a "frustrated cat" during her visit to Taj Mahal, in Agra, Uttar Pradesh.</p><p>The Mandi MP's comments came as a response to Rahul Gandhi's remarks, during his recent visit to the United States, where he stated that India is "sitting on an economic disaster".</p><p>He had also warned that India risks getting into serious trouble if it continues on the current economic path.</p>.'India sitting on economic disaster,' says Rahul Gandhi in US; BJP terms him 'anti-India leader' who is 'hungry for power'.<p>Reacting to Gandhi's comments, Kangana, during a media interaction in Agra, told reporters that India is the fastest-growing economy in Asia and added that the congress leader was "behaving like a frustrated cat scratching a pole."</p><p>Kangana also took a dig at Gandhi's comments on Sunday that the RSS and BJP are "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists", accusing the Congress of opposing women's reservation rather than the "male-dominated BJP" (as described by Rahul Gandhi).</p>.'BJP, RSS are uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists,' says Rahul Gandhi as he shares Shiva-Parvati sculpture pic.<p>"If the BJP is male-dominated, why is it fighting for the Women's Reservation Bill? It is the Congress that is opposing the bill and preventing its implementation. The anti-women mindset is that of the Congress," Kangana said.</p><p>The actor-politician visited the Taj Mahal on Sunday and spent around an hour admiring the monument and posing for photographs and selfies. She visited the mausoleum around 3 pm, accompanied by family members and escorted by security.</p><p><em>(With PTI inputs)</em></p>

headline: Watch Kangana Ranaut's Agra visit: From praising Taj Mahal to calling Rahul Gandhi a ‘Khisiyaai Billi’ ov
content: AGRA: BJP MP and actor Kangana Ranaut visited the Taj Mahal in Agra on Sunday, praising the monument's artistic and historical significance before launching a sharp attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the Indian economy.Taking a dig at Rahul Gandhi, the Mandi MP compared him to a 'Khisiyaai Billi Khamba noche' and accused the Congress of opposing the Women's Reservation BillRanaut spent around an hour at the monument, admiring its marble architecture and posing for photographs and selfies.She arrived at the mausoleum around 3 pm, accompanied by family members and escorted by security. Her visit also drew the attention of tourists, several of whom gathered to catch a glimpse of her.Kangana praises taj mahalSpeaking about her visit, Ranaut described the Taj Mahal as a beautiful blend of art and history and said she was glad to have the opportunity to bring her family along."It is very beautiful; it has always been a wonderful confluence of art and history... Today I got the good fortune and opportunity to bring my family along. The arrangements are very good, and it is a matter of great pride for our country," she said.Kangana's jibe at Rahul GandhiAfter exploring the monument, Ranaut spoke to reporters about India's economic position, saying the country was among Asia's leading economies despite global challenges, including ongoing wars and an economic crisis."Look at the economy in Asia. India is currently among the leading economies. Despite the wars and the global economic crisis, you can see every day how our BJP government is absorbing and handling the situation. This is not something anyone needs to tell you; you can look at the data yourself. But Rahul Gandhi, as I always say, is like a 'Khisiyaai Billi Khamba noche'. The Opposition will keep doing that...." she said.Reacting to Rahul Gandhi's allegation that the RSS and BJP are "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists", Ranaut questioned the Congress's position on the Women's Reservation Bill and accused the party of having an anti-women mindset."If the BJP is male-dominated, why is it fighting for the Women's Reservation Bill? And if these people have greater sympathy for women, why are they not allowing the Women's Reservation Bill to be passed? It is only the Congress that has an anti-women mindset," she said.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Agra | Silver Rate in Agra | Bank Holidays in Agra | Public Holidays in Agra | Agra AQI | Weather in Agra | Petrol Price in Agra | Diesel Price in Agra | CNG Price in Agra | LPG Price in AgraStay updated with the latest Agra news. headline: MP’s Mandsaur Missing Bus Driver’s Headless Skeleton Found In Well After Three Months, Family Suspects
content: Piplia Mandi (Madhya Pradesh): The skeletal remains of a bus driver missing for three months were recovered from a well in Rupni village under Nahargarh police station in Mandsaur district on Saturday evening, sparking protests by his family on Sunday, who suspect murder.The deceased, identified as Kanhaiyalal Prajapat of Jamuniya Meena village, worked for Prince Bus. His head and both arms were reportedly missing from the remains.Following Sunday's post-mortem at Mandsaur district hospital, relatives refused to accept the body and staged a brief road blockade at Gandhi Chauraha, demanding immediate arrests.According to the family, Kanhaiyalal left with the bus on Aug 21. On Aug 22, he parked it at Ranayara village around 7 pm and went to a man named Rakesh Dhangar's restaurant in Rupni but never returned.His maternal uncle Badrilal filed a missing person's report on Aug 31. The family subsequently approached the collector and superintendent of police on Sept 22, naming Bhim Singh, Jagdish, Shyam Lal and Ranjit Singh for investigation.Farmer leader Shyamlal Jokchand and Congress leaders Somil Nahata, Rajesh Raghuvanshi and Mukesh Dhakad supported the family's demands. Officials, including the tehsildar and CSP, reached the hospital. The family also sought Rs one lakh assistance through the Red Cross.Nahargarh station in-charge Varun Tiwari said preliminary findings suggested suicide, but the post-mortem report and further investigation would determine the circumstances. The body remains at the district hospital.Level up your brain the fun way. headline: CII pitches sweeping reforms to prepare financial system for 2047
content: NEW DELHI: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) has proposed a sweeping set of financial sector reforms to help India build the capacity to fund a $26.5 trillion economy by 2047. The recommendations span banking, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), capital markets, insurance and financial technology, and include a permanent liquidity window for well-governed NBFCs, changes to priority sector lending norms and wider institutional access to corporate bonds.The recommendations come as the government reviews the financial sector through the High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat, set up following its announcement in the Union Budget for 2026-27. The six-month exercise will examine the long-term capital needs of banks, development finance institutions (DFIs) and NBFCs, review priority sector lending and chart a roadmap for artificial intelligence and digital adoption.CII's analysis estimates that a $26.5 trillion economy by 2047 would require financial assets of nearly $106 trillion, against about $7 trillion currently. Banking assets would need to grow 3-3.5 percentage points faster than nominal gross domestic product (GDP), raising the bank assets-to-GDP ratio from around 1.0 times to 1.5 times.“The task now is to build a system that can finance an economy several times its present size by 2047. That requires deeper and longer-tenor pools of capital, credit that reaches the sectors that will drive growth, and regulation that keeps pace with how finance is delivered,” said Chandrajit Banerjee, director general, CII.Strengthening NBFCsCII has proposed a permanent, rule-based liquidity and refinancing window for well-governed NBFCs, which account for about 23% of credit but source nearly 45% of their borrowings from banks. Access would depend on compliance, collateral standards and eligibility criteria, helping prevent market stress and rollover pressures from constraining credit to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and retail borrowers.It has also sought parity with other regulated lenders in recovery mechanisms, including lowering the NBFC threshold under the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest (SARFAESI) Act from ₹20 lakh to ₹1 lakh, matching the limit for banks and housing finance companies.Other proposals include access for regulated NBFCs to debt recovery tribunals, the Central Repository of Information on Large Credits subject to safeguards, and central fraud registries with reciprocal data-sharing obligations.Reworking priority sector lendingOn priority sector lending, CII has proposed raising the renewable energy loan limit from ₹35 crore to ₹80-100 crore per borrower to cover medium-sized projects, and including circular economy activities such as recycling and battery reuse.It has also called for aligning sub-targets for small and marginal farmers with assessed credit demand, reviewing priority sector categories every three to five years, and replacing the 2% cap on incremental export credit with a dedicated export sub-target. Eligibility should also extend to factoring, export receivables and supply-chain finance, it said.With the MSME credit gap estimated at ₹25-30 trillion, CII has proposed making insurance against fire, floods, machinery breakdown and business interruption a standard feature of government-guaranteed MSME loans to reduce non-performing asset risks and guarantee invocation.Deepening capital markets and insuranceTo widen the corporate bond investor base, CII has proposed calibrated exposure for pension funds, insurers and provident funds to securities rated below AA and to longer-tenor instruments. India's corporate bond market accounts for around 15% of GDP, against 36% in China and more than 80% in South Korea, according to its analysis.Other proposals include extending the Corporate Debt Market Development Fund to below-investment-grade securities with defined activation triggers, allowing target maturity funds across AA, A and BBB ratings, and setting up a credit enhancement institution for smaller and lower-rated issuers outside infrastructure, including NBFCs.In insurance, CII has recommended zero-rating individual health and life policies under the goods and services tax regime, rather than exempting them, to allow insurers to claim input tax credit. It has also sought alignment of insurers' tax computation with IRDAI-prescribed reserves as the sector moves towards Ind AS.A proposed national catastrophe and climate risk pool would combine mandatory cession by primary insurers, catastrophe bonds issued through GIFT International Financial Services Centre, a sovereign reinsurance backstop and parametric insurance for climate events.CII has also called for calibrated increases in investment limits for insurers, banks and financial institutions in alternative investment funds (AIFs), while opening participation to mutual funds, pension funds and the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation.Digital and institutional reformsOn digital financial infrastructure, CII has proposed extending the Account Aggregator framework to public databases, including land records, e-Mandi transactions, Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act records and ration card data, subject to consent safeguards.It has also recommended raising the voting rights cap in private sector banks from 26% to up to 49%, with governance safeguards, to align voting rights with economic ownership. Separately, it has called for early approval of the proposal to raise the foreign investment limit in public sector banks from 20% to 49%.Coordinated reforms across banks, NBFCs, capital markets, insurers and pension funds are needed to mobilise long-term capital and strengthen the financial system for India's growth ambitions, CII said.

headline: Education is corner stone of development and self-reliance of State: CM
content:
The Chief Minister said that a degree is not only recognition of a student's hard work but also represents their responsibility towards society and the nation. Education is not merely about securing employment; it is a means of developing critical thinking, understanding, research, innovation and bringing positive changes to society. He emphasized that the greatest strength of any country lies in its educated, aware and responsible citizens.

He said that in an era of rapid advancements in artificial intelligence, robotics, biotechnology, data science and digital technology, the education system must prepare young people not only to seek employment but also to generate employment, undertake research and promote innovation.

The Chief Minister stated that the State Government considers education a vital foundation for development and self-reliance. The government's objective is to provide the youth of Himachal Pradesh modern knowledge and technology and enable them to establish their identity at national and international levels. Considering the challenging geographical conditions of the state, he said that it is the government's responsibility to ensure access to quality education and resources for children living in remote villages.

He said that Himachal Pradesh has made remarkable progress in the field of quality education. In 2021, the state ranked 21st in the country, whereas it has now improved to the fifth position. The State Government has introduced English-medium education from Class I and implemented the CBSE curriculum in 156 government schools. Preparations are also underway to open 100 additional CBSE schools from the next academic session.

The Chief Minister said that the availability of qualified teachers is essential for ensuring quality education. In this direction, 10,000 posts have been filled in the Education Department, while recruitment of another 3,000 teachers is underway.

He emphasized that the education of no meritorious student should be disrupted due to financial constraints. To promote equality in education, the State Government has decided to remove the caste-related column from school admission forms from the upcoming academic session. He said that children should be identified by their talent and hard work, while eligible families will continue to receive benefits under government welfare schemes as before.

headline: VERY VERY IMPORTANT NEWS RECEIVED FROM DIRECTOR PUBLIC RELATIONS SHIMLA FOCUSING CM THAKUR SUKHVINDER SINGH AND HIS ASSOCIATES
content:
HPPCL records 3,459.99 MUs power, Rs. 1,387.49 crore revenue in four years

SHIMLA, 22.11.26-The Himachal Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (HPPCL) has recorded power generation of 3,459.99 Million Units resulting in a revenue accumulation of Rs. 1,387.49 crore in its last four years since December, 2022. The 100 MW Sainj Hydroelectric Project in Kullu district contributed 1,252.56 MUs of electricity earning a revenue of Rs. 462.55 crore.

Similarly, 65 MW Kashang Stage-I Hydroelectric Project in Kinnaur generated 776.328 MUs and a revenue of Rs. 252 crore. The 5 MW Berra Dol solar power project in Bilaspur District contributed 62.78 MUs and a revenue of Rs. 27.05 crore. The 11 MUs Sawra Kuddu Hydroelectric Project in Shimla district contributed 1,190.383 MUs of electricity earning a revenue of Rs. 589.6 crore. The 32 MW Pekhubela solar power project in Una district and inaugurated on 20th June, 2024 by the Chief Minister Thakur Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, recorded net power generation of 113.27 MUs realizing revenue of Rs. 32.89 crore.

Likewise, the 5 MW Bhanjal solar power project located in Una district generated 18.87 MUs and revenue of Rs. 6.83 crore. The 10 MW Aghlor solar power project in Una district contributed 25.02 MUs and a revenue of Rs. 7.75 crore.

Apart from these commissioned projects, various hydro power projects were under execution, including 450 MW Shongtong Karcham Hydroelectric Project in Kinnaur district, the work of which has been expedited and the project is expected to be completed by April, 2027. The works on the 130 MW Integrated Kashang Stage-II & III Hydroelectric Project in Kinnaur district and 48 MW Chanju-III HEP in Chamba district would be completed in the coming years. The construction of the diversion tunnel of the 40 MW Renukaji Dam Project in Sirmaur district is currently underway and the main dam works are expected to be awarded in the next fiscal.

The 191 MW Thana Plaun HEP in Mandi Distt, the 48 MW Surgani Sundla Hydroelectric Project, designed to utilize the tail water of Baira Suil Hydroelectric Project, the 1,630 MW Renukaji Pump Storage Project in Sirmaur district, the 270 MW Thana Plaun Pump Storage Project in District Mandi, the 780 MW Jangi Thopan Hydro Electric Project in District Kinnaur and the 422 MW Kishau Multipurpose Project on River Tons are at pre-construction stage. These projects are intended to support the integration of renewable energy into the power system and provide energy storage and balancing capabilities.

headline: 'Rahul Gandhi is behaving like a frustrated cat': Kangana hits back at Congress leader
content:
Agra: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut visited the Taj Mahal on Sunday and attacked Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the Indian economy, saying the Congress leader is acting like a "frustrated cat."

The actor-politician spent around an hour admiring the monument and posing for photographs and selfies.

She visited the mausoleum around 3 pm, accompanied by family members and escorted by security.

After exploring the monument, the Mandi MP told reporters that India is the fastest-growing economy in Asia and "Rahul Gandhi is behaving like a frustrated cat scratching a pole."

Reacting to Gandhi's allegation that the RSS and BJP are "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists", Kangana accused the Congress of opposing the women's reservation.

"If the BJP is male-dominated, why is it fighting for the Women's Reservation Bill? It is the Congress that is opposing the bill and preventing its implementation. The anti-women mindset is that of the Congress," she said.

headline: Odisha targets 98 lakh metric tonnes of paddy procurement in 2026-27
content: The Odisha government drew up an extensive plan on Sunday to procure 98 lakh metric tonnes (MT) of paddy during the 2026-27 Kharif and Rabi season s, aiming to ensure a smooth procurement process and timely payment to farmers. Advertisment Also Read: Odisha sets 78 lakh tonne paddy procurement target for Kharif season The decision was discussed at a meeting of the Paddy Procurement Committee chaired by Chief Secretary Anu Garg. Advertisment Of the total target, the government aims to procure 78 lakh MT during the Kharif season alone. The procurement process will continue until March 31. As many as 22.27 lakh farmers have registered themselves to sell their paddy this year, marking a 13 per cent increase compared to the previous year, a senior official said. Farmers will receive Rs 3,100 per quintal for common-grade paddy, including input assistance. The government has also made arrangements to transfer the payment directly into farmers' bank accounts within 48 hours of the sale. 4,067 Paddy Mandis To Remain Under CCTV Surveillance Paddy procurement will be carried out through 4,067 mandis across the State. To prevent irregularities such as illegal deductions in the name of quality-related cuts (Katni Chhatni), mandis will remain under 24-hour CCTV surveillance. Mandi nodal officers and supervisors will be deployed to monitor procurement activities and ensure transparency. The government will also keep strict surveillance along Odisha's borders to prevent the illegal entry of paddy from neighbouring states. With an increased procurement target and a higher number of registered farmers, the State government is focusing on timely procurement, transparent transactions and safeguards against malpractice to ensure farmers receive the stipulated price for their produce.
