headline: Government has asked us to reconsider restricting all protests to Freedom Park, says Bengaluru’s new Chief Commissioner of Police
content: Bengaluru Following the restructuring of Bengaluru City Police into five commissionerates, several concerns, including dual reporting structures, uneven distribution of police stations, and the status of the Central Crime Branch, have been flagged. https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/bangalore/ In an interview with The Hindu, the newly-appointed Chief Commissioner of Police, Bengaluru City, R. Hithendra, addresses these concerns and explains the plans ahead. CM’s agenda for Bengaluru police: Zero tolerance for drugs, hate speech and traffic congestion CM’s agenda for Bengaluru police: Zero tolerance for drugs, hate speech and traffic congestion CM’s agenda for Bengaluru police: Zero tolerance for drugs, hate speech and traffic congestion storyline 1 You have taken charge during a transition phase. What will be your immediate focus? First, to establish a new layer of top-level governance. Second, to resolve coordination issues between the commissionerates. The issue is the relocation of manpower, which we will resolve soon. Once operations begin, nobody will work in silos. Every Commissioner has to report to me, so all coordination issues will eventually come to my table. We also aim to enhance transparency in governance, make the city safer, ensure women’s safety and control drugs. The new organisational structure has dual reporting built into it. Isn’t it problematic? RH: This dual reporting structure is deliberate. Officers sitting in the city centre cannot supervise those posted in Kengeri or Whitefield effectively. Therefore, there will be supervision at the local level as well as at the top level. There is no clarity on Central Crime Branch There is no clarity on Central Crime Branch There is no clarity on Central Crime Branch storyline 1 The Traffic Commissioner will oversee planning and implementation plans, while micro-level issues will be handled by the local commissionerates. A junior officer used to head Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) and struggled to get their views across in inter-departmental meetings. Now with a Commissioner for Traffic, BTP’s point of view will be well taken. The officer will also have more time to focus on larger planning and strategy. This will help in administrative work like tenders as well. Likewise, in the case of crimes, cases that require special attention and have pan-city repercussions will be handled by the Anti-Rowdy Squad. There is some confusion about the future of the CCB. There is no confusion. The CCB has been renamed the Anti-Rowdy Squad. If you go by the interpretation of statutes, only the squad has been renamed, and everything else remains unchanged. Dual reporting structures built into the new police system in Bengaluru, raise concerns Dual reporting structures built into the new police system in Bengaluru, raise concerns Speaking to The Hindu, senior officers who have previously held the position of Traffic DCPs in the city said the new hierarchy could create complications in obtaining approvals, planning, and coordinating with civic bodies Dual reporting structures built into the new police system in Bengaluru, raise concerns storyline 1 TH: Some of the new divisions created have fewer police stations, not all urbanised police stations around the city have been added either. RH: The idea is that the Central Commissionerate will remain the same. But the other four commissionerates will gradually expand to include more police stations of adjoining districts, where the areas are sufficiently urbanised. TH: There has been a long-standing demand that all protests should not be restricted to Freedom Park alone. Will the The Licensing and Regulation of Protests, Demonstrations and Protest Marches (Bengaluru City) Order, 2021 be reconsidered? RH: The Home Minister has asked us to reconsider this. We are thinking on those lines, but no decision has been made yet. TH: Cybercrimes now account for a majority of crimes in the City. But investigations have mostly been able to crack the lowest rung and not go up further. How do you intend to change this? RH: Skill upgradation is being undertaken for investigators at the Criminal Investigation Department. However, those who receive training are subsequently transferred. Those who are skilled need to be retained. We need to formulate a policy for this. Bengaluru Police Commissioner orders probe against sub-inspector for role in Renukaswamy murder case Bengaluru Police Commissioner orders probe against sub-inspector for role in Renukaswamy murder case Bengaluru Police Commissioner orders probe against sub-inspector for role in Renukaswamy murder case storyline 1 TH: Even in drug-related cases, arrests do not seem to go beyond the peddlers. You have till recently headed the Anti Narcotics Task Force. How do you intend to bring that experience to your new assignment? RH: We have an FIR-to-chargesheet ratio of one is to one, which means that if there is one name in the FIR, we are chargesheeting only one person. If a peddler is caught, they must have procured the drugs from somewhere and intended to sell them to consumers. Those aspects need to be looked at. We have flagged this issue to the investigating officers. Henceforth, we will focus more on investigations following the seizure of contraband.

headline: Beyond the Myth of the Gandhis
content: Prominent leaders in Indian politics have traditionally been elevated to pedestals of reverence and unquestioning loyalty by their supporters. Such adulation is often matched by relentless vilification, with detractors subjecting them to exaggerated criticism and aspersions. The Gandhis, arguably the most politically consequential family in independent India, have long occupied an almost mythical, hallowed place in the country’s political imagination. The most significant contribution of Sonia Gandhi’s much-discussed memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, is its attempt, from an insider’s perspective, to demystify and humanise the seemingly impenetrable, much-speculated-about lives of the family.Moving beyond conventional political analyses of the family’s electoral fortunes and governance records, the book offers a rare and intimate account of the people who have inhabited Sonia’s world in India. The absence of memoirs by Indira or Rajiv Gandhi, combined with Sonia’s characteristic reticence, has only heightened curiosity about the book. It is, therefore, unsurprising that the personal takes precedence over the political. In Sonia’s own words, “This is a memoir, wherein politics serves to frame the main narrative, which is a personal account of my thoughts, feelings and decisions.” Yet, a life story is never simply a spontaneous recollection of events; it is also a conscious exercise in deciding what to reveal and how. Whether readers interpret them as political messaging or personal reflection is ultimately up to them.First, as its title suggests, the book celebrates love and familial bonds, often obscured by the harsh glare of political commentary. Beyond the romantic, lifelong companionship between Sonia and Rajiv, the memoir explores the affection, expectations, disagreements and occasional bickering that shaped relationships within the family: between Indira and her sons, Sonia and her mother-in-law, Sonia and Maneka, and Rajiv and Sonia as parents to their children. It also offers a heartwarming account of Sonia’s ordinary, modest, conservative yet fun-filled childhood in a small Italian town. Along the way, it reveals the many facets of the Gandhi household: Indira’s eye for detail, occasional temper and love of art and culture; Sanjay as “good company full of humour and pranks”; and the shared interests that brought Rajiv and Sanjay together. .While Sonia Gandhi is critical of the ideological worldview and governance style of her political rivals, she acknowledges Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s rise from a humble background and his aversion to Delhi’s political elite.Second, and perhaps most significantly, the primacy of duty over personal desire emerges as a recurring theme. Sonia’s sense of duty, notably, predates her entry into the Gandhi household. She traces it to her upbringing in Italy under the watch of a strict disciplinarian father with a widely respected army background. “Thus the story of my family, as that of many Italians of the time, was one of duty: Big or small, certain things had to be done, certain rules had to be followed,” she writes. This sense of obligation acquired a deeper significance after her marriage into the Gandhi family, as her aspiration for the ‘normal, simple life’ she had envisaged repeatedly gave way to the demands of public service and the family’s expectations.These choices came at a considerable personal cost. Challenging assumptions about the unqualified privileges enjoyed by members of a political dynasty, the memoir recounts the ordeals the family endured by virtue of its proximity to power. From Rajiv giving up his cherished career as a pilot to Sonia’s inner turmoil over his, and subsequently her own, entry into politics despite her deep reservations, the book captures the erosion of personal freedom and the relentless public scrutiny that defined their lives. The denial of an ordinary childhood, compounded by the ever-present fear of tragedy, also shaped Rahul and Priyanka’s formative years. The assassinations of Indira and Rajiv remain the most devastating manifestations of this vulnerability.Finally, Sonia’s account of her own political career, confined largely to the final sections, reflects the restraint that has characterised her public life. While she is sharply critical of the ideological worldview and governance style of her political rivals, she acknowledges Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s rise from a humble background and his aversion to Delhi’s political elite. Recalling Rajiv’s premiership, she refers to “those close to us, who had taken on a political role came to overreach themselves; when the inevitable rupture occurred, they turned hostile and hit back”, but chooses not to elaborate. She is more forthcoming, however, in offering her perspective on some longstanding allegations, including her strained relationship with former Prime Minister PV Narasimha Rao. Interestingly, she also acknowledges the ‘grey’ areas of politics and the need for pragmatism, including the necessity of building bridges with parties such as the DMK, NCP and AAP despite ideological differences, in the pursuit of a ‘greater purpose’.No book, particularly a political memoir, is without its limitations. Although the UPA years and post-2014 political developments receive some attention, a deeper engagement with Sonia’s tenure as Congress president, the party’s organisational shortcomings, would have added considerable depth to the narrative. But this is, after all, ‘her story’, one that is, as she emphasises, ‘more personal than political’. In that sense, the book excels as a touching personal account of a deeply political life..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Ludhiana: Salary of 33 teachers withheld over BLO duty, union objects | Hindustan Times
content: A directive by the office of the electoral registration officer (Sahnewal)-cum-sub-divisional magistrate (Ludhiana East) to withhold the November salaries of 33 government school teachers for not performing booth level officer (BLO) duties has triggered resentment among teachers, who allege they are being pressured into dual duties despite already being deployed for census work.Issued on November 17, the letter instructed the district education officers (secondary and elementary) not to disburse the November salaries of the listed staff—comprising 18 teachers from secondary and middle schools, and 15 teachers and head teachers from primary schools—unless they obtain a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the SDM office.Dharamjeet Singh Dhillon, state finance secretary of the Lecturer Cadre Union Punjab and its Ludhiana district president, termed the directive unnecessary mental and financial harassment. Affected teachers pointed out that they have already received appointment letters, identity cards, and materials for census duties from the same office.They further cited clear instructions from the additional deputy commissioner (rural development) stating that staff assigned census work must not be deployed elsewhere, alleging that the election cell was not following these directions.The union added that a warning of disciplinary action under Section 134 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, has deepened anxiety among educators and threatens to disrupt classroom teaching.Urging senior officials to coordinate between the election and census cells, Dhillon demanded the immediate withdrawal of the salary-withholding order and exemption from BLO duties for staff on census deployment. “The department should stop putting teachers under mental and financial pressure in the name of duties,” he said.When contacted, Ludhiana East sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) Baljinder Singh said, “We will certainly hear out employees who are already assigned census duties and take action accordingly.”

headline: Ludhiana: Amid lack of monitoring, workers continue repairs on PSPCL poles without safety gear
content: Despite the Punjab government distributing 10,500 safety kits worth ₹12.60 crore among employees of the Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL) nearly four months ago, workers can still be seen climbing electricity poles to carry out repair work without wearing the prescribed safety equipment.In recent months, two PSPCL workers lost their lives due to electrocution in recent months. The safety kits given to the workers include voltage sensors, pole safety belts, helmets, gloves, safety goggles and reflective jackets among other items. Pole safety belts prevent workers from falling in case of any mishap.However, the lack of regular monitoring at work sites raises concerns over whether workers are consistently using the prescribed equipment while carrying out repairs particularly in areas with multiple electricity lines.When contacted, junior engineer (JE) Varinder Singh said, “During distribution, it was ensured that all workers got the safety kits. The PSPCL gives tenders to contractors who further engage workers to carry out the work. The contractors are responsible for ensuring that the workers they hire follow safety measures and use the required equipment. We cannot reach every location and keep checking all the time. When we visit a particular site, the workers are not always there.”According to Jasdev Singh Hans, PSPCL chief engineer (Ludhiana central zone), the corporation gives tenders to contractors who subsequently hire workers to carry out the repair and maintenance work. The contractor is primarily responsible in case of a mishap but the PSPCL also has a responsibility to ensure that safety measures are followed, he said. “If we find anyone working without following the required safety measures, we take action immediately. We can impose a penalty or even blacklist them,” he added.Recent mishapsOn August 29, a 42-year-old contractual PSPCL worker from Govindsar, Sukhjit Singh, died after being electrocuted while replacing a faulty jumper near the 66-kV Giaspura substation. He was working on the Kabir Nagar feeder after a shutdown permit had been obtained. Back-feeding from some generator triggered the mishap, officials said.On September 23, Resham Singh, a CHB worker with the PSPCL, died after suffering an electric shock while fixing a fault in Sahnewal. A permit had reportedly been obtained and the Bhagwanpura AP feeder was shut down. However, he reportedly climbed onto the Dugri AP feeder which was live and suffered an electric shock.

headline: PMLA case against suspended DIG: ED summons seven serving and retired Punjab officials, including IAS, IP
content: NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned seven serving and retired Punjab government officials, including IAS and IPS officers, for questioning in a money-laundering case against suspended state DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar, officials said on Sunday.Of the seven officials summoned, five are currently serving in the government, while the others have retired.The ED is also investigating their alleged links with Bhullar's aide, Krishanu Sharda, who has been arrested in the case.Kumar Rahul, secretary in Punjab's health and family welfare department, has been asked to appear before the ED on Monday, while Anand Sagar, staff officer to the commissioner of Faridkot division, has been summoned on November 25. Neeru Katyal Gupta, special secretary in the General Administration and Coordination Department, is scheduled to appear on November 26.The agency has also summoned two police officers. Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh has been called for questioning on November 26, while Ludhiana Police Commissioner Swapan Sharma has been asked to appear the following day.The two retired officials summoned are former bureaucrats. Gurpreet Sapra, who previously served as the Jalandhar Commissioner, has been asked to appear on November 26. Arun Sekhri, who served as divisional commissioner for Faridkot, Ferozepur and Jalandhar, has been summoned for questioning on November 25.The money-laundering case against Bhullar under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) stems from two FIRs registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) against him and his associates over alleged bribery and possession of assets disproportionate to their known sources of income.Bhullar, who was serving as Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police, Ropar Range, was arrested by the CBI in October 2025. The arrest followed a complaint by a scrap dealer who alleged that a bribe had been demanded from him through an intermediary to settle a case.(With PTI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: ED summons several serving, retired Punjab IAS, IPS officers in DIG HS Bhullar case
content: Chandigarh: The Enforcement Directorate has summoned half a dozen serving and retired Punjab government bureaucrats, including IAS and IPS officers, for questioning in the money-laundering case against suspended state DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar and entities linked to him, officials said on Sunday. .According to officials, the ED is exploring their alleged links with Bhullar’s aide, Krishanu Sharda, who was arrested in the case. .ED has asked those summoned to appear at its office in Chandigarh. .Those summoned include Kumar Rahul, a 2000 batch IAS officer and Administrative Secretary of the Health and Family Welfare department. He has been asked to appear before the agency on Monday. Anand Sagar Sharma, PCS (2012 batch), Staff Officer to Commissioner, Faridkot Division, has been asked to come to the ED office on November 25, while Neeru Katyal Gupta, IAS officer (2016 batch) and Special Secretary, General Administration and Coordination, has been summoned for November 26. .SSP (PPS) Fazilka Gagan Ajit Singh has been summoned to appear on November 26, while Ludhiana Commissioner of Police Swapan Sharma (IPS officer of 2009 batch) has been summoned on November 27. .ED raids against ex-Telangana MLA Nayak, her company in PMLA case.Two retired officers -- Gurpreet Sapra of IAS (PCS) 2005 batch and Arun Sekhri IAS (PCS) of 2004 batch–– are also among those asked to depose before the federal agency's Chandigarh office on November 26 and November 25, respectively. .Sapra last served as the Commissioner of Jalandhar, while Sekhri was the Divisional Commissioner of Faridkot, Ferozepur and Jalandhar districts. .The Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case stems from two CBI FIRs filed against Bhullar and his associates on charges of bribery and alleged possession of disproportionate assets. .Bhullar, who was serving as the Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police (Ropar Range), was arrested by the CBI in October 2025 after a scrap dealer alleged that a bribe was demanded from him through an intermediary to settle a case.

headline: Warring launches ‘Insaaf March’ against Mann govt in Ludhiana | Hindustan Times
content: Former Punjab Congress president and Ludhiana MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring on Saturday launched the party’s ‘Insaaf March’ from the Clock Tower here to corner the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the law and order situation, gangsterism, extortion, drug abuse and economic distress in Punjab.The march passed through Chaura Bazar before culminating near Division Number 3 Chowk, where Warring addressed party leaders and supporters.Several senior Congress leaders – including AICC secretary Ravinder Dalvi, former MLA Surinder Dawar, who is being considered a probable Congress candidate from the Central assembly constituency, former MLAs Simarjit Singh Bains, Kuldeep Vaid, Rakesh Pandey and district Congress committee president Sanjay Talwar – and workers participated in the march. However, former cabinet minister Bharat Bhushan Ashu and his supporters conspicuously stayed away.Former Cabinet Minister Malkiat Singh Dakha, Capt Sandeep Sandhu, Pawan Dewan, KK Bawa, Balwinder Singh Bains and Jassi Khangura were also present.Announcing that the march would be taken out in every city and town of the state, Warring said the Congress would continue to hold the state government accountable for its failures.Citing 170 murder cases filed in Ludhiana between 2022 and 2024, Warring questioned chief minister Bhagwant Mann over the law and order situation. He alleged that gangsters operating from inside prisons were threatening traders and businessmen for extortion.He also flagged difficulties confronting Ludhiana’s textile, dyeing and bicycle industries, non-payment of dearness allowance (DA) to government employees, farmers’ protests and the drug menace.Warring also welcomed Saurav Sachdeva, who recently left the BJP to join the Congress.The Saturday march also came amid questions over Warring’s participation in the recent Congress programmes, including former CM Charanjit Singh Channi’s ‘Jawani Sambhal Yatra’.

headline: Congress protests against AAP govt in Ludhiana
content: Congress leaders and workers, led by former city Youth Congress district president Yogesh Handa, staged a protest at Baba Than Singh Chowk in Ludhiana Central constituency against the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government, alleging a sharp deterioration in law and order across Punjab.Addressing the gathering on the occasion, Handa claimed that the state’s law-and-order machinery had collapsed under the AAP regime, emboldening gangsters and criminals.He alleged that incidents of murder, robbery, theft and extortion were increasing, with criminals committing offences openly and without fear of the law enforcement agencies. According to him, the rising crime rate had created an atmosphere of fear and insecurity among citizens, traders and business owners.

headline: Why basmati farmers have reasons to be happy despite drought across much of India
content: Large swathes of India – the southern states, Maharashtra, Saurashtra-Kutch, Rajasthan, west Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and the Northeast – are reeling under dry weather with incipient farmer distress, thanks to El Niño. But this isn’t so with the basmati rice belt of Punjab, Haryana and west Uttar Pradesh (UP), where farmers are reaping the benefits of higher crop yields as well as prices. Rajesh Kumar Kundu, belonging to Bhusli village in Haryana’s Karnal district, has harvested an average 22-23 quintals per acre of paddy (rice with husk) from Pusa Basmati-1509, a popular short-duration variety with 115-120 days seed-to-grain maturity. This was as against 18-20 quintals in 2025. It's not yield alone. The 52-year-old, who cultivates basmati on 15 acres and sugarcane on his balance 25-acre land, also realised Rs 3,900-4,000 per quintal for the crop that he sold between September 15 and 20 at Karnal’s Nayi Anaj Mandi or new grain market. His last year’s sale price range was just Rs 2,800-3,000. Deepak Kumar, on Friday, sold 100 quintals of Pusa Basmati-1718 paddy from five out of his 10-acre holding in Kalheri village of Karnal’s Gharaunda tehsil (block). “My yield of 20 quintals was almost the same, but the Rs 4,800/quintal rate I received is higher than the Rs 3,600 of last year,” said this farmer, who has also planted Pusa Basmati-1121 on two acres and PR-14 on three acres. Pusa-1718 and Pusa-1121 are both medium-duration (140-145 days maturity) basmati varieties, while PR-14 is a non-basmati paddy. “Last year, we had excess rainfall in August-September, when the crop was at flowering stage. There was also some damage from the Fijivirus disease causing stunting and dwarfing in rice plants. This year, we had no such floods or prolonged inundation. So, yields have been 4-5 quintals higher in Pusa-1509 and 3-4 quintals for Pusa-1121 and 1718,” noted Gurcharan Singh Sandhu, a seed farmer from Brass village in Karnal’s Nissing sub-tehsil. Sandhi grows high-quality foundation seeds of the Pusa basmati varieties – bred by the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) – on 80 acres of his own and another 50 acres of leased land. He multiplies these from 100% genetically-pure breeder seeds sourced from IARI, both for selling back to the New Delhi-based institute and supplying to other farmers. “This is one of those rare years, where basmati farmers are enjoying the twin benefits of higher yields and remunerative prices,” Shiv Kumar Garg, a commission agent and proprietor of Shri Krishna Trading Company at the Karnal mandi, pointed out. Pusa Basmati-1121 paddy is now selling at Rs 5,200-5,500 per quintal in this wholesale market, with the crop harvested manually, as opposed to combines, fetching the higher rates. Prices for Pusa Basmati-1718 are, likewise, at Rs 4,700-5,200 per quintal. Last year, the two varieties (marketed during November-December) fetched only Rs 3,800-4,200 and 3,500-3,700 per quintal respectively. “This time, prices for Pusa-1509 (the crop of west UP arrives from July and that of Haryana from late-August through mid-October) too were at Rs 3,800-4,300 per quintal, versus last year’s 2,700-3,200,” added Garg. The reason for the better price realisations has been sustained export demand, coupled with a poor crop last year. “Production in 2023 and 2024 was good. Low prices, in turn, led to higher exports alongside domestic sales. But as the 2025 crop was bad, there was very little carry-forward stocks, resulting in higher prices this year,” according to Vijay Kumar Setia, chairman and managing director of the Rs 1,450-crore turnover Chaman Lal Setia Exports Ltd. Setia’s company, which sells the ‘Maharani’ brand of basmati rice, has its unit with a paddy processing capacity of 480 tonnes per day on the Karnal-Kaithal road. Every tonne of paddy milled yields 620-630 kg of rice. Out of the 620-630 kg, the non-broken grains or “head” rice constitutes 75-80% in Pusa-1121 and Pusa-1718, while lower (around 65%) for Pusa-1509. India shipped out a record 60-65 lakh tonnes (lt) of basmati rice worth $5.8-5.9 billion annually in 2024-25 and 2025-26 (April-March). The current fiscal has seen a drop in quantity, but higher value of shipments. The increased unit value export realisations – from $872 (Rs 75,284) per tonne in April-September 2025 to $959 (Rs 91,303) in April-September 2026 (see table) – has enabled farmers to obtain higher paddy rates. Dhermesh Verma, director of TerraSense Intellicrop Pvt. Ltd, has estimated this year’s total basmati paddy crop at 111.04 lt, 12.2% up from 99.01 lt of 2025. All major growing states have posted higher output – Haryana (39.91 lt to 44.03 lt), Punjab (26.56 lt to 34.20 lt), west UP (29.91 lt to 30.03 lt) and Jammu & Kashmir (1.26 lt to 1.47 lt) – with overall average yields also rising from 16.12 to 18.88 quintals per acre. Basmati production – from the seven states (including Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Delhi) covering the aromatic rice strain’s protected “geographical indication” area – hit an all-time-high of 113.08 lt in 2023 and 110.78 lt in 2024, before dipping to 99.01 lt in 2025. “The basmati crop requires open skies and bright sunshine during its flowering time for maximum pollination and proper grain setting. Last year, the flowers either fell or could not get fertilised because of heavy rains. Therefore, you had empty kernels being formed, translating into lower yields,” explained Verma, whose company uses remote sensing data analytics and ground truthing for assessing crop acreage, yields and production. The lack of rainfall, in a way, has been blessing for the basmati belt farmers – even if not for their counterparts in most other states.

headline: HC suspends sentence of Manimajra govt staffer | Hindustan Times
content: The Punjab and Haryana high court has suspended the jail term of Shyam Singh Chauhan, an employee working as a senior assistant in the office of the deputy chief controller of explosives in Manimajra, in a 9-year-old corruption case. He was convicted by a CBI court in August and awarded a four-year jail term.He had appealed against the same arguing that prosecution failed to prove the demand and acceptance of illegal gratification. The appellant remained on bail for about nine years during the trial without any misuse of liberty, has no criminal antecedents and has a family dependent upon him. He has already undergone custody of about three months. The sentence is for a fixed term of four years only and the appeal, being of the year 2026, is not likely to be heard in the near future. The appeal would thus be rendered infructuous if the appellant is made to serve the entire sentence, his counsel, senior advocate Bipan Ghai had argued.The court suspended the sentence observing that the appellant remained on bail for about nine years since August 2017 and nothing has been brought to the notice of the court to show that he misused the liberty or tampered with the prosecution evidence. “This circumstance indicates that he is not likely to flee from justice. The record of the trial which continued for nine years is voluminous and the appeal is not likely to be taken up soon,” it said ordering his release on bail but asked him not to leave the country.The case dates back to 2017 when one Devendra Pal Singh, a resident of Mandi, Himachal Pradesh alleged that Chauhan demanded a bribe in return for issuing a licence. On July 11, 2017, the CBI laid a trap and arrested Chauhan while he was allegedly accepting the bribe near the Manimajra office. Based on this, the CBI registered a case in July 2017 under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

headline: 13 children among 23 injured as cylinder explodes in Councillor’s home in UP’s Jalaun
content: Twenty-three people, including 13 children, sustained burn injuries following a powerful explosion caused by a domestic gas (LPG) cylinder in the Orai area of Jalaun district on Sunday evening, police said.Nineteen individuals who suffered severe burns have been referred to Jhansi Medical College for better medical care.Superintendent of Police (SP) Suresh Chandra Rawat said that a fire broke out unexpectedly in a domestic gas cylinder at the residence of local Councillor Mata Prasad in Shantinagar locality around 6 pm on Sunday.He explained that as family members and people nearby were attempting to extinguish the fire, the cylinder exploded violently, injuring 23 people, including 13 children.Rawat added that upon receiving information about the incident, police and administrative officials arrived at the scene, initiated relief and rescue operations, and ensured that all the injured were promptly transported to the hospital.According to police, 19 of the severely injured were sent by ambulance to Jhansi Medical College, whereas the remaining four are undergoing treatment in the District Hospital in Orai.An investigation into the incident is underway, the SP said.

headline: Leaders’ conduct may have been wanting: Shekhawat on BJP’s rural poll defeat in Rajasthan, vows review
content: Senior BJP leader and Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Sunday acknowledged the BJP’s defeat in the rural local body elections across panchayat samitis and zila parishads in Rajasthan, saying the party would conduct a comprehensive review to identify the reasons behind the setback.The Congress swept the rural elections in the state shortly after the BJP had put up a strong performance in the urban local body elections.Speaking on the defeat, Shekhawat, the Jodhpur MP, said, “An election reflects the people's mandate, and we accept it with respect. There may have been shortcomings in communicating the work of our double-engine government effectively at the grassroots level. There may also have been a lack of enthusiasm among our workers, or shortcomings in the conduct and behaviour of those holding senior positions. In the BJP, every victory and defeat is followed by a review.”On his arrival in Rajasthan, Shekhawat said the BJP had, somewhere along the line, failed to effectively communicate the work of the double-engine government at the grassroots level. He also acknowledged that there might have been shortcomings in the enthusiasm and energy of party workers on certain issues.“The Bharatiya Janata Party has a practice of conducting reviews after every victory and every defeat. Whether we win or lose an election, we sit down and review our performance,” he said.He added that the review process had begun at various levels within the party. Reviews would be conducted at the grassroots, district and constituency levels, followed by a review in Jaipur, he said.The rural poll results mark a major electoral setback for the BJP in Rajasthan.

headline: Akhilesh promises to reopen 27,000 schools, revive Yash Bharati awards if SP wins 2027 UP polls
content: The Samajwadi Party president, Akhilesh Yadav, on Saturday promised to reopen 27,000 closed primary schools across Uttar Pradesh and revive the Yash Bharati awards, with the award amount restored to Rs 1 lakh, if his party returns to power in the 2027 Assembly elections.Speaking at an event marking the birth anniversary of former Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, where laptops were distributed to students, Akhilesh criticised the BJP government over the closure of primary schools and what he described as the deteriorating condition of government educational institutions.Claiming that around 27,000 primary schools had been shut down in the state, he said the Samajwadi Party would reopen them if voted to power. Referring to his constituency of Jaswant Nagar, he said students had been affected by the closure of schools and their relocation to other institutions.He also accused the BJP government of neglecting model educational institutions established during the SP's tenure, citing Abhinav School in Lucknow and the school in Saifai. He said these institutions had been envisioned to provide quality education and modern infrastructure, but their condition had deteriorated under the present government.Akhilesh argued that strengthening primary education was essential for students to progress to higher educational institutions, including ITIs, IITs and IIITs. He also referred to IIIT Lucknow, saying the institution had been developed during the SP government and that education needed to keep pace with technological advancements.He stressed that educational institutions needed to adapt to changing technology and focus on actual delivery rather than slogans. Alleging a decline in enrolment in government schools and Government Inter Colleges (GICs), he said the state needed to strengthen its public education system.On the representation of PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) communities, Akhilesh said members of the grouping would also be represented in the Cabinet if the Samajwadi Party formed the government.Accusing the BJP of invoking religious sentiments, Akhilesh clarified that his party had no objection to religious discourses but opposed controversial remarks about Hindu deities."The Samajwadi Party is not against 'katha'. But what were the views expressed about the father of Lord Shri Ram, and what was said about Lord Krishna? These are the same BJP people who once made Lord Hanuman dance at their programme. Can anyone make such remarks about Lord Ram's father? What would happen if someone from among us made a similar statement?" Akhilesh said.Although he did not name anyone, his remarks appeared to be directed at Bageshwar Dham chief priest Dhirendra Shastri over his controversial remarks about Lord Ram's father.Yadav also hit back at Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and BJP leader Keshav Prasad Maurya over his remarks that SP leaders, who had once hesitated to chant "Jai Shri Ram", were now uncomfortable with the slogan "Radhe Radhe".Responding to Maurya's comments, Akhilesh said, "I would never invite him (Maurya) to my house in my lifetime."

headline: HC strikes down Haryana Government orders withdrawing stamp duty exemption for farmers
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has struck down two Haryana Government communications withdrawing stamp duty and registration fee exemptions for farmers purchasing alternative agricultural land with compensation received for acquired land. Among other things, the Bench held that an administrative instruction cannot override statutory notifications or retrospectively take away benefits on the basis of which citizens have already completed transactions.The ruling by Justice Kuldeep Tiwari came on a bunch of 113 petitions. The Bench, during the course of hearing, was told that the State issued a clarification in 2019 that no additional benefits under the Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) Policy or Section 31 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act would be admissible in cases where awards were made with effect from January 1, 2014.In April 2021, it directed special audits for 2018-19, 2019-20 and 2020-21 to detect alleged losses of stamp duty and registration fees “in respect of transactions involving landowners whose land had been acquired under the Land Acquisition Act and had been awarded compensation and initiate proceedings under the provisions of the Stamp Act.After hearing rival contentions and going through the documents, Justice Tiwari asserted the impugned letters undisputedly were not issued under any statutory provision. Making it clear that the administrative letters suffered from “several” constitutional and executive infirmities, the Bench asserted the communications were “neither framed nor issued in the name of the Governor of Haryana”. As such, they failed to satisfy the mandatory constitutional requirement. “Article 166(1) mandates that all executive action of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor,” the Bench added.Justice Tiwari added the impugned letters were not published in the Haryana Government Gazette, a statutory prerequisite for any order modifying the rules framed under the provisions of the Stamp Act or the Registration Act. “Crucially, the impugned letters neither cite nor invoke any statutory rule-making authority. Instead, they function as internal executive directives, issuing administrative instructions to the field officer,” the Bench observed.Justice Tiwari observed there was no dispute that the State Government possessed the power to rescind a remission already granted by resorting to the appropriate legal mechanism. “However, such power does not automatically include the power to rescind it retrospectively. Any decision withdrawing a remission takes effect from the date of its notification. Consequently, the impugned letters, giving power for retrospective withdrawal of the remission, are beyond the scope of Section 9 of the Stamp Act,” the Bench observed.Before parting with the order, the Bench asserted it had no hesitation in holding that the impugned letters did not withstand judicial scrutiny and were, accordingly, set aside.

headline: SP forms 4-member panel for seat-sharing talks with INDIA bloc allies
content: The Samajwadi Party on Sunday constituted a four-member committee to hold discussions on seat-sharing arrangements with its INDIA bloc allies for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav formed the panel, which includes its national general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, state president Shyam Lal Pal and Lok Sabha MPs Rajiv Rai and Iqra Choudhary, the party said on X.आगामी उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा चुनाव (2027) हेतु समाजवादी पार्टी की ओर से INDIA गठबंधन के सीट समझौते के लिए माननीय राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष जी द्वारा निम्नलिखित लोगों की कमेटी गठित की गई है:राष्ट्रीय प्रमुख महासचिव श्री रामगोपाल यादव जीप्रदेश अध्यक्ष श्री श्यामलाल पाल जीमाननीय सांसद श्री राजीव राय जीमाननीय सांसद सुश्री इकरा चौधरी जी— Samajwadi Party (@samajwadiparty) November 22, 2026The committee will hold discussions and negotiations with the INDIA bloc partners on the allocation of seats for the Assembly elections due early next year.

headline: 8th Pay Commission salary hike: Why employees want 50% DA merged with basic pay before fitment factor calculation
content: Central government employees could see a higher starting point for their revised salaries under the 8th Pay Commission if a fresh proposal to merge 50% of dearness allowance (DA) with basic pay and pension is accepted. The demand, submitted by the Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh (BPMS), seeks to make the merger a separate step before the Commission determines the revised pay and pension structures.In its submission dated 18 November 2026, BPMS asked the Commission to merge 50% of the existing DA with basic pay and pension before finalising the new structure. The proposal was presented during the federation's second-round interaction with the Commission. BPMS is an all-India federation of defence workers recognised by the Ministry of Defence.The timing of the proposed merger matters because the fitment factor used by a pay commission is applied to the existing basic pay to arrive at revised basic pay. If DA is first merged into basic pay, the fitment factor would apply to a higher base.How could DA merger affect your basic salary?Consider a central government employee in Pay Level 6 drawing a basic salary of ₹44,900.The latest DA rate, effective 1 July 2026, is 63% of basic pay, following the Centre's 3% increase announced in October. This translates into DA of ₹28,287 a month.If 50% of this DA, or approximately ₹14,144, is merged with basic pay, the employee's revised basic pay base would increase to around ₹59,044, before the fitment factor is applied.This represents an increase of approximately 31.5% over the existing basic pay.However, this is an illustration of BPMS's proposed mechanism, not a confirmed salary increase. The final benefit would depend on the Commission's recommendations and the government's decision on the fitment factor and revised pay structure.Why employees want the merger before pay revisionDA is revised periodically to compensate central government employees for inflation. It is calculated as a percentage of basic pay and is currently revised twice a year.Employees' associations have argued that as DA rises, merging a portion of it with basic pay would provide a more meaningful increase in the salary base. This is because several salary-linked benefits and retirement benefits are calculated using basic pay.BPMS wants the merger to happen before the revised pay structure is determined, rather than being implicitly accounted for in the fitment factor.The demand also brings back a long-standing debate around how previous Pay Commissions have treated DA while revising salaries. Under the 7th Pay Commission, the fitment factor of 2.57 incorporated an element corresponding to the merger of basic pay with DA assumed at 125% as of 1 January 2016. This was not implemented as a separate 50% DA merger immediately before the pay revision.Is the government likely to approve the DA merger?There is no government approval for the latest demand. In a written reply to the Lok Sabha on 1 December 2025, the Ministry of Finance had said that no proposal to merge existing DA with basic pay was under consideration.The government had also explained that DA and dearness relief (DR) are revised every six months using the All India Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers to compensate for changes in the cost of living.The 8th Central Pay Commission was formally constituted on 3 November 2025 and has 18 months to submit its recommendations. Its decisions will cover salaries, allowances and retirement benefits of eligible central government employees and pensioners.Until the Commission submits its recommendations and the government accepts them, the proposed DA merger remains a demand rather than an assured increase in employees' salaries.

headline: Cardiac arrest 15 months after buying ₹1 crore policy, insurance company denies money to widow; here's what happened
content: A man from Raipur passed away due to cardiac arrest. However, the insurance company refused to pay benefits to the wife of the late man. According to a report by NDTV Profit, a consumer court of the state has directed an insurer to pay ₹1 crore as death benefit to a woman whose husband purchased the life insurance policy about 15 months before his death.Why insurer denied money after death despite policyThe insurer reportedly denied the claim to the wife citing that the policyholder had not disclosed other life insurance policies held with different companies. However, the commission overturned the decision and called its rejection an unfair trade practice and a deficiency in service.What court saidThe Additional Bench of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Raipur has ordered the insurer to release the entire ₹1 crore death benefit. It also directed an additional ₹1.15 lakh towards compensation and legal expenses. While ₹1 lakh is intended for the physical and mental distress caused to the complainant, ₹15,000 is for litigation costs, added the report.These payments are to be made within 45 days of the order. Failing to pay the total amount, the insurer will attract an annual interest of 7% on the total amount until settlement. The order was reportedly passed on November 3 by a bench headed by President Prashant Kundu, with Anand Vergese.Case explainedThe case was filed by Chanda Pincha after the death of her husband, Pawan Pincha, who worked as a director at a private company, reported the publication. It is believed that Pincha had bought the life insurance policy on September 10, 2018 and paid an annual premium of ₹36,969.40.The policy provided a life cover of ₹1 crore for him and an additional ₹50 lakh for his wife, who was the secondary insured. The said policy was valid for 39 years, with a maturity date of September 10, 2057.After Pawan Pincha died of sudden cardiac arrest on December 21, 2019, his wife approached the insurer to claim the ₹1 crore as the nominated beneficiary.Life insurance company's claimsHowever, the company rejected her application on March 17, 2020, and claimed that Pawan had failed to disclose other life insurance policies with substantial sum assured amounts.The insurer reportedly challenged the consumer commission's jurisdiction on territorial and financial grounds. It also seemingly argued that the insurance agent should have been made a party to the case.After probing the affidavits, medical records, policy documents and correspondence, the commission rejected the insurer's objections. It observed that the company had accepted Pawan Pincha's application and collected the premium fee while it had an opportunity to verify his existing insurance coverage before issuing the policy.The bench also found no evidence to suggest that Chanda had any role in withholding information or that the insurer's decision to reject the claim was justified, added the report.Reportedly, other insurance companies had already settled claims under some of Pawan's separate life insurance policies.In the end, the commission concluded that the insurer had wrongly denied the death benefit under a policy that was still in force.

headline: IRDAI fined Star Health Rs 2 crore penalty for unfair claim deductions & rejections; what policyholders should know?
content: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has imposed a Rs 2 crore penalty on Star Health and Allied Insurance for multiple violations, including claims rejected on unjustifiable grounds, deductions made outside policy terms and conditions, and customers not being told why their claims were rejected or reduced.​ The IRDAI issued the final order on November 20, imposing the penalty along with several regulatory warnings and directions. The discrepancies in Star Health’s financial structure surfaced during regular inspections conducted by the regulatory authority between January 31 and February 11, 2022. The authority then issued a show-cause notice on December 4, 2024, and held a personal hearing on June 18, 2025. Why IRDAI penalised Star Health? The company rejected several Covid-19 hospitalisation claims, even when treating doctors had advised in-patient treatment. This contradicted their own in-house flagship policy, Family Health Optima, which covers hospitalisation expenses incurred on the advice of a medical professional. They argued that the patient's conditions were mild and could have been managed with home isolation under the Ministry of Health guidelines. Moreover, all Covid-19 rejections were reviewed by an in-house committee that cited widespread overcharging across hospitals. The IRDAI inspection also revealed that the insurance company failed to produce proof that it actually sent written explanations to policyholders justifying why hospitalisation was deemed unnecessary. .Is IRDAI a blind watchdog?.Unverified tariff discounts on hospital bills Moreover, the insurer, according to the order, deducted claim amounts using General Insurance Council (GIC) rates and “reasonable and customary” clauses without specifically linking them to policy terms or hospital overbilling. They failed to prove that formal rejection/deduction letters were sent to policyholders citing exact policy clauses. Interestingly, in the sample claims examined by the IRDAI, Star Health also deducted negotiated “tariff discounts” when paying network hospitals., arguing that it protected the customer’s “sum insured”. But the final hospital bills did not show any discount. They argued that it protects the customer’s “sum insured” even if the discount is not printed on the final bill. Apparently, the hospital sends a final bill to the insurer before discharge. If the insurer feels the charges are too high, they negotiate for a discount. The hospitals then revise the bill and the negotiated deduction is termed as “discounts”. The insurer approves the claim basis of that and then the customer gets a final copy. However, the regulator could not identify that the hospitals had actually given those discounts upfront and the Star could not verify it either. The rules mandate that agreed discounts are shown upfront in the hospital’s final bill shown upfront on the hospital's final bill so that co-payments, deductibles, and Sum Insured excesses are calculated after netting off the discount. Without upfront bill disclosure, hospitals could potentially recover those "discounted" amounts directly from patients under the guise of disallowed items. IRDAI's 90-day compliance directive The company has been directed to update their systems to ensure that every final settlement clearly states allowed, disallowed, non-payable, and discount amounts, alongside the remaining “Sum Insured”. They have also been asked to file a comprehensive action taken report (ATR) within 90 days.

headline: Punjab politics: Captain Amarinder at Sonia book launch, AAP faces ‘dhokha’ jibe
content: It was supposed to be the launch of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, but for Punjab Congressmen, the guest list told a different story. Capt Amarinder Singh, now a BJP leader, was the only political figure from Punjab invited to the event, while no Punjab Congress leader appeared on the invitation list. He sat in the front row alongside Congress veterans, and Rahul Gandhi even recalled a personal anecdote involving Amarinder and his father, Rajiv Gandhi. The invitation was enough to set the cat among the pigeons in Punjab's political circles. Was the Gandhi family keeping a door open for the former CM, who walked out of the Congress after his bitter 2021 exit? Or was it simply an acknowledgement of old family ties? Amarinder has denied any possibility of returning to the Congress, saying he attended a social event and was reciprocating Sonia Gandhi's gesture of attending three of his book launches. But in Punjab politics, even the book launch became a political event. Badlav or dhokha? The third edition of the Punjab Conclave, organised by veteran journalist-turned-politician and former AAP MLA Kanwar Sandhu, witnessed an unexpected exchange when educationist-turned-BJP Rajya Sabha MP Satnam Singh Sandhu put the host on the spot. Asking Kanwar Sandhu how he rated the AAP's promise of 'badlav' (change) in Punjab, Satnam Singh Sandhu perhaps expected a measured response. He got none. Without mincing words, the former MLA shot back: “Punjab naal dhokha hi ho gya (Punjab has been cheated).” The response drew guffaws from the audience, leaving the BJP MP with little room to take the conversation elsewhere. But Kanwar Sandhu was not done. Turning to his namesake, he added a word of caution: “Tusi vi dhokha na kha jaayo (You too should not end up being cheated).” The exchange had the audience amused. An extra power centre? A woman relative of an AAP leader appears to be taking an active interest in matters concerning the Punjab government, and not just behind the scenes. She has reportedly been calling government officers, seeking intervention in matters and asking them to address public grievances. Her calls, it is learnt, have extended to various government offices, with officers being approached for work concerning people from different parts of Punjab. While it is not clear whether she has been formally assigned any role in handling public grievances, her growing involvement has not gone unnoticed in bureaucratic circles. The development has also raised eyebrows over the emergence of informal channels for accessing the administration. With the AAP having often accused previous governments of running parallel power centres, the question doing the rounds is whether an unelected relative is now becoming another point of contact for people seeking government intervention. Three hours, and Punjab watched The death of Amritpal Singh’s grandmother brought an unusual political silence in Punjab. No political party seemed keen to comment, but everyone was watching Jallupur Khera as the jailed Khadoor Sahib MP arrived for his grandmother’s cremation, allowed just three hours at home under heavy security. The interest went beyond a family bereavement. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Amritpal won Khadoor Sahib and Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa won Faridkot, both as Independents. Though neither contested on a Waris Punjab De symbol, their victories reflected the political undercurrent the outfit represents. With 2027 approaching, no party wants to misread or dismiss that constituency. The deployment of around 800 policemen showed how closely the administration watched those three hours. The political class was no less attentive, even if it chose to remain silent.

headline: ASSAM RIFLES ORGANISES 6TH EDITION OF HALF MARATHON 2026 IN SHILLONG
content: The 6th Edition of the Assam Rifles Half Marathon 2026 was successfully organised at the Headquarters of the Directorate General Assam Rifles, Laitkor, Shillong on 22 November 2026. Organised as part of the ongoing efforts to promote the “Fit India Movement”, the annual sporting event, first introduced in 2021, has emerged as a prominent platform for promoting physical fitness, healthy living, sportsmanship and national integration. The event witnessed enthusiastic participation from runners representing various States and Union Territories across the country. Almost 4500 participants, representing all States and Union Territories, took part in different age categories, reflecting the spirit of unity in diversity and strengthening the bonds of national integration. Conducted against the picturesque backdrop of the East Khasi Hills at Laitkor, the Half Marathon brought together professional athletes, fitness enthusiasts, Armed Forces personnel, youth and citizens from diverse backgrounds. The event was attended by distinguished dignitaries from the Government, Armed Forces and various civil organisations. The Half Marathon was conducted in three categories: Cloud Chase (21 km), Pine Path (10 km) and Crystal Stream (5 km). The 21 km Half Marathon was flagged off by Lt Gen Vikas Lakhera, AVSM, SM, Director General Assam Rifles, Mrs Vibha Lakhera, President ARWWA, Mr Nitin Bhatnagar, Executive Director and State Head, IO AOD, Indian Oil Corporation Limited and Shri Arunabh Sharma, AGM, RBO, Shillong Urban (SBI), while the 10 km run was flagged off by Maj Gen Jai Singh Bainsla, SM, ADG Assam Rifles, Mrs Ritu Bainsla, Vice President ARWWA, Shri Shivesh Shukla, DGM, Circle Head Guwahati (PNB) and Mr Abhinav Rai, Brand Manager & representative from ITC and the 5 km by Brig & Mrs Swarn Singh, Brig & Mrs Sachinder Tiwari. The event recorded an overall participation from 30 states & Union territories across the country. Participants received medals, certificates and commemorative T-shirts in recognition of their enthusiasm and sporting spirit. Cash prizes worth ₹25 lakh were earmarked for winners across various categories, along with consolation prizes to encourage participation and sporting excellence. In the overall 21 km Men's Category, Mr Panchana Bera, emerged as the winner with an impressive timing of 1hr 08mins 10secs and in the 21 km Women's Category, Ms Munni Devi, secured first position with a timing of 1hr 24mins 34secs. In the 10km Men's Category, Mr Ravi Chaudhury, emerged as the winner with an impressive timing of 31mins 35secs and in the 10 km Women's Category, Ms Ruby Kashyap, secured first position with a timing of 36mins 43secs.

headline: Yash Bharti Samman to be restored, honorarium to be doubled if SP returns to power: Akhilesh
content: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday promised to reinstate the Yash Bharti Samman and double the monthly honorarium for its recipients from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh if his party forms the government in Uttar Pradesh in 2027.Addressing a press conference here organised on the occasion of the birth anniversary of party founder Mulaym Singh Yadav, he said his father, popularly known as Netaji, had always stood by people during difficult times and encouraged talent across the state."Netaji never abandoned anyone in difficult times. He always helped those in need and continuously connected people to strengthen the socialist movement and its inclusive ideology," he said.Recalling the initiatives undertaken during the previous Samajwadi Party government, Yadav highlighted the distribution of laptops to students and the institution of the Yash Bharti awards to recognise outstanding talent."If the Samajwadi Party forms the government in 2027, the Yash Bharti Samman will be reinstated. The honorarium given to its recipients will be increased from Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh," he said.Mentioning laptop distribution to meritorious students from various institutions at the event, he said distributing laptops was a continuation of Netaji's legacy and the Samajwadi movement."Congratulating the hardworking students and toppers, I want to tell them that laptops are only a tool. Ultimately, success depends on your hard work and determination," Yadav said.He assured that a Samajwadi government would provide adequate infrastructure and funds to make the law university in Lucknow one of the country's leading institutions."We will ensure better and safer hostel facilities for female students. Our aim will be to provide world-class accommodation and infrastructure," he said.Referring to medical institutions, Yadav said the previous SP government had provided facilities on the lines of the Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences to medical staff at King George's Medical University, RamQuestioning disparities in the salaries of medical personnel, he took a dig at the government's 'One Nation, One Election' slogan."If we form the government, we will implement 'One Bond, One Salary' for medical students," he said.Yadav said people were joining the PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak)and the party would make efforts to unite different sections of society to strengthen the movement.He also announced that a memorial dedicated to Mulayam Singh Yadav, whose work is going on in Saifai, would be inaugurated once the Samajwadi Party formed the government.Recalling the educational initiatives undertaken during his party's tenure, Yadav said schools in Saifai and Lucknow were developed despite criticism at the time."We developed schools in Saifai and Lucknow, but those who came later ruined them. Some people do not like good things," he alleged.He also referred to the establishment of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and IIIT Lucknow, accusing the present government of encouraging land mafia activities and failing to develop the proposed wellness city.Taking a swipe at the government's technology initiatives, Yadav sarcastically described the tablets being distributed to students as devices belonging to the "Harappan age"."Technology has now reached villages. Education must be updated with modern technology. Merely raising slogans will not help students," he said.During the press conference, Yadav also criticised what he described as the government's harsh language.At the party's seat-sharing coordination committee meeting with the Congress, Yadav did not make a direct reply."Why should I tell? Check with your sources," he said.

headline: India’s longest-serving woman top cop calmed tempers in UP’s Lakhimpur Kheri after 4 farmers were killed in 2021: Who is she?
content: At a time when women remain under-represented in the upper echelons of policing, IPS officer Laxmi Singh has set a national record by becoming the longest-serving woman police commissioner heading a district-level police commissionerate in India. The 2000-batch Uttar Pradesh cadre officer has been at the helm of Gautam Buddh Nagar Police since November 30, 2022, completing three years, 11 months and 16 days in office as of November 15, according to a recent assessment. The distinction does not include women who have headed state police forces as Directors General of Police.Born on May 2, 1974, in Lucknow, Singh is the daughter of Indra Dev Singh.Her academic background was not conventional for someone entering the police service. She holds a BTech degree in Mechanical Engineering and a postgraduate degree in Sociology. She joined the Indian Police Service in 2000 and emerged as one of the leading candidates in the Civil Services Examination, securing an all-India rank of 33. During her training at the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy, Hyderabad, she was recognised as the best probationer and received a silver baton from the Prime Minister and a pistol from the Union Home Ministry.Her professional journey took her through several districts and specialised assignments, including Varanasi, Chitrakoot, Gonda, Farrukhabad, Baghpat and Bulandshahr. She served as a senior superintendent of police before moving to the ranks of Deputy Inspector General in 2013, Inspector General in 2018 and Additional Director General of Police in January 2025. Her assignments included the Special Task Force and police training establishment in Meerut, besides the Lucknow range.Her tenure has involved investigations and operations concerning organised crime. She was also entrusted with examining the role of police personnel in the encounter of gangster Vikas Dubey. During the October 2021 Lakhimpur Kheri violence, as IG of the Lucknow Range, she led ground negotiations with agitated farmer unions following the deaths of four Sikh farmers, successfully defusing a volatile standoff, preventing wider unrest, and earning the Chief Minister’s Excellence Service Police Medal.Her service decorations include the Police Medal for Meritorious Service (2016), UP Police commendation medals too.Taking charge in Noida, she inherited a demanding policing landscape shaped by rapid urbanisation, industrial expansion, traffic congestion, cybercrime and porous borders with Delhi and neighbouring districts. She identified women's safety, organised crime, better police infrastructure and cybercrime investigation as priorities. Her approach has also attracted scrutiny. In 2023, she ordered the disbanding of women's safety units at 27 police stations after complaints of corruption and negligence were found substantiated, raising questions about how specialised support for women complainants would be maintained.Her personal life has also intersected with politics. She is married to Rajeshwar Singh, a former Enforcement Directorate joint director who entered politics after voluntary retirement and became a BJP MLA from Lucknow's Sarojini Nagar constituency. During the 2022 Assembly elections, the Samajwadi Party sought her transfer, alleging that her position as Lucknow range IG could influence the election in her husband's favour. Allahabad High Court subsequently dismissed a PIL seeking her transfer. The allegations were political claims, not established findings of misconduct.Her father, who was prominent lawyer in Lucknow, was fatally shot in the Kaiserbagh area of Lucknow on August 8, 2002, while returning home from court on his scooter. Unrelated to her police work, the murder stemmed from a dispute over a property on Sitapur Road. Following a 24-year legal battle, a special CBI court in Lucknow convicted three men, Vikram Yadav, Panna Singh, and Brijesh Kumar Yadav, of murder and criminal conspiracy in July 2026, sentencing them to life imprisonment while three other accused passed away during the trial.Laxmi Singh pushed for an independent Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe and relentlessly pursued the legal battle alongside her mother for 24 years and finally watched her father's culprit meeting their end.Singh's family relative, speaking to The Tribune, have often spoken about her challenges of working in a male-dominated profession, describing the additional difficulties of entering policing with an engineering background. Her long tenure in Noida is a milestone in women's representation, but it also places her leadership under continuing public scrutiny, the test of a police commissioner remains not merely the length of service, but public safety, impartiality and institutional accountability.

headline: 775 government schools in Karnal to be inspected within two weeks
content: Deputy Commissioner Anand Kumar Sharma said that Class-I and Class-II officers would inspect all government schools across Karnal district to review the available facilities and assess their overall functioning. He said schools had already been allotted to the respective officers and the inspection exercise would be completed within the next one to two weeks. A comprehensive report would subsequently be submitted to the headquarters.Sharma was addressing a meeting of district officials at the Mini Secretariat conference hall on Monday. Earlier, during a video conference with Deputy Commissioners across the state, Haryana Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi had directed them to ensure inspections of government schools by Class-I and Class-II officers posted in their respective districts.The Chief Secretary emphasised that the exercise should be conducted seriously and that no negligence would be tolerated. He directed the officers to carefully assess the arrangements and facilities available in schools and ensure that inspection reports were submitted to the headquarters within the stipulated timeframe.During the video conference, the Chief Secretary also referred to the Supreme Court’s directions regarding the provision of separate toilet facilities for women advocates in all bar rooms. He instructed the district administrations to ensure that separate toilets were provided wherever they were not available and to submit compliance reports to the headquarters.Sharing details of the arrangements in Karnal district, Sharma said that a total of 775 schools had been identified for inspection. These schools had been allotted to Class-I and Class-II officers, and a meeting of the concerned officers had already been held to brief them on their responsibilities and issue necessary instructions.The Deputy Commissioner further said that reports would be collected from all designated officers after the inspections were completed. “The administration will ensure that all 775 schools are inspected within the prescribed timeframe and a consolidated report is submitted to the headquarters,” he said.

headline: Agniveers can marry during second term after policy tweak
content: The Agnipath scheme for recruiting troops into the Indian armed forces has been tweaked, with Agniveers now being permitted to marry during their second term of engagement with the forces.Sources said a decision had been taken jointly by the three armed forces to allow soldiers recruited under the scheme to marry during their second term, a two-year deployment. The Army and the IAF are in the process of issuing formal instructions, while the Navy has already issued orders permitting marriage for Agniveers.Earlier this month, the three armed forces discussed the issue and approved the proposal. As of now, the policy bars an Agniveer from marrying during the mandated four-year tenure in the Army, Navy or IAF. This clause remains unchanged, sources said, adding that permission for marriage would apply only during the second term of engagement.The standard recruitment age for Agniveers is 17.5 to 21 years, meaning most recruits would not be of legal marriageable age when inducted for the first term.The change in policy follows the Union Government's decision earlier this month to modify the scheme by announcing that all Agniveers completing four years of service would first be retained for a further two years and thereafter absorbed as regular soldiers.Under the original policy, Agniveers were to serve for four years. Of these, 25 per cent were to be retained as regular soldiers, while 75 per cent were to exit. Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan had announced the two-year extension in service for Agniveers and said all would subsequently be absorbed.Soldiers absorbed as regular personnel after completing the initial four-year term can also marry once that term ends.With no personnel exiting the force under the revised arrangement, the no-marriage clause needed to be reviewed. “The service rules are made by the armed forces and a relaxation was in order to allow marriages,” a senior official explained.An official said the restriction on marriage had created social concerns. Most soldiers come from rural backgrounds. A recruit joining as an Agniveer between the ages of 17 and 21 and serving for six years could face difficulties in finding suitable matches, as marriages in many rural areas take place at a relatively young age.

headline: ‘Don’t treat employees like children’: Spotify continues Work-From-Anywhere policy; how it helps the company, money-wise
content: While most big companies have moved back to the office, Spotify is sticking with its Work From Anywhere policy, introduced in February 2021. Employees can work from home, use an office or agree on a mix with managers. Spotify’s HR chief, Katarina Berg, said in an October 2024 interview with Raconteur that companies should trust the adults they hire. She warned against hiring “grown-ups” and then treating them “like children”.That trust has a financial side. Fewer people using offices every day gives Spotify room to cut property costs. Lower staff turnover can also reduce the need to find and train replacements. Spotify has yet to disclose how much the policy saves after expenses. But here are some estimates.In 2023, Spotify started reviewing how much office space it needed worldwide. It sought to rent out unused space at New York’s 4 World Trade Center. Giving up space can reduce future rent payments, utility bills and maintenance costs. Subletting can also bring in income while a lease is still running.The change came with upfront accounting charges. Spotify’s filings show a €90 million property write-down in the second quarter of 2023. It recorded €43 million in property write-downs in 2024 and €8 million in 2025.These charges lowered the value of office assets in Spotify’s accounts. They weighed on reported earnings without requiring an equivalent cash payment when Spotify recorded them.Keeping staff for longer offers another financial benefit. Spotify’s employee departure rate was 15% lower in the second quarter of 2022. The company compared that quarter with the same period in 2019, before the pandemic.Spotify also reported that its average hiring time fell by six days. A shorter hiring process can reduce the time recruiters and managers spend filling vacancies.The policy also gives Spotify a wider pool of candidates. Its hiring can reach people who live far from an office. Employees have flexibility to move within markets where Spotify operates. Fortune reported in 2022 that about 6% of staff had moved after the policy began.What Spotify still pays forSome expenses continue even when staff work away from company offices. Spotify pays for home office equipment and offers workspace memberships to staff without nearby offices. It also brings teams together during periodic “core weeks” for in-person meetings and planning.The company sets salary bands by country, giving employees room to move between cities. Spotify kept New York and San Francisco salary benchmarks for employees moving to cheaper cities. That limits how much Spotify can save on those employees’ salaries.Berg acknowledged that working together online can be harder. Spotify worked with the Stockholm School of Economics to study how remote work affects innovation.The research also examines how people participate when working remotely. Spotify still offers office space for employees who prefer working in person.Global Workplace Analytics puts annual savings at about $11,000 per employee. That estimate assumes employees work remotely half the time. Its estimate includes savings from using less office space, fewer absences and lower staff turnover.That figure is an industry benchmark. Spotify has published no comparable figure for savings per employee. Its own disclosures show the property charges and how hiring and staff departures changed.

headline: 2 teachers suspended after 5-year-old boy gets locked inside classroom in Ballia
content: Two teachers, including an acting headmistress, at a government primary school in Uttar Pradesh's Ballia have been suspended for negligence after a five-year-old boy got locked inside a classroom, an official said on Sunday.The incident took place on Thursday at the Tirnai Maula Rai Primary School under the Nagra education block, which also operates an Anganwadi centre.The child, Shivam, had gone to the Anganwadi centre for classes when he got locked inside a classroom. He kept crying for a long time before a woman heard him and alerted the nearby villagers, who broke open the lock and rescued Shivam.The incident triggered protests by the villagers, who gathered at the school on Friday.District Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) Manish Kumar Singh said an inquiry was conducted by Nagra block education officer Ratna Shankar Pandey.The inquiry found that acting headmistress Anamika Maurya and a teacher named Antima Yadav had closed the school without checking the classrooms, resulting in the child remaining locked, Pandey said."The incident reflected serious negligence in the discharge of their duties. Both teachers have been suspended with immediate effect," he said.Rasra block education officer Om Prakash Tiwari has been assigned to conduct further investigation into the matter, he added.
