headline: Why India's highway bridges develop cracks early? NHAI engineer flags bearings, expansion joints - what research found
content: A research paper authored by a senior engineer at the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has highlighted how neglect of relatively small bridge components, including bearings, expansion joints and drainage systems, is contributing to the early deterioration of highway bridges that are designed to have a 100-year lifespan, reported The Tribune.Presenting his findings at the recently held annual session of the Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad, Dr Narwal noted that these components frequently receive inadequate attention during both the construction and maintenance stages.Who is Dr Narwal? What does research paper say?Dr Narwal currently serves as Project Director-cum-Deputy General Manager (Technical) at the NHAI's Project Implementation Unit in Amritsar. Before this, he worked in Hisar district with the Haryana State Road Development Corporation, which operates under the Public Works Department (PWD).At the Indian Roads Congress session, he presented a research paper titled “Early Age Deterioration of Highway Bridges Due to Bearings and Expansion Joints Malfunction: Root Causes, Dynamic Response and a Preventive Framework”. His research explores the factors behind the premature deterioration of newly built highway bridges, which begin developing defects well before reaching their intended service life.This oversight can leave bridges needing repairs and rehabilitation within just five to 10 years of becoming operational. According to the study, the deterioration is often linked to these supporting elements rather than the bridges' primary structural components.Drawing on field assessments of functioning highway bridges, the research has also appeared in the Journal of Indian Road Congress. It points to incorrect installation, misalignment, insufficient seating and inadequate upkeep of bearings and expansion joints as key factors contributing to early structural deterioration.“These components may account for only a small fraction of a bridge's overall construction cost, but they play a critical role in transferring loads and accommodating the movement of the structure,” he stated in the paper, the report noted.Dr Narwal's research highlights that defective bearings, whether locked, incorrectly aligned or poorly positioned, can interfere with the proper distribution of loads from the bridge deck to its supporting framework. This can create excessive stress on the structure, potentially causing cracks in girders, pedestals and other components.“Similarly, leaking expansion joints allow water, chlorides and debris to reach the bearings and substructure, accelerating corrosion and concrete deterioration. Missing or inadequate drainage arrangements further aggravate the problem,” the study states.Drawing on multiple field investigations and case studies, Dr Narwal found that a majority of the defects identified during inspections could be traced back to the construction phase. He observed that many of these problems could have been avoided through adherence to approved designs, technical specifications and manufacturers' guidelines for installation. What measures can prevent early deterioration of highway bridges? Dr Narwal has outlined a set of preventive measures to identify and rectify construction-related defects before bridges are opened for public use. His proposed framework calls for compulsory installation checklists, designated inspection stages during construction, a Bridge Completion and Commissioning Certificate and an initial assessment of the bridge's condition. The research also suggests a phased inspection programme for newly operational bridges, with checks scheduled one, three, six, 12 and 24 months after commissioning. The aim is to identify early signs of damage and address them before they develop into major structural problems. “Preventing defects at the construction stage is far more economical than undertaking expensive repairs after a bridge becomes operational,” the paper states. It further emphasises that achieving the intended 100-year lifespan of highway bridges requires a comprehensive system involving sound design, stringent quality checks, monitored installation procedures and consistent inspections after commissioning.

headline: BJP's Haryana organisational push: Smriti Irani to hold district-level meetings across Jind, Rohtak, Jhaj
content: JHAJJAR: BJP national general secretary and Haryana in-charge Smriti Irani, accompanied by party national secretary and state co-in-charge Dr Bhola Singh, will undertake a three-day organisational tour of Haryana from December 4 to 6, visiting Jind, Rohtak and Jhajjar.The visit is aimed at strengthening the party organisation through direct interaction with leaders and workers across different levels, including senior party veterans, district office-bearers, former public representatives and grassroots functionaries.The party has drawn up an extensive itinerary covering a series of meetings in all three districts. The programme will provide an opportunity for the visiting leaders to interact with both experienced organisational functionaries and newer workers, while reviewing the party's organisational network at the district and booth levels.Former Haryana agriculture minister Om Prakash Dhankar said the party was making elaborate preparations for the visit. He said Irani's proposed visit to Jhajjar was particularly significant as it would be her first visit to the district.Several organisational meetings have been planned at the BJP office, including interactions with former office-bearers who have served three terms, former state-level office-bearers residing in the district and former office-bearers of various party wings.The three-day tour will begin in Jind on December 4. Irani and Singh are scheduled to meet senior party workers aged above 70 between noon and 12.40 pm.This will be followed by interactions with district office-bearers, office secretaries, state-level functionaries residing in the district and presidents of various party wings.After lunch, the leaders will meet former office-bearers who have served three terms, former state-level functionaries and former office-bearers of party wings. A separate session has been scheduled with former public representatives who have served three terms.The evening schedule includes meetings with the minister in charge, district president, district in-charge and district general secretary, followed by a core group meeting from 6 pm to 7 pm. The leaders will stay overnight in Jind.On December 5, before proceeding to Rohtak, the leaders will have tea at the residence of a booth president in Jind between 9 am and 10 am, interacting with booth committee members and panna pramukhs.The BJP leaders are scheduled to reach Rohtak between 10 am and 11 am on December 5. District BJP president Ranbir Dhaka, an advocate, said preparations for Irani's visit were underway at the party office and workers had been assigned responsibilities to ensure the smooth conduct of the programme.Dhaka said this would be Irani's second visit to Rohtak for organisational meetings since she assumed charge as the party's Haryana in-charge. He said the meetings would bring together both new and senior party workers, providing an opportunity to strengthen coordination and the organisational structure.The Rohtak programme will begin with an interaction with workers aged above 70 from 11.30 am to 12.10 pm. Meetings with district office-bearers, office secretaries, state-level functionaries residing in the district and presidents of party wings will follow.After lunch, the leaders will interact with former office-bearers who have served three terms, former state-level functionaries and former office-bearers of party wings. A separate meeting will be held with former public representatives who have served three terms.The schedule also includes meetings with the minister in charge, district president, district in-charge and district general secretary. A core group meeting will be held from 5.20 pm to 6.20 pm, followed by an overnight stay in Rohtak.On December 6, the leaders will again connect with grassroots workers through a tea meeting at a booth president's residence in Rohtak between 9 am and 10 am. Booth committee members and panna pramukhs will participate in the interaction.The final leg of the tour will take place in Jhajjar on December 6, where Irani is scheduled to arrive between 10 am and 11 am. Her visit is being viewed as significant by the district unit as it will be her first visit to Jhajjar in her capacity as the party's Haryana in-charge.The programme will begin with a meeting with senior workers aged above 70 from 11.30 am to 12.10 pm. This will be followed by a session with district office-bearers, office secretaries, state-level functionaries residing in the district and presidents of party wings.After lunch, the leaders will interact with former office-bearers who have served three terms, former state-level office-bearers and former office-bearers of party wings. A separate meeting has been scheduled with former public representatives who have served three terms.The evening sessions will include interactions with the minister in charge, district president, district in-charge and district general secretary. The tour's final scheduled engagement will be a core group meeting from 5.20 pm to 6.20 pm.

headline: Sangrur’s waste-management failure reaches Punjab, Haryana HC
content: Sangrur’s failure to establish a permanent solid waste-processing and disposal facility, despite repeated municipal proposals, has come under judicial scrutiny with the filing of a public interest litigation (PIL) before the Punjab and Haryana High Court.Among other things, the petition seeks directions to the Punjab Government and district authorities to provide suitable land, establish an authorised facility or consider a regional waste-management arrangement at Dirba.The petitioners, Jasinder Sekhon, Sanit Grewal and Pardeep Kumar, have alleged that the Municipal Council continues to depend on privately leased land for dumping garbage, without establishing dependable infrastructure for its processing and disposal. They have contended that the authorities have failed to discharge their statutory responsibilities despite the Municipal Solid Wastes (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, and the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.Elaborating, Sekhon and the other petitioners have states that Sangrur has 29 municipal wards and approximately 17,500 households, generating around 37 metric tonnes of solid waste daily. But the city’s waste-management arrangements have remained dependent on temporary measures rather than a permanent solution.“This figure itself shows the need for a regular collection system, adequate vehicles, facilities for segregation and processing, and a lawful arrangement for disposal of the residue,” the petitioners added.The petition was placed before the Bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Parmod Goyal. After hearing counsel Shehbaz Thind on the petitioners’ behalf, the Bench fixed the case for further hearing on December 22.The petitioners added Sangrur Municipal Council in its report dated February 13 submitted to the Punjab Pollution Control itself admitted that it had facing difficulties in managing solid waste for the last five years due to non-availability of suitable land. It was further stated that the approach road to the existing dumping site was unpaved and the site remained inaccessible for four to five days during rainfall, resulting in accumulation of garbage at various collection points throughout the city.“Thus, the Municipal Council has itself acknowledged that the shortage of suitable land and lack of basicinfrastructure are directly affecting the collection and disposal of garbage. Despite this position being brought to the notice of the authorities concerned, no permanent arrangement has been made so far,” the petitioners contended.They further added that the respondents failed to discharge their statutory duties concerning segregation, processing and disposal of municipal solid waste despite the obligations imposed under the Municipal Solid Wastes (Management and Handling) Rules, and the Solid Waste Management Rules of 2016 and 2026.

headline: Punjab, Haryana fall short on farm fire management; Delhi also misses many targets: CAQM report on pollution action | India News
content: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Sunday released a report card on the performance of the governments in Delhi and neighbouring states regarding achieving targets set under their 2026 action plans for tackling air pollution.This report card tabulates data up to October 31, while the final report card for 2026 will be released January next year.The targets were set for numerous categories, including increasing construction and demolition waste processing capacity, and the number of Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS) and parking lots.Also read: RJD supporters tear down posters near Nitish Setu inaugurated by PM Modi in Vaishali; 3 held For instance, in the paddy-stubble management category, governments were given different targets for utilising biomass pellets and briquettes.Both Haryana and Punjab have so far shown "unsatisfactory" performance in this category. While Haryana has achieved 35 per cent of its target (19,66,127.75 tonnes), Punjab has achieved 53 per cent (22,02,500 tonnes).However, Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh achieved 100 per cent of their target for functional crop residue management (CRM) machines, except Punjab, which achieved 88 per cent.Also read: Carbon capture is a key flashpoint at COP31. Why it is contested & how it differs from CO2 removalDelhi achieved its target of installing 19 CAAQMS, while Haryana so far has not installed even a single CAAQMS against the target of 23.Delhi, Haryana, and Rajasthan have shown unsatisfactory performance in achieving their targets for building parking lots. Delhi has built only 15 out of the 266 lots it is supposed to develop by the end of 2026. Haryana has built nine out of 79, Rajasthan four out of 19, but Uttar Pradesh has built 21 against its target of 24.In the category of increasing city buses, Delhi achieved 71 per cent of its target, Haryana 8 per cent, Rajasthan zero per cent, and Uttar Pradesh 44 per cent.In the case of increasing municipal solid waste (MSW) processing capacity, all four regions have shown unsatisfactory performance. Delhi is at the bottom of the list, with zero increase in MSW processing capacity against a target of 650 tonnes per day.Also read: COP31 becomes longest-ever UN climate summit, EU rejects 'greenwashing of fossil fuels'All of the regions failed to set up even a single green crematorium this year, according to the report card. Delhi was required to build 49, Haryana 196, Rajasthan 53, and Uttar Pradesh 123.In a statement on Sunday, the CAQM said, "The final report card for 2026 will be out in January 2027. States and Delhi governments have the opportunity to improve their ranking by accelerating their efforts during the remaining time of the year 2026."

headline: ₹1.86 crore in cash, gold seized from Panchkula CGST officer arrested by CBI for ₹10 lakh bribe | Details
content: Days after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested a Superintendent of Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) in Haryana's Panchkula for allegedly accepting a ₹10 lakh bribe, a major development has emerged in the case, with officials reportedly seizing cash and precious metals worth a total of ₹1.86 crore from his residence.According to PTI, the Superintendent has been identified as Luvkush Kumar, who was arrested after the agency registered an FIR against him following a complaint from a businessman.CBI seizes cash, precious metals: What we knowAccording to media reports, the CBI searched Kumar's Panchkula residence on Friday and allegedly recovered Indian and foreign currency notes worth ₹24.29 lakh and ₹15.65 lakh, respectively.The CBI also recovered gold and silver bullion and jewellery estimated to be worth ₹1.46 crore, bringing the total value of the seized assets to around ₹1.86 crore. It also found documents related to six bank accounts, investment portfolios, life insurance policies, and several immovable properties.The agency also found documents detailing vehicle ownership in the names of the accused and his family members, as well as records of financial transactions.Why was Luvkush Kumar arrested?Kumar, who was posted in Sector 25, Panchkula, was arrested after the agency laid a trap following a complaint from a businessman. The complainant alleged that Kumar had sought a bribe of ₹50 lakh in exchange for extending favourable treatment to his firm in a GST-related case.In a statement, CBI spokesperson Beena Yadav said, "It was alleged that the accused superintendent had initially demanded illegal gratification of ₹50 lakh from the complainant, a partner in a private firm, for allegedly extending undue favour in connection with GST proceedings against the firm, including not imposing heavy penalties and issuing further demand notices."During negotiations, the bribe demand was initially reduced to ₹20 lakh, with ₹10 lakh to be paid as the first instalment. However, according to a Hindustan Times report, Kumar subsequently raised the demand to ₹25 lakh and agreed to accept ₹10 lakh upfront, with the remaining amount to be paid later. The CBI said its preliminary verification corroborated the alleged demand for illegal gratification. Further investigation is underway.Yadav added, "It was further revealed that the accused increased the bribe demand to ₹25 lakh and agreed to accept ₹10 lakh as the first instalment." The spokesperson noted that the agency conducted a trap operation on Thursday and caught Kumar while he was accepting a ₹10 lakh bribe from the complainant.(with agency inputs)

headline: Haryana installs 802 boundary pillars along UP border | Hindustan Times
content: The Haryana government has installed 802 boundary pillars along the Haryana-Uttar Pradesh border thus intensifying efforts to strengthen interstate boundary demarcation.Financial commissioner, revenue (FCR) Sumita Misra said that 802 of the 1,221 boundary pillars identified by the Survey of India had been installed across five districts.According to a November 13 progress report, Sonepat has installed 157 of its 173 identified pillars, Faridabad 145 of 159, Palwal 194 of 385, Karnal 181 of 302 and Panipat 125 of 202.The FCR said special attention is required for Palwal district, where a substantial number of pillars are yet to be erected. She directed the concerned officers to intensify efforts to complete the remaining boundary pillar installation work and ensure that adequate additional manpower is deployed wherever required. She said that the district administration must work in close coordination with the executing agencies to remove operational bottlenecks and expedite the work. Misra said that 2,287 paperless land demarcation reports had been accepted across Haryana as of November 17. Significantly, 143 reports were processed in just 13 days, reflecting progress in the adoption of digital procedures for land demarcation.Reviewing the SVAMITVA Urban Programme, Misra said that 237 applications had been received across the revenue, land records and consolidation departments. Of these, 40 applications had been decided, including 11 approvals and 29 rejections, while 197 were pending.

headline: Delhi to Panipat in one hour: Will Namo Bharat turn Haryana into NCR's next housing hotspot?
content: The 136.3-km Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridor, estimated to cost ₹33,051 crore, is targeted for completion by 2030. According to the project announcement, the corridor has received land-use approval from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), following clearances from the Centre and Haryana government.The proposed corridor will run parallel to the Delhi–Ambala highway (NH-44), connecting Delhi with major residential, industrial and commercial centres in Haryana.Once operational, the Delhi–Panipat journey is expected to take approximately one hour, compared with the current two to two-and-a-half hours. Travel to Karnal could fall from around four hours to 90 minutes.With 22 proposed stations and trains expected to operate every five to ten minutes, the project could make daily commuting more convenient for working professionals, students and business owners.Stations at Kundli, Bahalgarh Chowk, Rajiv Gandhi Education City and Murthal could particularly improve accessibility across the Sonipat belt.Could Haryana become NCR's next housing hotspot?Improved connectivity could encourage homebuyers to consider emerging residential locations outside Delhi and established NCR markets.ALSO READ: Dwarka Expressway vs Noida-Greater Noida Expressway: Which NCR housing corridor is winning in 2026?Abhay Kumar Mishra, President and CEO of Jindal Realty, said, “The Delhi–Panipat–Karnal Namo Bharat corridor will give a new dimension to connectivity between the NCR and Haryana. It will shorten the distance between Delhi and cities such as Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal, and help these areas connect better with major economic centres.”He added, “With fast, convenient public transport, the potential for residential, commercial and mixed-use development in these cities will grow.”The corridor could also encourage developers to introduce integrated residential communities, commercial complexes and retail infrastructure around proposed stations.Haryana's Transit-Oriented Development policy could further support higher-density development near transport hubs.Will affordable housing attract Delhi professionals?For buyers priced out of established NCR neighbourhoods, Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal could offer alternatives, although actual affordability will depend on location and property prices.DON'T MISS: From private terraces to entertainment lounges: How luxury home preferences are changingHowever, commuting costs, station accessibility and last-mile transport will remain important considerations.A one-hour train journey may still involve additional travel between homes, stations and workplaces.Moreover, the corridor's benefits will depend on timely execution, operational connectivity and supporting infrastructure.For prospective buyers, improved transport links could strengthen the long-term appeal of Haryana's residential markets, but property appreciation is not guaranteed.The proposed Namo Bharat corridor may expand housing choices across the region, with its ultimate impact determined by affordability, connectivity and sustained employment demand.

headline: Haryana showcases film policy and shooting opportunities at WAVES film bazaar in Goa
content: Haryana is showcasing its film policy, rich cultural heritage and film production opportunities at the WAVES Film Bazaar, being held as part of the 57th International Film Festival in Goa.On the opening day, several representatives of the film industry expressed interest in the opportunities available for filmmaking and allied activities in the state.Through its pavilion, the Haryana Government is presenting the state's film policy, available shooting locations and initiatives to encourage film production before national and international film industry representatives.On the first day of the WAVES Film Bazaar, Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, Chanchal Kumar, visited the Haryana Pavilion.He was briefed on various aspects of the state's film policy and held detailed discussions on promoting film shooting, simplifying the shooting permission process and facilitating filmmakers.He also expressed interest in the state's filmmaking potential and the initiatives being undertaken in this direction.Representing Haryana at the event were Additional Director, Information and Public Relations Department Manish Lohan, Joint Director Neeraj Kumar, and Assistant Public Relations Officer Vikas Mor.The Haryana Pavilion is serving as an important platform to familiarise filmmakers, directors, production houses and industry representatives from India and abroad with shooting opportunities in the state. Through this initiative, the Haryana Government is working to position. Haryana as an attractive destination for film shooting and production.

headline: Haryana, Punjab have fallen short of capital expenditure targets: Report
content: Haryana has fallen short of its capital expenditure targets by 22 per cent and Punjab by 39 per cent from 2021-22 to 2024-25, implying the states failed to utilise the funds budgeted for creating public assets, according to a report by PRS Legislative Research.The report, ‘State of State Finances 2026-27’, shows that shortfall in revenue receipts combined with limits on borrowings implies that states have less money to spend. Certain revenue expenditure items such as salaries, pensions and interest payments cannot be cut during the year. Consequently, a higher burden of expenditure cuts is borne by the capital account.In the case of Haryana, the underspending in revenue expenditure was by 10 per cent, and in the case of Punjab, by 2 per cent from 2021-22 to 2024-25.The report notes that higher revenue expenditure reduces the fiscal space available for capital investment-spending on asset creation such as roads, bridges, hospitals and irrigation infrastructure. The capital outlay was a mere 1 per cent of GSDP in Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, while in Punjab, it is 2 per cent in 2026-27 (Budget Estimates).In 2026-27, 12 states have budgeted a revenue deficit. Assam has budgeted a revenue balance (no surplus or deficit). The remaining 18 states have budgeted a revenue surplus. Haryana has budgeted a revenue deficit of 0.9% of GSDP in 2026-27, while in the case of Himachal Pradesh, it is highest at 2.4% of GSDP, followed by Punjab at 2.2% of GSDP.States with outstanding liabilities of more than 40% of GSDP include Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Punjab while in Haryana, it is around 30%.The report notes that more than 85% of Haryana’s expenditure is spent on revenue items. About 56% of revenue receipts are spent on interest, salaries and pensions.All states provide subsidies in sectors such as agriculture, power and transport. In the case of Haryana, 10.9% of revenue receipts went to subsidies in 2024-25, while in Himachal Pradesh it was 4.5%. In the case of Punjab, it was as high as 19.3%.Most states provide subsidies in the power sector, in the form of free electricity to consumers or assistance to distribution companies. About 94% of subsidies given in Punjab were for the power sector in 2024-25. Other states with a higher share in power subsidies included Rajasthan (88%) and Bihar (84%). In Haryana, 55 per cent of subsidies were recorded in the power sector, while in the case of Himachal Pradesh, it was 50%.In the sector-wise outlay in 2026-27, Haryana is likely to spend 12.6% of its budget outlay on education, while Punjab has allocated 12.9%. HP’s allocation is much higher at 19.6%. Overall, Bihar’s allocation is the highest among all states (21.7%).On health, Haryana has allocated 7.1% of its budget outlay, Punjab has allocated just 4.7% and Himachal is going to spend 6.4%. Meanwhile, five states are estimated to meet the National Health Policy target of 8% spending on health, with Delhi’s allocation being the highest at 14.1%.Jharkhand (17.1%) and West Bengal (16.7%) have the highest allocation for social welfare and nutrition in 2026-27, with more than half of their social welfare budget going to unconditional cash transfers to women. Haryana has allocated 11.1% of its budget on social welfare and nutrition; Punjab is likely to spend a bit more at 11.3%, while Himachal Pradesh has allocated just 4.4%.

headline: Karnal: Studies in government schools hit as tutors tied up with non-teaching duties
content: Regular studies in government schools are taking a back seat as teachers remain occupied with non-academic duties, leaving little time for classroom teaching.After being engaged in Census and Special Intensive Revision (SIR) duties, teachers have now been scheduled to attend a series of training programmes in November and December.The situation has raised concerns among parents and teachers, as students are yet to complete their syllabus ahead of the annual examinations. Even teachers who have not been assigned Census or SIR duties are reportedly occupied with administrative work, including board examination registrations, portal updates and other official assignments.With the winter break scheduled for January and the next phase of Census and SIR work expected to begin soon, parents fear that regular teaching may suffer further. Teachers’ associations have urged the government not to assign non-academic responsibilities to teachers and allow them to focus on their primary duty of teaching.Satpal Sindhu, state president of the Haryana School Lecturers Association (HSLA), said the association had raised the issue with higher authorities, pointing out that a large number of teachers were unable to take regular classes due to non-academic assignments. “We have requested the authorities not to assign non-teaching duties to teachers, as these responsibilities are affecting regular classroom teaching. Parents want results and teachers have also to show their results. In such circumstances, we are not able to produce results as per the expectations of the parents and board,” he said.He said the disruption had started almost at the beginning of the academic session, when teachers were deployed for Census-related work. The first phase of the exercise continued until May 31, keeping many teachers away from their primary responsibility.Before they could fully return to classrooms, another assignment was given to them. Special Intensive Revision (SIR) work began on June 15 and is still going on.The coming two months are also unlikely to bring much relief. The Education Department has scheduled several training programmes in November and December, he said, adding that language teacher training is being organised, while PTI/D.P. Yoga training is scheduled for November 16 to December 15. Primary teacher yoga training and district-level principal training will take place in the coming days. “We will meet Education Minister Mahipal Dhanda to bring the issue to his knowledge,” he said.“We want to teach, but we are not being allowed to teach. Either we are on Census duty, engaged in SIR work, attending training programmes or completing office assignments. When will we get time for our students,” said a teacher on the condition of anonymity.Parents, too, have expressed concern over the situation. “Our children will have to appear in annual examinations, but when will their syllabus be completed. The government must immediately relieve teachers of non-teaching duties,” a parent said.A senior officer of the Haryana Secondary Education Department said that teachers had been assigned Census and SIR duties but were conducting surveys after school hours. “We tried our best to ensure that students’ studies do not suffer. Efforts will be made in coming days to ensure that classroom teaching is not affected,” he added.

headline: Shimla’s Heritage Beauty Lost in a Web of Wires; New Law Targets Cable Operators
content: Shimla: The picturesque beauty of Shimla, renowned for its heritage buildings and scenic surroundings, is increasingly being overshadowed by a tangled network of overhead electricity wires, internet cables and television connections. What should be an attractive urban landscape is gradually turning into a maze of hanging cables, raising concerns over visual pollution, public safety and the preservation of the town’s heritage character. The problem is not limited to the state capital. Several other urban centres across Himachal Pradesh, including Dharamshala, Mandi, Solan, Hamirpur, Bilaspur, Una and Kullu, are also grappling with the growing menace of unregulated overhead cables. With multiple internet service providers, telecommunications companies and cable television operators expanding their networks, electricity poles and building facades have increasingly become crowded with wires installed without any uniform arrangement. In Shimla, the situation is particularly noticeable in commercial and residential localities such as Lower Bazaar, Sanjauli, Dhalli, Chhota Shimla and other congested parts of the town. Wires criss-cross streets, hang loosely from poles, stretch between buildings and, at several places, remain suspended at inconvenient heights. Abandoned cables that are no longer in use often continue to occupy space, adding to the visual clutter. For a city that attracts tourists throughout the year because of its architectural heritage and natural surroundings, the uncontrolled spread of such infrastructure presents an unpleasant picture. The tangled cables frequently obscure building facades and diminish the visual appeal of streets, markets and prominent public spaces. The situation is equally concerning in other hill towns, where narrow roads, congested markets and densely populated localities leave little room for poorly maintained overhead infrastructure. Apart from affecting the appearance of towns, loosely hanging wires can obstruct pedestrians, create difficulties for vehicles and pose potential safety risks, particularly during storms, heavy rainfall and snowfall. Recognising the growing problem, the Himachal Pradesh government has taken a legislative step to regulate the installation of overhead cables and strengthen the powers of urban local bodies.

headline: Chandigarh man shares first-month Blinkit earnings of ₹39,000, offers advice to aspiring delivery partners
content: A Chandigarh-based man has shared his experience of working as a delivery partner with quick-commerce platform Blinkit, revealing that he earned approximately ₹39,000 during his first month. He also shared some insights for those considering similar jobs, pointing to factors such as working hours, location and physical stamina that can influence the experience.In a post on Reddit, the man described his initial month on the job as a fairly satisfactory experience, saying he had encountered no significant issues so far. He explained that he typically works for around 12 hours on weekdays, while his shifts stretch to nearly 16 hours over the weekend due to a surge in customer orders.Blinkit delivery partner earns ₹39,000 in first monthThe man said the platform's incentive structure and bonus targets were manageable. He added that tips received from customers provided an additional boost to his overall earnings."I've been working as a Blinkit Delivery Partner for a month now, and it's been pretty decent so far, nothing much to complain about. I work in Chandigarh, so navigating sectors and houses is pretty easy, the Pay is alright, I've made around 39k this first month because Saturdays and Sundays were PACKED," he wrote. Why does he recommend renting an electric vehicle? The delivery partner also advised people using petrol-powered two-wheelers to consider switching to rented electric vehicles (EVs) for deliveries. According to him, transporting bulky or heavy orders on a regular bike can be challenging. He believes an electric vehicle could make the job more convenient, particularly when handling heavier deliveries.He described the work as a potentially worthwhile income opportunity, especially for those seeking part-time employment. However, he warned that the physical demands should not be overlooked, as spending 12 hours or longer riding around the city every day can become exhausting.The man also revealed that he intends to put aside his earnings to purchase a new smartphone before eventually investing in an upgraded bike. Why does he think Chandigarh is suitable for delivery partners? Highlighting the role of location in determining the overall experience, the man said delivery partners working in cities with better urban planning could find it easier to complete orders. He cited Chandigarh as an example, explaining that its organised sectors and relatively easy navigation help keep delivery trips short and manageable. He also mentioned receiving generous tips from customers in the city. "If your city is a smartly planned like Chandigarh, you could definitely look to become one, since it's easy to navigate traffic and houses here; my trips are short and smooth. And since the residents are wealthy as hell too, i often get good tips as well. Tho, if you're weak physically, I think it might be too much for you. Since 12 hours of constant work can get to people," he added. (Disclaimer: This article is based on a viral social media post and online reactions. LiveMint cannot independently verify the authenticity of the content and does not claim or endorse it.)

headline: 'Insulting India abroad': Nitin Nabin lashes out at Rahul Gandhi over his remarks in US
content: Chandigarh: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of "insulting" the country abroad, alleging the Lok Sabha leader of opposition is pained by India's progress. .Nabin kicked-off the saffron party's campaign for the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation elections slated for December, addressing a gathering of workers and officer bearers at the Ramlila Ground here. The election of councillors for 35 wards of Chandigarh Municipal Corporation will be held on December 23, and votes will be counted on December 26. .During his address, Nabin asserted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the country is taking significant strides forward. "There was a time when India was considered among the 'fragile five' economies... today, India has emerged as the fourth largest economy in the world." .Targeting Congress and its leaders, the BJP chief alleged they go abroad only to "insult this soil". ."They are pained by development, by the pace of India's progress, and, in an attempt to mislead people, they claim India's economy is a disaster. They insult this soil," he said, in an apparent reference to Rahul Gandhi's remarks during his recent visit to the US. .L K Advani was clear that opposition would support government on security issues: Nitin Nabin."Rahul ji, even the World Bank admits that under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, nearly 50 crore Indian families have been pulled out of poverty and made self-reliant. ."The Asian Development Bank says it too. The International Monetary Fund says India's growth rate is set to make it the fastest-growing country," Nabin asserted. .However, these figures -- shared by acclaimed international institutions -- are not acknowledged by the Congress and its leaders, he claimed. ."I will tell you why he (Rahul Gandhi) does not believe them: because he does not see his own development, he does not see the development of his family, or his party. He has no interest in the development of the country. His interest lies in selfish gains," Nabin lashed out. .Rahul Gandhi, during an interaction at Columbia University in New York earlier this week, claimed India is sitting on an "economic disaster" with massive unemployment, a broken manufacturing base and deep-rooted problems in the education system.

headline: Hosts Chandigarh Clinch Both Boys' and Girls' Titles in Softball at 70th National School Games; 34 Teams from 17 States and UTs Participate
content: Chandigarh, November 22, 2026:Host Chandigarh emerged as the overall winner in both the Under-19 Boys’ and Girls’ categories of Softball at the 70th National School Games (2026–27), which concluded today with the closing ceremony at Government Model Senior Secondary School (GMSSS), Sector 37-B, Chandigarh. Organised by the Department of School Education, Chandigarh Administration, the five-day championship witnessed participation from 34 teams representing 17 States and Union Territories, with around 650 players, coaches, team managers and officials taking part. Chandigarh secured the first position in both categories, followed by Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra in the Boys’ category, while Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh secured the second and third positions, respectively, in the Girls’ category. The final standings of the championship were as follows: Boys’ Category – Top Eight1. Chandigarh2. Chhattisgarh3. Maharashtra4. Haryana5. Andhra Pradesh6. Odisha7. Delhi8. Rajasthan Girls’ Category – Top Eight1. Chandigarh2. Maharashtra3. Chhattisgarh4. Odisha5. Haryana6. Telangana7. Rajasthan8. Kerala The closing ceremony was attended by Chief Guest Ms. Neena Kalia, Deputy Director School Education-I, and Guest of Honour Ms. Bindu Arora, Deputy Director School Education-II. SGFI Field Officer Sh. Dronveer Singh Yadav and SGFI Observer Sh. Amarjeet Kumar Sharma, Secretary General, SGFI, were also present. headline: Chandigarh: Nabin in city today, to kick-off BJP’s campaign | Hindustan Times
content: With the countdown beginning for the municipal corporation (MC) elections slated December 23, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has stepped up its political mobilisation in Chandigarh, setting an ambitious target of winning all 35 wards.To this end, the party is bringing senior leaders from Delhi to oversee its campaign. On Sunday, the party’s national president Nitin Nabin will formally kick-start the campaign with a workers’ conference at Ramlila Ground, Sector 27.Ahead of Nabin’s visit, city unit president Jatinder Pal Malhotra, party in-charge Mahendra Pandey, election in-charge and BJP MLA from Delhi’s Malviya Nagar Satish Upadhyay, and senior leader Sanjay Tandon addressed a press conference on Saturday.“The party will register a historic victory on all seats in Chandigarh,” said Tandon.The contest is crucial for it is being seen as a semi-final ahead of the Punjab assembly elections due in 2027. The performance of political parties in the city could offer an indication of their urban voter support, organisational strength and ability to mobilise cadres ahead of the Punjab electoral battle. Chandigarh is a Union Territory and has a separate electoral contest, but its political trends are likely to be closely watched by parties preparing for Punjab.Ownership rights to be BJP’s key poll pitchSeeking to project the issue of ownership rights as a major achievement, Tandon said the BJP had consistently taken up the demand of Chandigarh residents living in houses allotted under rehabilitation schemes.“Our party leaders and workers took up the matter with the Centre in Delhi and held sustained discussions with the administrator. As a result of these efforts, the way has now been cleared for granting ownership rights to nearly 13,000 families,” he said.He added that the process would be extended in phases, with the next phase expected within six months to cover residents holding general power of attorney (GPA) documents.Meanwhile, the BJP leadership said its election manifesto, or Sankalp Patra, would be prepared through public participation rather than discussions confined to the party office.Malhotra said suggestions would be invited from resident welfare associations, market associations, social organisations and ordinary residents. The party intends to seek feedback on civic amenities, adoption of modern technology, digitisation and improvements in the functioning of the MC.The party currently has the highest number of councillors in the House. While the party had won 20 of the 26 wards in the 2016 civic elections, AAP emerged as the single-largest party in the 2021 elections to the expanded 35-member House, winning 14 seats against the BJP’s 12 and Congress’s eight.The BJP managed to retain the mayor’s post in four of the five annual mayoral elections during the current House’s tenure, with the exception being 2024, when AAP’s Kuldeep Kumar was declared elected following the Supreme Court’s intervention in the controversial mayoral election.

headline: Chandigarh: PU confers degrees on 887 law students | Hindustan Times
content: Panjab University (PU) conferred degrees on 887 graduates and postgraduates at its eighth Law Convocation on Saturday, with students from the University Institute of Legal Studies (UILS), department of laws and regional centres at Ludhiana, Hoshiarpur and Muktsar receiving their degrees.Justice Augustine George Masih, Judge of the Supreme Court of India, attended the ceremony as the chief guest, while Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra, Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana high court, was the guest of honour. University authorities, high court judges, faculty members, graduating students and their families also attended the ceremony.Addressing the graduates, Justice Masih congratulated the students and their families and urged young lawyers to take responsibility for their professional journeys and work towards their goals. He emphasised that constitutional values, particularly liberty and equality, must guide the legal profession. Advising graduates to gain practical experience, he encouraged them to spend time in courts, choose their professional associates carefully and make effective use of their time. Stressing the importance of continuous learning, he cautioned against assuming that one knows everything. He said a good lawyer must understand the responsibilities associated with the profession and not merely know the law.Justice Mishra congratulated the graduates and said a new chapter in their lives had begun. Drawing on his professional experience, he observed that law could not be learnt from books alone but also required practical exposure to court proceedings and interaction with society. He advised young lawyers to observe court proceedings, listen carefully and remain calm while dealing with professional challenges. “Respect and honesty are the ornaments of a lawyer,” he said.In her welcome address, PU vice-chancellor (V-C) Meenakshi Goyal highlighted the role of legal education in shaping society. She said a convocation marked not only the culmination of academic engagement but also the beginning of a new journey. Emphasising the responsibility and public trust associated with the legal profession, she urged graduates to uphold integrity, compassion, fairness and commitment to justice. She added that the strength of the legal system depended not only on its laws and institutions but also on the character, independence and ethical conduct of those serving it.Of the 887 degree recipients, 414 were from UILS, 275 from the department of laws, 101 from the regional centre, Ludhiana, 72 from the regional centre, Hoshiarpur, and 25 from the regional centre, Muktsar.At UILS, 360 students received BA/BCom LLB degrees and 54 were awarded LLM degrees. The department of laws had 255 LLB and 20 LLM graduates.At the regional centre, Ludhiana, 56 students received BA LLB degrees, 35 received LLB degrees and 10 were awarded LLM degrees. At Hoshiarpur, the recipients included 39 BA LLB, 15 LLB and 18 LLM graduates. All 25 graduates from the Muktsar centre were awarded LLB degrees.The Prof DN Jauhar Gold Medal for academic excellence was awarded to Ritika.The convocation was jointly organised by UILS, headed by director Shruti Bedi, and the department of laws, headed by chairperson prof Vandana Arora.Tales of grit“I want to become a judge and establish my own identity. In small towns, girls’ education is often not given enough priority, but my father always encouraged me to pursue higher studies. Through my journey, I want to inspire other girls to follow their dreams and realise the importance of education.”— Urvashi Chaudhary“I have faced around 70-80 fractures because of my bone condition, but I never let it stop me from pursuing my dreams. After completing my law degree from PU, I am now practising at the Ropar district courts. I want to prove my abilities through my preparation, arguments and work in court.”— RishuDespite having a 64% disability, I never gave up on my dreams. I believe students with disabilities should get equal opportunities, better accessibility and proper information about government schemes. I am now preparing for the judiciary and want to build my career in the legal field.”— Harsifat S Nanda

headline: PGI bags silver for research excellence
content: Chandigarh: PGIMER has bagged the Silver Category Award for Health Research Excellence under Publication Evaluation Metrics at the 3rd DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit 2026, securing the distinction for the second consecutive year.The award was presented at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on November 17 by ICMR director general and DHR secretary Dr Rajiv Bahl. Dr Prateek Bhatia, faculty in-charge of PGIMER’s MERC Cell, received it on behalf of the institute.The honour recognises PGIMER’s performance in research publications and academic work.Pic captionDr Prateek Bhatia receives the award on behalf of PGIMER at the DHR-ICMR summit in New Delhi.

headline: ED Summons Seven Punjab IAS, IPS Officers As DIG Bhullar Corruption Probe Widens
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned seven serving and retired Punjab government officials, including senior IAS, IPS and PCS officers, as its money-laundering investigation into suspended Deputy Inspector General Harcharan Singh Bhullar expands into the state’s administrative and police establishment. The summons, reported on November 22, mark a significant development in the investigation into alleged bribery, illegal financial dealings and misuse of official positions involving Bhullar and his suspected middleman, Krishanu Sharda. Five serving officers and two retired bureaucrats have been directed to appear before the ED’s Chandigarh office between November 23 and November 27. Those summoned include Ludhiana Police Commissioner Swapan Sharma, Fazilka Senior Superintendent of Police Gagan Ajit Singh and senior officials from Punjab’s Health and General Administration departments. Investigators are examining whether Sharda acted as an intermediary to secure official favours, influence transfers and facilitate government decisions in exchange for money. headline: Sirsa MLA Gokul Setia writes to Haryana CM Saini in blood, detained during protest
content: With Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini in Sirsa district on Sunday to attend a marathon in Kalanwali and chair a meeting of the District Grievance Redressal Committee in Sirsa, Congress MLA Gokul Setia was detained during a protest after writing a letter in his blood to the Chief Minister over the city’s civic problems.Setia had announced a day earlier that he would sit at Shaheed Bhagat Singh Chowk at 9 am on Sunday and write the letter using his blood to draw the government’s attention to Sirsa’s "deteriorating" condition.“Sirsa is shedding tears of blood, but the government is unable to see the city’s plight,” he said.The MLA had also shared a video on Friday showing him allegedly pulling up a road surface with his bare hands, accusing officials of corruption and poor-quality construction.Setia claimed that garbage was scattered across the city, water supply and sewerage systems were in poor condition, and sanitation work had come to a halt. He also raised concerns over the poor condition of the Auto Market and lack of water in canals.He said he had submitted files for six-seven development projects in his constituency to the Chief Minister around five months ago, but none had been implemented. He also accused officials of failing to act on public issues.Asked about Setia’s blood-written letter during his visit to Kalanwali, Saini said he would discuss the matter after reaching Sirsa.Addressing the marathon, the Chief Minister said more than 1.40 lakh people had registered for the event. He said the fight against drugs was a shared responsibility of families, schools, hospitals and society, and warned drug traffickers to either quit the illegal trade or leave Haryana.

headline: Haryana CM Saini Lays Foundation Stone for Ambala Ram Temple Complex
content: Haryana CM Lays Foundation for Ram Temple and Infrastructure Projects Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini performed the Bhoomi Pujan and laid the foundation stone for the Ram temple complex in Ambala on Saturday, according to the Haryana Chief Minister's Office (CMO). On the occasion, Saini announced a contribution of Rs 51 lakh towards the construction of the temple complex. Earlier, on November 15, CM Saini unveiled a slew of public infrastructure projects worth 44.83 crore rupees across the Pipli, Ladwa, and Thanesar regions, aimed at strengthening local power grids, healthcare access, and urban sanitation. During a visit to Pipli, Saini offered prayers at the historic Neeldhari Gurudwara Pipli Sahib, invoking blessings for the social harmony, peace, and economic prosperity of the state's residents, and formally inaugurated four completed projects valued at 13.36 crore rupees, while the foundation stones were laid for two projects worth Rs 31.474 crore. Meanwhile, newly operational assets include 33 KV electrical substations in Sector-28, Kurukshetra, and Jogna Khera, engineered to curb power fluctuations and stabilise regional grid capacity. Furthermore, new sub-health facilities were inaugurated in Mirzapur and Dayalpur villages, each built at an investment of 55.50 lakh rupees to expand primary healthcare delivery at the grassroots level. Building on the inaugurated works, Saini laid the foundation stones for two major infrastructural undertakings totalling 31.47 crore rupees. Among them is a comprehensive sewerage network paired with a 6.50 million-litre-per-day (MLD) intermediate pumping station, designed to resolve long-standing drainage and wastewater management challenges in Pipli, Beed Pipli, and surrounding residential colonies along the Pipli-Ladwa corridor. A second foundation stone was laid for the extensive renovation, structural improvement, and aesthetic beautification of KDB Road in Thanesar. The project spans the critical arterial stretch from the GT Road intersection at the Sector 2/3 dividing line up to Udham Singh Chowk, a move local civic authorities expect to ease traffic congestion and modernise urban transit corridors in the district.

headline: Haryana grants protected status to 5,000-year-old Harappan-era Kharar Alipur mound in Hisar district
content: The Haryana Government has declared a 5,000-year-old Harappan archaeological site at Kharar Alipur village of Hisar district, contemporary to the ancient Rakhigarhi settlement, as a state-protected monument.The government has brought 46 kanal and 11 marla of land comprising the mound under statutory protection under Section 4(3) of the Haryana Ancient and Historical Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1964. A notification to this effect was issued on November 19.Dr Narender Parmar, Deputy Director, Department of Archaeology and Museums, said the site was contemporary to the Harappan-era Rakhigarhi. Located about 45 km apart, the two sites might have been linked, with Rakhigarhi serving as a major urban centre and the Kharar Alipur mound possibly functioning as a satellite settlement.“Some archaeologists have carried out exploratory work at the mound, but no excavation has been undertaken so far. We hope to begin excavation at the site in the near future. As a first step, the government has notified the land as protected to preserve evidence that appears to be linked to the Saraswati-Sindhu Civilisation,” Dr Parmar said.The notification prohibits unauthorised excavation, construction and encroachment on the protected land.Dinesh Sheoran, former sarpanch of Rakhigarhi village who has been associated with archaeological work in the area, said noted archaeologist Prof Ravindra Nath Singh had referred to the Kharar Alipur mound in his writings. Subsequently, other scholars, including an archaeologist from Deccan College, Pune, also explored the site.“However, no excavation has been carried out here till date,” he said, adding that the government's decision to preserve and protect the site was a welcome step.He said scientific excavation could uncover pottery, tools, ornaments, household structures and other artefacts, offering insights into the lifestyle, food habits, housing patterns and trade networks of people who lived in the region during the Harappan period.Dr Mahender Singh, professor of history at DN College, Hisar, said a considerable part of the district was associated with the Harappan culture, with archaeological remains reported from Kharar Alipur, Panghal, Mughalpura, Siswal and Khanak villages.The protected status is expected to pave the way for systematic archaeological excavations by the Haryana Archaeology Department or the Archaeological Survey of India.

headline: AMRIT Pharmacy aims to ease patients’ financial burden in Yamunanagar, says health official
content: Officiating Civil Surgeon Dr Divya Mangla said AMRIT Pharmacy was an initiative of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, aimed at providing affordable medicines and reliable implants for treatment. She said its objective was to reduce out-of-pocket expenses for patients.She further said AMRIT Pharmacy would offer more than 6,500 medicines, implants, surgical disposables and other medical products at an average discount of up to 50 per cent on their maximum retail price (MRP). “In addition, expensive generic and life-saving medicines for serious ailments such as cancer, heart disease, kidney disease and diabetes would also be available here at affordable rates,” Dr Mangla said.CM Nayab Singh Saini digitally inaugurated AMRIT Pharmacy outlets in 16 districts of Haryana, including Yamunanagar, on Friday.In Yamunanagar, an outlet was also inaugurated at Mukand Lal District Civil Hospital by Officiating Civil Surgeon Dr Divya Mangla.Dr Mangla said AMRIT Pharmacy outlets had been opened primarily on the premises of government hospitals and medical colleges in different districts of the state to make affordable medicines accessible to patients.Principal Medical Officer Dr Vipul Goyal said the outlet would remain open from 8 am to 8 pm.

headline: Delhi knows how to dress for a wedding. Mumbai, please ditch the corset gowns
content: The Delhi-Bombay rivalry is nothing new. And I’ll pick Delhi over Bombay any day (no offence, Mumbaikars). But come wedding season, I’m reminded exactly why. I’ve walked into enough Bombay weddings to wonder whether I’d landed at a Bandra cocktail party instead. Bodycon gowns, satin skirts, corset tops, dramatic cut-outs. Gowns everywhere. Even the Indian outfits have been bastardised: dhoti pants with a cape, pre-draped sarees that look more like dresses, and skirts paired with corset blouses. I love a good Western outfit. But does every occasion have to resemble a red-carpet after-party? Sorry, Shanaya, you don’t need a plunging neckline and a thigh-high slit to make a statement. And I’m not talking about Bollywood. Sonam Kapoor has been championing Indian textiles for years. Kareena and Karisma Kapoor know what to do with a beautiful saree. I’m talking about the weddings the rest of us attend. Cousins, school friends, colleagues, family friends. Middle-class, upper-middle-class, even wealthy families. Somewhere along the way, gowns became the default wedding uniform. Delhi, of course, has its own fashion crimes. The questionable blonde highlights, the over-contoured faces, the enormous diamond sets and the aunties who seem to be competing with the bride. It can all be a bit much. But at least Delhi knows how to dress for a wedding. Here, you’ll see women in embroidered shararas and ghararas, heavy lehengas, beautiful Banarasi sarees and phulkari dupattas. Someone will have a passa pinned to one side of her head. Someone else will bring out a Kashmiri shawl that’s been in the family for decades. There’ll be chikankari, mukaish, kaamdani, gota work, zari and enough jewellery to fill a shop.

headline: Nepal PM Balen Shah arrives in Delhi for first bilateral visit, to hold talks with PM Modi on Monday
content: In a first-ever bilateral visit to India, Nepal's Prime Minister Balen Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday.Shah is in India for a two-day state visit to discuss financial assistance, improved connectivity among others with his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi..Shah will meet President Droupadi Murmu and hold delegation-level talks with PM Modi on Monday..The visit is significant as negotiations are already going on between the two countries over Nepal securing additional international air entry routes through Indian airspace..According to Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the two sides will also discuss the inauguration of various energy cooperation projects and the laying of foundation stones for new projects..India-Nepal ties need a reset; Balendra Shah's visit could be the moment.PM Modi extended the invitation when the government led by Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) leader Shah was formed in March, around six months after a youth-led Gen Z protest brought down the K P Sharma Oli government in September last year..Newly elected Nepali prime ministers have traditionally chosen India for their first official bilateral trip, reflecting the weight attached to ties with the southern neighbour. The convention is not binding, however: Oli broke with it in 2024 by choosing China.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: Only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi? SC weighs proposal
content: The Supreme Court on Monday said it was considering allowing only BS-VI vehicles in the national capital as it expressed concern over the recurring air pollution crisis in Delhi-NCR during winter.A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan was hearing a suo motu case examining the regulatory framework governing air pollution. “We are clear. We want only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not NCR,” Justice Bagchi said.BS-VI refers to emission standards for all major on-road vehicle categories in India. The standards apply to light and heavy-duty vehicles as well as two- and three-wheelers.The Bench said it would examine what further short-term and long-term measures were required to tackle air pollution.The Delhi Government has already notified a ban on the entry of vehicles below BS-VI emission standards from November 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027.More than 10 lakh vehicles in neighbouring NCR cities, including Gurugram, Faridabad, Noida, Greater Noida and Ghaziabad, are estimated to have been affected by the Delhi Government’s decision to prohibit the entry of vehicles that do not meet BS-VI emission norms.The directive bars BS-IV passenger cars and commercial goods vehicles registered outside Delhi. Two-wheelers are exempt. According to the advisory, BS-VI, CNG and electric vehicles will be allowed to enter the national capital in accordance with prescribed rules and exemptions.Asking the neighbouring states of Haryana, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh to actively participate in tackling air pollution, the court directed them to file status reports detailing the steps taken to address the problem.The Bench also directed the Advocates General of the NCR states to appear personally on the next date of hearing, while appreciating the fact that Delhi's AQI had not entered the “severe” category.It said: “Why not ensure that commercial vehicles don't enter Delhi at all? But that does not mean Delhi residents do not require essential goods. They need vegetables, fruits and other day-to-day items. So everything will have to be available. What can be the alternative?“Can there be something at the border, some warehousing facility, so that battery-operated or other non-polluting vehicles can bring these goods into the city? This kind of arrangement may not be possible this year or next year. But why not have such a system in place within five years to ensure that not a single commercial vehicle enters Delhi?”
