headline: 22 weddings, 10,000 guests: South Delhi braces for major traffic snarls
content: Traffic congestion is expected on several key roads in south Delhi on Sunday as at least 22 marriage functions are scheduled in the area, with more than 10,000 people and an estimated 4,500 additional vehicles expected, Delhi Traffic Police said.The wedding functions are scheduled on SSN Marg (Bhati Mines Road), Bandh Road, Mandi Road and MG Road, according to a traffic advisory issued for Sunday.Congestion is expected on SSN Marg, 100 Foota Road, Anuvrat Marg, Aurobindo Marg, Mandi Road, Jonapur Road, Mehrauli-Gurugram Road and Mehrauli-Mahipalpur Road.The traffic police said adequate personnel have been deployed to regulate vehicular movement in the areas.Commuters have been advised to avoid the stretches, wherever possible, and use Delhi Metro to save time and fuel.They have also been asked to plan their journeys and follow Delhi Traffic Police's social media handles for real-time updates and information on diversions.Wedding guests have been requested to park their vehicles only in the designated parking areas and avoid roadside parking.The traffic helpline number is 1095, while the emergency number is 112.With the wedding season commencing in the national capital, processions, heavy vehicular movement and evening rush-hour traffic brought several roads to a crawl on Saturday, leading to commuters facing hours-long delays.The congestion was particularly severe across south and south-west Delhi, where blaring brass bands, orchestras and firecrackers accompanied wedding processions en route to the venues.

headline: CAQM asks Delhi, NCR States to prepare 2027 air pollution action plans with 15-20% reduction target
content: New Delhi: The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has asked the governments of Delhi and the States in the National Capital Region (NCR) to prepare comprehensive State Action Plans for 2027, including district-level action plans, to control air pollution across sectors. What can Commission for Air Quality Management do to improve Delhi air? storyline 1 “For the first time, District-Level Action Plans are to be formulated as an integral part of the State Action Plans. This will facilitate planned and focused implementation of pollution control measures at the grassroots level, effective monitoring of progress, identification of implementation gaps and timely corrective action, with clearly defined accountability,” the CAQM said in a statement on Saturday. Delhi records ‘poor’ AQI, minimum temperature settles at 11.8°C Delhi records ‘poor’ AQI, minimum temperature settles at 11.8°C IGNOU-Maidan Garhi recorded the highest AQI at 377, followed by Uttam Nagar at 340 Delhi records ‘poor’ AQI, minimum temperature settles at 11.8°C storyline 1 Officials responsible for meeting the prescribed targets will also be identified by name and designation to establish clear ownership, responsibility and accountability for implementation and outcomes. Based on past experience and emerging requirements, the Commission will also specify additional measures and interventions to be incorporated into the action plans. “These significant additions to the State Action Plans are of critical importance in advancing the Commission’s mandate of ensuring sustained improvement in air quality across Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas. The initiative seeks to move beyond conventional planning towards a structured, measurable and accountable framework for achieving tangible improvements in air quality,” the statement said. Delhi’s air pollution: What can an air purifier really do? | Explained Delhi’s air pollution: What can an air purifier really do? | Explained With sales surging amid worsening air quality across Delhi-NCR, pulmonologists explain what air purifiers can filter, what they cannot remove and how much protection they offer against pollution Delhi’s air pollution: What can an air purifier really do? | Explained storyline 1 District-level plans As in the current action plan, the CAQM has directed the States to define sector-wise actions, measurable targets, timelines and monitoring parameters. “The proposed actions shall be designed to achieve tangible improvements in air quality and contribute towards an overall reduction of 15%-20% in annual average air pollution levels (AQI, PM2.5 and PM10), compared with 2026, through focused interventions across major pollution sources, namely vehicular pollution, road dust, industrial emissions, construction and demolition (C&D) activities, municipal solid waste (MSW) management, crop residue management, diesel generator (DG) sets, crematoria and other local pollution sources,” it said. The 2026 annual action plan is currently in force, and the CAQM is monitoring its implementation. In September, The Hindu had reported that only about 40%-60% of the measures promised in the 2026 annual action plans had been completed by Delhi and districts in adjoining States, including Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan and Punjab, according to sources. The States had submitted the plans to the CAQM in January, and they were finalised in February. Indoor air pollution poses critical, year-round health threat Indoor air pollution poses critical, year-round health threat Outdoor emissions regularly infiltrate living spaces, combining with domestic activities to create complex, toxic indoor environments Indoor air pollution poses critical, year-round health threat storyline 1 Drone trials Separately, a private company demonstrated the use of drones to spray water to reduce air pollution for the Delhi government on Saturday. “A free demonstration was held at a railway construction site near CWG Village. The drone was connected to a water tank on the ground and could spray water over the area. Further demonstrations will be conducted over seven days to assess its impact. The technology is useful only in open areas,” an official said.

headline: Punjab: BJP launches phone numbers, QR code to seek suggestions for election manifesto | Hindustan Times
content: The Punjab unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Sunday launched three phone numbers to invite suggestions from people across the state for preparing what it described as a “people’s manifesto” for the 2027 assembly elections.Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon said the numbers were 07971943333, 9913002027 and 7508560065.A QR code has also been launched to seek suggestions from people for the party’s manifesto, he said.“We will welcome suggestions from every section and thereafter the poll manifesto will be prepared. It will be a people’s manifesto,” Dhillon told reporters here. “We have only one agenda, which is Punjab’s progress and development. It will be a manifesto for every Punjabi,” he said.The party will also send vans to villages and cities to collect suggestions from people for the manifesto, Dhillon said.Targeting the AAP government over issues such as law and order, drug menace, gangsterism and rising debt, he accused it of having “destroyed Punjab” during its tenure.He claimed that Punjab had lagged behind in terms of development and that the AAP government had failed to ensure that funds sent by the Centre reached the people of the state.The Punjab BJP chief also claimed that the state’s outstanding debt had nearly doubled from ₹2.82 lakh crore under the AAP government.BJP’s Punjab affairs in-charge Satish Poonia, manifesto committee chairman Avinash Rai Khanna, manifesto committee member and national vice-president Manpreet Singh Badal, HS Phoolka, Rajya Sabha MP Rajinder Gupta, former state president Manoranjan Kalia, former MLA Ashwani Sekhri, former Union minister Som Parkash and Rana Gurmeet Singh Sodhi were present on the occasion.

headline: Who is Sukhdev Singh Kang? Meet Punjab-born businessman who wants to turn Sonia Gandhi’s Italy home into museum
content: Sukhdev Singh Kang, who identifies himself as a 'sevadar', wishes to convert Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's ancestral house in Italy, which he purchased in 2020, into a museum and has urged the Gandhi family to visit the property. Speaking with ThePrint, Kang shared that he has not made any changes to the property and that he did not purchase it with investment intentions. "I am a sevadar. I have not bought the house for business purposes. Sikhs buy things and then forget about them. I want to tell everyone. We just have the keys to the house. We keep it clean and pay the taxes. This is madam Sonia Gandhi and Rahul ji’s house. They can come here anytime. We have not rented out the property,” Kang was quoted as saying by ThePrint.Who is Sukhdev Singh Kang?Kang, an Italy-based businessman, has his roots in Punjab. The 52-year-old moved to Italy from Hoshiarpur in 1992 and has been residing there ever since, according to news agency PTI.Kang took up several jobs, including working on a dairy farm, in the agriculture sector, and at a factory, before turning into an entrepreneur.During the Covid-19 pandemic, Kang acquired the house of Gandhi in Lusiana, in Italy's Vicenza province, where she was born on December 9, 1946.Kang, an admirer of the Gandhi family, registered the property in the name of his wife and daughter. The property has not been rented out, and a caretaker has been appointed to look after its maintenance. Kang pays around 1,000 euros ( ₹1,01,480) in annual house taxes and ensures that it remains in good condition. He also organised a paath (religious prayer ceremony) on Sonia Gandhi’s birthday, praying for her long life.What does the house look like?Speaking with ThePrint, Kang said the three-room home, located in a grey stone and concrete building, resembles a five-star hotel from the inside. He has kept the property largely unchanged, with the only addition being a portrait of Darbar Sahib, also known as the Golden Temple, in the living room."We have kept the house as it was 50 years ago. I cannot change its architecture. It still has its old furniture and small portraits of family members. The house has a very good feel about it,” Kang told the publication.Recalling how he came to acquire the property, Kang said, "I learnt from some of my contacts in Italy that there was keenness that the house should go to an Indian and a Sikh family."Since acquiring the house, he has preserved it in its original condition, with plans to eventually transform it into a museum. He hopes the proposed museum will become another tourist attraction in Italy, particularly for Indian visitors.Kang believes the museum could draw hundreds of visitors once it is fully developed, while also benefiting the local village economy. He said his wife and daughter support the idea.Kang added that his family had rejected earlier proposals to rent out the property or turn it into a gurdwara, as they wanted to retain its historical connection with Sonia Gandhi and the Maino family.He is keen to develop a modern museum at the earliest but said the absence of detailed information about the family has slowed down the process. As a next step, he hopes to meet Sonia Gandhi and her children, Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi, to seek their guidance on the personal belongings, photographs, documents and other memorabilia that could be displayed at the proposed museum.

headline: AAP to sound 2027 Punjab poll bugle at Moga rally on Nov 26; Kejriwal, CM Mann to launch campaign
content: Moga (Punjab), November 22: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) is set to kick-start its campaign for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections at a major rally in Moga on November 26, with party national convener Arvind Kejriwal and Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann scheduled to address the gathering. Ahead of the rally, AAP leaders Sonia Mann, the party’s candidate from Rajasansi, and MLA Davinderjit Singh Laddi Dhos visited the venue at Mattwani village on Sunday to review preparations. They appealed to people from across Punjab to attend the event, which will also mark the party’s Foundation Day. Sonia Mann said the rally would highlight the Bhagwant Mann government’s work during its four-and-a-half-year tenure. She said arrangements, including a large stage and parking facilities, were being made to accommodate the expected gathering. Listing the government’s initiatives, she referred to the Road Safety Force, health insurance coverage, Aam Aadmi Clinics and free electricity supply. She also cited the proposed financial assistance of Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,500 for women, improved daytime power supply for farmers and expanded canal water supply for agricultural fields. On the issue of gangsters, Sonia Mann accused previous governments of allowing criminal networks to take root in Punjab and said the present government was working to dismantle them. Questioning the previous Congress government over the installation of anti-drone systems along Punjab’s border, she asked why the systems had not been put in place when the party was also in power at the Centre. She said the AAP government had taken steps in this direction, while border security remained primarily the Centre’s responsibility.

headline: Punjab BJP seeks public suggestions for 2027 election manifesto
content: CHANDIGARH: With less than two and a half months left for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, the state unit of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) today launched an extensive public suggestion campaign to prepare its vision document for the assembly polls. Punjab BJP State President Kewal Singh Dhillon formally launched the campaign by unveiling three phone numbers and a QR code in the presence of Punjab BJP affairs in-charge Dr Satish Poonia, Manifesto Committee Chairman Avinash Rai Khanna and other committee members. Addressing the media at the party’s state office, Dhillon said that the only solution to Punjab’s crisis of drugs, gangsterism, corruption and debt is a BJP double-engine government. When the Central and State governments work with the same vision, the state will progress at a pace of doubling its growth by the day. He said that with this vision, the Punjab BJP is releasing helpline numbers and a QR code for its website so that every citizen of Punjab can directly connect with the party and share their suggestions and views. BJP Punjab will contest the elections on the issues ofaddiction and development. Our sole agenda is the development of Punjab, making the state drug-free, securing the future of its youth and ensuring prosperity for Punjab. Manifesto Committee Chairman and former Rajya Sabha MP, Avinash Rai Khanna, said that the party has issued three phone numbers and a QR code to collect suggestions from the public. The first number, 0797-194-3333, can be called directly to submit suggestions. The second number, 991-300-2027, is meant for missed calls, following which the party office will call the person back to collect their suggestions. .The third number, 750-856-0065, can be used to send suggestions through WhatsApp messages. People can also submit their suggestions through the QR code. He added that vans would be deployed across Punjab to collect suggestions from the public. These vans will carry information about the achievements of the Modi government and will also have suggestion boxes where people can submit their ideas.A committee headed by Manpreet Singh Badal will examine these suggestions and incorporate them into the vision document. Khanna said that the BJP’s vision document would be prepared on the basis of the aspirations, expectations and suggestions of the people of Punjab. It would not merely be a document limited to the election period, but a commitment made to the people, which the party would work to fulfil with complete dedication.He said that the committee headed by Manpreet Singh Badal would review all suggestions and incorporate them into the vision document. People would be reached through suggestion boxes, phone calls and messages. BJP vans would travel to villages and cities to collect suggestions from the public.He said the party was making efforts to release the vision document by next month. It would include the policies of the Central Government along with a roadmap for Punjab’s development. Our objective is to prepare a manifesto of the people so that Punjab can once again become prosperous and regain its position as the number-one state.Manifesto Committee member and National Vice President Manpreet Singh Badal, Advocate HS Phoolka, Rajya Sabha MP Rajinder Gupta, former state president Manoranjan Kalia, former MLA Ashwani Sekhri, former Union Minister Som Parkash, Rana Gurmeet Singh Sodhi, Parampal Kaur and State Media Head Vineet Joshi were also present On the occasion..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Late-Night Firing on Kharar-Morinda Road Leaves Gurugram Man Injured
content: Kharar, Nov 22: Police in Gharuan have launched a manhunt after seven unidentified occupants of a black SUV allegedly shot and injured a 24-year-old man from Gurugram near the toll plaza on the Kharar-Morinda road on Saturday night. The victim, Udit Kataria, took a bullet to the hip while a second shot punctured his car’s rear tyre. According to Kataria’s police statement, he had visited Kharar on November 20 to meet his friend Lakshay. Late Saturday night, while driving toward Morinda for dinner, the pair spotted a black SUV with a temporary registration plate parked near Rurki Pukhta village and stopped alongside it, mistaking the occupants for people they knew. The situation escalated when the SUV occupants allegedly resorted to verbal abuse and opened fire upon being confronted. Showing presence of mind, Lakshay sped away from the scene toward the Kharar toll plaza and arranged alternative transport to take his injured friend to Civil Hospital, Phase VI, Mohali. Doctors subsequently referred Kataria to Government Medical College and Hospital, Sector 32, Chandigarh, before shifting him to PGI for specialized care. Police have registered an FIR under attempt to murder and rioting provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, as well as Sections 25, 54, and 59 of the Arms Act.

headline: ECL provision requirement around ₹5k cr, no impact on profitability: PNB MD
content: Punjab National Bank (PNB) may require an additional provision of around ₹5,000 crore upon migration to the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework of RBI from April 1, 2027, but the transition is unlikely to have any significant impact on profitability or capital position, the bank's MD and CEO Ashok Chandra said.The bank had initially estimated an ECL provision requirement of ₹9,000-10,000 crore based on preliminary manual calculations.However, a detailed assessment using a digital system has brought down the estimated requirement to around ₹8,000 crore, Chandra told PTI in an interview.The reduction of around ₹1,000-1,500 crore reflects the bank's sound underwriting standards over the past six years, he added.PNB has already built up floating ECL provisions of ₹2,560 crore and maintained another ₹1,150 crore as a separate provision in its standard assets portfolio, he said, adding that, after adjusting for these provisions, the incremental requirement at the time of migration is expected to be around ₹4,500-5,000 crore.Chandra said the bank has not yet decided whether to absorb the entire additional provision in one go or stagger it over a period of time."Even if we migrate fully to the ECL framework in the first year itself, the impact on our capital adequacy ratio (CAR) will be around 52-53 basis points. From the current level of around 17.95 per cent, our CAR would still remain at around 17.5 per cent," he said.The ECL framework, which is scheduled to be implemented from the beginning of next fiscal year, will require banks to make forward-looking provisions for expected credit losses rather than relying primarily on the existing incurred-loss approach.Besides, he said, credit card and cash management services verticals are expected to generate around ₹200 crore each in quarterly profit from the next financial year.The bank has created dedicated digital platforms for three key businesses -- credit cards, supply chain management and cash management services -- each headed by a general manager to drive growth, he said.The initiatives are aimed at strengthening the bank's non-interest income amid anticipated challenges in treasury earnings and loan recoveries, he said.Chandra said PNB's credit card business, which started in 2008, had a base of around 6.04 lakh cards till March 2025. Following the rollout of its digital platform, the bank added another 5 lakh cards over the subsequent nine months, taking the total base to around 11 lakh.The bank has also launched its premium PNB Metal Credit Card Luxura, which has attracted 27,140 customers so far.PNB aims to expand its overall credit card base to more than 13 lakh, while targeting at least 30,000 premium cardholders by March 2027, he said, adding that the vertical should contribute around ₹200 crore in profit every quarter beginning next financial year.On the supply chain finance front, Chandra said the bank has built an end-to-end digital platform for dealer and vendor financing.Within nine months of launching the vertical, PNB has recorded sanctions of approximately ₹7,800 crore, with an outstanding portfolio of around ₹5,200 crore, he said.The third focus area is cash management services, which already contributes around ₹130-140 crore in profit every quarter. The bank expects this vertical to achieve its ₹200 crore quarterly profit target from the first quarter of the next financial year, he said."These are the three areas on which we are going to put a lot of focus. These initiatives will drive the fee-based income of the bank," Chandra said.

headline: Ancient Harappan Mound in Hisar’s Kharar Alipur Notified as Protected Heritage Site
content: Hisar, Nov 22: In a significant move to safeguard ancient heritage, the Haryana Government has accorded state-protected monument status to a 5,000-year-old Harappan-era site at Kharar Alipur village in Hisar district. Through a notification issued on November 19 under Section 4(3) of the Haryana Ancient and Historical Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1964, 46 kanal and 11 marla of the historic mound have been placed under legal protection, barring unauthorized construction, digging, and encroachment. According to Dr Narender Parmar, Deputy Director at the Department of Archaeology and Museums, the newly protected mound dates back to the same period as the renowned Rakhigarhi site. Located about 45 km away from Rakhigarhi, researchers suggest Kharar Alipur may have operated as a satellite settlement connected to the larger urban center. Emphasizing the need to secure archaeological evidence before systematic digging begins, Dr Parmar maintained that statutory protection marks the initial phase of conservation. “Some archaeologists have carried out exploratory work at the mound, but no excavation has been undertaken so far. We hope to begin excavation at the site in the near future. As a first step, the government has notified the land as protected to preserve evidence that appears to be linked to the Saraswati-Sindhu Civilisation,” he affirmed.

headline: CGST Faridabad detects pan masala manufacturing unit running undeclared pouch-packing machines in Rewari; four machines seized; one arrested under HSNS Cess Act, 2025
content: GST Press Release, Arrest news, Health Security se National Security Advisory, Health Security se National Security Press Release Acting on specific intelligence, the CGST Faridabad Commissionerate conducted a search on 16.11.2026 at the premises of a firm at Ram Garh Road, Rewari, Haryana, suspected of manufacturing pan masala without discharging the Health Security se National Security (HSNS) Cess. During the search, four vertical pouch-packing machines used for manufacturing of “Dhanraj: brand pan masala were found installed. Investigation revealed that the firm had neither obtained registration under the HSNS Cess Act, 2025 nor declared its packing machines as required under provisions of the Act. The HSNS Cess came in force from 01.02.2026, is levied on manufacturers of pan masala on the basis of the capacity of the machines installed. The amount of Cess not paid/evaded is Rs. 116.48 crore calculated as per HSNS Cess Act, 2025. Operating machines for the manufacture of pan masala without declaring them is an offence under provisions of the HSNS Cess Act, 2025. Accordingly, one person, who owns and operates the said machines, was arrested and produced before the jurisdictional court and remanded him judicial custody of 14 days. headline: Cut 1, plant 10; NGT to Chd admn on tree felling policy
content: Chandigarh: When a tree is cut to make way for development, is planting three saplings enough to compensate for its loss? Raising this question on the tree cutting policy of Chandigarh, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has called for a review of existing compensation norms. According to the Tribunal, at least 10 trees must be planted for every tree removed — a move that could significantly change how the city undertakes projects involving tree removal.Hearing a petition on felling of trees for the Bulk Market project in Sector 56, the tribunal noted that the environmental clearance (EC) condition requires compensatory plantation of at least 10 trees for every tree removed. It directed the chief secretary to examine the issue and consider appropriate modifications to the Tree Felling Policy, bringing the issue beyond the disputed project to future tree-felling cases across the city.The UT administration’s existing policy provides for planting a minimum of three trees for every tree removed, with at least one to be planted at the original location immediately, if possible. It also calls for preferably planting the same species that has been removed, in keeping with the city’s urban planning and heritage considerations.The case is related to allegations of illegal felling of 332 trees for the Bulk Market project. While UT authorities did not dispute the removal of 305 trees, their counsel told the Tribunal that permission for felling had been granted under the policy and 920 trees had been planted as compensatory plantation.The Tribunal sought details of approvals at various stages, including the final order of the secretary, forests, granting permission for the felling. The UT counsel sought time to place on record that due consideration had been given to the necessity of tree removal and compensatory plantation, along with the final approval.The order also brings the approval mechanism under focus. The Tree Felling Committee is only a recommendatory body. Its recommendations are routed through the department head concerned and the chief conservator of forests/forest department before final sanction is granted by the secretary, forests.NGT said the 10-tree plantation requirement should be followed not only in the Sector 56 case but also in other such cases in Chandigarh. It granted four weeks to respondents to file a further affidavit, with the matter listed for March 5, 2027.BOX1: Restricted felling to formal approval1952: Chandigarh Trees Preservation Order laid down restrictions on cutting, lopping and destruction of protected trees, requiring prior permission of the competent authority2017: Following judicial intervention over the removal of dead and dangerous trees, UT framed a policy delegating approvals for removing such trees to designated senior officials. It also prescribed planting five trees of the same species for every tree removed, including one at the original location.July 2022: Administration introduced a revamped procedure with a Tree Felling Committee, a single-window mechanism for applications and a structured approval process. The forest secretary was designated to grant final approval for green-tree fellingCurrent policy: Compensatory plantation was prescribed at a minimum of three trees for each tree removed, preferably of the same species, with at least one to be planted at the original site, if possibleNov 2026: NGT called for the 10:1 plantation norm to be followed and asked the chief secretary to consider changes to the existing policyBOX2: What Could Change With NGT Norm?Existing requirement | NGT’s guidelineMinimum three trees for each tree felled | At least 10 trees for every tree removedOne tree at original location, if possible | 10-tree compensation requirement to be followedPreferably the same species | Plantation should meet compensatory requirements under EC conditionsWhat this means: Any future project requiring tree removal could face a significantly higher plantation obligation if Chandigarh revises its policy in line with the Tribunal’s observationsYou Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Delhi Traffic Police flags 1,421 vehicles with more than 100 pending challans to Transport Department
content: NEW DELHI Flagging 1,421 vehicles that have each accumulated 100 or more traffic challans, the Delhi traffic police has sought action against registered owners of these vehicles from the Transport Department, officials said. The list prepared by the traffic police’s Zone-I comprises 723 commercial vehicles, 600 private cars, 85 two-wheelers and 13 vehicles belonging to other categories. The matter has been taken up with the transport commissioner, Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, with a request to examine the cases for appropriate action under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and other applicable rules. The Transport Department has started issuing notices to the registered owners of the identified vehicles, the police said. According to the traffic police, the high number of challans against individual vehicles points to repeated violations rather than isolated instances of traffic offences. It said such persistent non-compliance warranted closer scrutiny, particularly because it posed risks to pedestrians, cyclists and other motorists. The traffic police have asked the Transport Department to examine the violation history of each vehicle and consider appropriate action against its registered owner. The initiative aims to ensure that vehicles with repeated traffic violations are followed up by both enforcement and transport authorities. The police have also urged vehicle owners to check their vehicles’ challan history and take corrective measures, particularly if the vehicles are in use by multiple people. Owners have been asked to bring recurring violations to the attention of drivers and ensure that traffic rules are followed.

headline: Punjab: IAS, IPS officers among seven summoned by ED in PMLA probe linked to Bhullar graft case | Hindustan Times
content: The Enforcement Directorate has summoned seven serving and retired Punjab government bureaucrats, including IAS and IPS officers, for questioning in the money laundering probe originating from a graft case against suspended deputy inspector general of police Harcharan Singh Bhullar and entities linked to him, officials familiar with the matter said on Sunday.The ED is exploring their alleged links with Bhullar’s aide Krishanu Sharda who was arrested in the case, they added. The central agency has summoned the officers on different dates at its Chandigarh-based zonal office this week.Those summoned include Kumar Rahul, a 2000-batch IAS officer and administrative secretary of the health and family Welfare department. He has been asked to appear before the agency on Monday. Anand Sagar Sharma, PCS (2012 batch), staff officer to commissioner, Faridkot division, has been asked to come to the ED office on November 25, while Neeru Katyal Gupta, IAS officer (2016 batch) and special secretary, general administration and coordination, has been summoned for November 26.Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh has been summoned to appear on November 26, while Ludhiana police commissioner Swapan Sharma (IPS officer of 2009 batch) has been summoned on November 27.Two retired officers — Gurpreet Sapra of IAS (PCS) 2005 batch and Arun Sekhri IAS (PCS) of 2004 batch — are also among those asked to depose before the federal agency on November 26 and November 25, respectively.Sapra last served as the Jalandhar commissioner while Sekhri was the divisional commissioner of Faridkot, Ferozepur and Jalandhar districts.Sharda acted as middleman: EDThe PMLA case stems from two CBI FIRs filed against Bhullar and his associates on charges of bribery and alleged possession of disproportionate assets. Bhullar, who was serving as the DIG, Ropar Range, was arrested by the CBI in October 2025 along with Sharda. The CBI had registered the case on a complaint by Akash Batta, who alleged that Bhullar demanded illegal gratification through Sharda for favourable treatment in an FIR registered at Sirhind police station and to ensure that no coercive action was taken against his business.On November 20, the ED filed a prosecution complaint before the special Prevention of Money Laundering Act court in Chandigarh in which it alleged that Sharda was acting as a middleman for several government officials, facilitating transfers, postings and other official work in exchange for money.The agency stated that Sharda had developed a network of contacts in the police, civil administration, revenue authorities and other government departments. According to the ED, Sharda acted as a conduit between people seeking official favours and public servants who could influence or decide such matters.The ED investigation revealed that a total of around ₹1 crore in alleged proceeds of crime was attributable to Sharda. It also found that ₹1 crore had been credited to eight bank and post office accounts held by him and his wife between 2013 and 2025.A significant increase in transactions was noticed from 2023 onwards, when credits of nearly ₹86 lakh were recorded, including cash deposits of around ₹59 lakh. Before 2023, the total credits stood at around ₹14 lakh, the ED said.Sharda, however, claimed that the money came from hockey coaching and tournament-related activities, while his wife earned through home tuition.The agency, on its part, said the accused failed to produce documentary evidence to substantiate these claims. “The income tax returns also did not reflect earnings corresponding to the amounts deposited in their accounts. The agency is also probing UPI transactions worth ₹17 lakh received in Sharda’s Bank of Baroda account, allegedly in connection with facilitating transfers, postings and other official work,” said the ED. The ED had arrested Sharda on September 18 and Bhullar on October 9 and questioned them thoroughly. Both are under judicial custody.

headline: PIL in Punjab and Haryana High Court flags Sangrur’s lack of permanent waste-processing facility
content: Chandigarh, November 22, 2026: Sangrur’s failure to establish a permanent solid waste-processing and disposal facility has come under judicial scrutiny, with three residents filing a public interest litigation (PIL) in the Punjab and Haryana High Court. The petitioners — Jasinder Sekhon, Sanit Grewal and Pardeep Kumar — have sought directions to the Punjab Government and district authorities to provide suitable land, set up an authorised waste-management facility or explore a regional arrangement at Dirba. The petition states that Sangrur has 29 municipal wards and around 17,500 households, generating nearly 37 metric tonnes of solid waste daily. However, the Municipal Council continues to rely on privately leased land for dumping garbage instead of having permanent processing and disposal infrastructure. Citing the council’s February 13 report to the Punjab Pollution Control Board, the petitioners said the civic body had acknowledged difficulties in managing waste due to the lack of suitable land. They also flagged poor access to the existing dumping site, which reportedly becomes inaccessible for four to five days during rainfall. A Bench comprising Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Parmod Goyal has listed the matter for further hearing on December 22.

headline: Punjab contractual teachers detained after pay-scale protest outside minister's home
content: Several contractual teachers were detained on Sunday after a protest outside Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema's residence in Sangrur over demands for a full pay scale and other service benefits. The demonstration, attended by teachers from different parts of the state, turned tense as protesters clashed with police personnel, leading to prolonged scuffles.The situation escalated when some women teachers allegedly pulled police personnel back during the confrontation. There were also reports of police personnel's uniforms being torn in the scuffle.The protesting teachers said the Punjab government had publicised the regularisation of around 12,710 teachers but had not extended the full pay scale to them. They claimed that despite performing duties similar to those of regular teachers, they continued to receive monthly salaries of only Rs 15,000 to Rs 18,000. TEACHERS DEMAND FULL PAY SCALE, SERVICE BENEFITSThe protesters questioned why they were being paid significantly less than regular teachers despite performing the same duties. They alleged that the government had denied them their rightful entitlements and the full pay scale even after announcing their regularisation.The teachers also said they had been holding a sustained protest outside the Sangrur Deputy Commissioner's office since November, but their demands had not received any concrete response from the government.They said the demonstration outside Cheema's residence was organised to press the government to address their long-pending demands.POLICE DETAIN PROTESTERS, MOVE THEM IN BUSESAs police began detaining protesters, several others also offered themselves for arrest after seeing their fellow teachers being taken away. The police subsequently put the detained protesters on buses and removed them from the site.DSP Sangrur Dalvir Singh said the police had given the teachers December 3 for a meeting with a government panel to discuss their demands.However, he alleged that the protesters resorted to violence and manhandled police personnel during Sunday's demonstration, with some uniforms also being torn.The DSP said such protests were not an appropriate way to raise demands and warned that legal action would be taken if protesters continued to manhandle police personnel. He also cautioned that if such behaviour persisted, the authorities could reconsider granting them time for meetings in the future.The teachers, meanwhile, maintained that their agitation would continue until the government granted them the full pay scale and other legitimate service benefits.- EndsInputs from Kulveer SinghMust Watch

headline: Money Laundering Probe: ED Summons Seven Serving, Retired Punjab Govt Officials For Questioning
content: Chandigarh: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has asked seven bureaucrats of the Punjab government to appear before it for questioning in connection with an ongoing money laundering investigation.The investigation relates to an alleged corruption case involving Harcharan Singh Bhullar, the DIG of Punjab Police, who was suspended. The probe has found that Krishanu Sharda, the accused who was an associate of Bhullar, allegedly acted as a liaison and was involved in securing undue favours from several state government officials.Those who have been summoned to the ED zonal office in Chandigarh on various dates include both in-service and retired IAS, IPS, and state civil services officers.Kumar Rahul — a 2000-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Punjab cadre, currently posted as the administrative secretary in the Departments of Health and Family Welfare and Medical Education and Research — has been directed to appear before the ED on November 23.Anand Sagar Sharma — a 2012-batch Punjab Civil Services officer, who serves as the staff officer to the divisional commissioner of Faridkot — has been summoned on November 25.Neeru Katyal Gupta — a 2016-batch IAS officer who has been posted as special secretary in the general administration and coordination since June 13 — has been summoned for November 26.Gagan Ajit Singh — an officer of the Punjab Police Service who was posted as the SSP of Fazilka — has been directed to appear on November 26.Swapn Sharma — a 2009-batch IPS officer currently posted as DIG-cum-Police Commissioner in Ludhiana — has been asked for questioning on November 27.Additionally, two retired bureaucrats have also been summoned. Gurpreet Sapra — a 2005-batch IAS officer who was posted as the Jalandhar Commissioner until September 19, 2023 — has been asked to appear on November 26.Similarly, Arun Sekhri — a 2004-batch IAS officer who retired on February 28 during his posting as the divisional commissioner of Faridkot — has been asked to appear on November 25.These officials will be questioned about their alleged role and the nature of the benefits purportedly obtained through an intermediary (liaisoner).The investigation is based on two FIRs registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) against Bhullar and others with allegations of bribery and the accumulation of assets disproportionate to known sources of income.Bhullar, who was posted as the DIG for Ropar Range at the time, was taken into custody by the CBI in October 2025, following a complaint from a scrap dealer alleging that an intermediary had demanded a bribe in exchange for settling a case.The ED said Rs eight lakh was allegedly demanded from a complainant, of which Rs five lakh was collected through Sharda in exchange for settling a criminal case and allowing the complainant to continue their scrap business without police interference.The agency further stated that the investigation revealed Sharda had assisted in receiving funds on behalf of Bhullar and facilitating their movement.During a search conducted under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, Rs 8.35 lakh in cash was seized, and bank and post office accounts — along with investments — were frozen, containing a total sum of approximately Rs 1.42 crore, the agency said.Also ReadED Chargesheet In KPSC Scam Alleges Illegal Payments, Leak Of Question Papers, Answer KeysED Summons Punjab CS, Principal Secy Finance For Questioning In Money Laundering Case

headline: Rajiv Gandhi Model Day-Boarding School Scheme Moves at Slow Pace; No School Has Started Classes Yet
content: Dharamshala: The Himachal Pradesh government’s ambitious Rajiv Gandhi Government Model Day-Boarding School Scheme, aimed at providing quality education with modern facilities, is progressing at a slow pace, with classes yet to commence in any of the approved schools. Despite approval for the establishment and upgradation of 50 schools across 33 Assembly constituencies, none of these institutions has started academic activities so far. This information was revealed in a written reply given by the Education Minister in the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly on Saturday in response to a question raised by Vinod Kumar, MLA from Nachan, seeking details about schools sanctioned under the scheme and their operational status. According to the government’s reply, approval has been granted for the construction of 13 new Rajiv Gandhi Government Model Day-Boarding Schools across the state. Kangra district has received the highest allocation, with seven schools proposed in Jawali, Jaisinghpur, Palampur, Nagrota Bagwan, Fatehpur, Indora and Jawalamukhi. In Hamirpur district, three new schools have been approved for Nadaun, Barsar and Bhoranj. Besides, one school each has been sanctioned for Chopal in Shimla district, Shillai in Sirmaur district and Gagret in Una district. In addition to establishing new institutions, the government has approved the upgradation of 37 existing government senior secondary schools into model day-boarding schools. These institutions are spread across 12 districts, including Bilaspur, Chamba, Hamirpur, Kangra, Kinnaur, Kullu, Lahaul-Spiti, Mandi, Shimla, Solan, Sirmaur and Una. The scheme is intended to strengthen the public education system by providing students with access to modern educational infrastructure and improved facilities. However, the fact that none of the 50 approved schools has started classes raises questions about the pace of implementation and the timeline for making these institutions functional.

headline: Delhi scores mixed results on CAQM report card
content: New Delhi Delhi has scored high marks in its air quality monitoring and in dealing with construction and demolition waste so far in 2026, but fell short in clearing up its landfills, according to the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM)’s report card, released on Sunday (November 22, 2026). The Commission was assessing the performance of Delhi and neighboring States against their 2026 action plan targets to tackle air pollution. The report card shows that, while Delhi achieved 100% of its targets in setting up Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMs), processing C&D waste, industrial inspections, and augmentation of EV charging stations, it has fallen behind when it comes to setting up green crematoriums, legacy waste liquidation, augmentation of large and small Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSM), and setting up of parking infrastructure. The report card only tabulates data up to October 31. “The final report card for 2026 will be out in January 2027. States and Delhi governments have the opportunity to improve their ranking by accelerating their efforts during the remaining time of the year 2026,” the CAQM said in a statement. Delhi’s air pollution: What can an air purifier really do? | Explained Delhi’s air pollution: What can an air purifier really do? | Explained With sales surging amid worsening air quality across Delhi-NCR, pulmonologists explain what air purifiers can filter, what they cannot remove and how much protection they offer against pollution Delhi’s air pollution: What can an air purifier really do? | Explained storyline 1 Structured and measurable States had submitted their 2026 action plans to the CAQM in January and finalised them in February. On Saturday, the CAQM wrote to the governments of Delhi and the NCR States, calling for the preparation of their comprehensive State Action Plans for 2027, including district action plans, to control air pollution in different sectors. This time, the CAQM seeks to move beyond conventional planning towards a structured, measurable, and accountable framework to achieve tangible improvements in air quality. According to the report card, Delhi has achieved its annual target of installing 19 CAAQMs and has exceeded its target for inspections of diesel generator sets, conducting 1,296 inspections against a target of 539. In industrial pollution control, Delhi has completed 1,609 industrial inspections against a target of 979. It has also achieved 100% of its targets for installing Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) in the identified 90 industries. headline: Two Women and One Male Aspirant in Race for Congress Ticket from Bathinda Rural
content: The political race for the Congress ticket from the Bathinda Rural Assembly constituency is beginning to attract attention, with two women and one male aspirant reportedly seeking the party nomination for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. All three have political backgrounds and previous associations with the constituency, making the ticket selection an interesting development within the Bathinda Congress. Among the prominent aspirants is former MLA Rupinder Kaur Ruby, who won the 2017 Punjab Assembly elections from Bathinda Rural on an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) ticket. However, she subsequently left AAP and joined the Congress. She contested the 2022 Assembly elections on a Congress ticket in Malout constituency but lost to AAP candidate Baljit Kaur. Now, she is once again seeking the Congress nomination from Bathinda Rural. Another woman contender is Dr. Jeevan Jot Kaur, daughter of former Deputy Speaker of the Punjab Vidhan Sabha and former Bathinda Rural MLA Ajaib Singh Bhatti. Her candidature brings the political legacy of the Bhatti family into the ticket-selection equation, given her father's previous association with neighbouring constituency Bhuco.Mandi . The third contender is Gurjant Singh Kutiwal, a former MLA from Bathinda Rural, who is also seeking the Congress ticket. His previous legislative experience and political association with the constituency make him another aspirant in the emerging contest. The ticket-selection exercise assumes particular significance following the appointment of Pargat Singh as President of the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC). Pargat Singh has declared that merit and winning capacity will be the sole criteria for selecting party candidates for the forthcoming Assembly elections. His stated approach will put the Congress leadership's candidate-selection policy to the test in Bathinda Rural. The party will have to consider the aspirants' political experience, previous electoral performances, organisational standing and connections with the constituency.

headline: Punjab-origin Navdeep Singh Bains elected as Ontario Liberal Party leader
content: BATHINDA: Punjab-origin political functionary Navdeep Singh Bains (49) has been elected as leader of Ontario Liberal Party in Ontario province of Canada. By winning the Ontario Liberal party leadership, Bains has become only the second turbaned Sikh to led any federal or provincial party in Canada. Before him, Jagmeet Singh headed New Democratic Party from 2017 to 2025.Navdeep Singh though was born in Toronto in June 1977, but his family hailed from Mahilpur in Hoshiarpur district of Punjab.Bains defeated Lee Fairclough in the third round for the election as leader of Ontario Liberal Party by getting 50.3% votes against 49.7% votes by Lee out of 20510 cast votes. In the first round Naveep got 44.1% votes against 33.7% by Fairclough and in the second ballot Navdeep got 46.1% against 38.2% by Fairclough. He was elected on the evening of November 21 and replaced Bonnie Crombie, who had left the party leadership earlier this year.Navdeep Singh has been elected as party leader only a day after two Punjab origin lawmakers were made as ministers in British Columbia provincial government apart from four other Punjab-origin members as parliamentary secretaries.Navdeep Singh, a business executive, who remained minister of innovation, science and industry in Justin Trudeau led federal government of Canada from 2015 to 2021, had started his political career by winning the first election from Mississauga-Brampton South in 2004. He remained MP from the seat till 2011 and MP from Mississauga-Malton till 2021 and left the federal politics.He started preparing to contest for party leadership in Ontario early 2026.Liberal Party presently has only 14 seats in 124 member provincial assembly in Ontario behind Progressive Conservative and New Democratic Party even though Liberal Party had got more vote share in February 2025 provincial elections.As per media reports, Bains aims to gain power by defeating Progressive Conservative government headed by Doug Ford in next provincial elections due in April 2030.

headline: Man From Haryana's Kurukshetra Dies In Pune, Body Buried In Pit; Family Alleges Foul Play
content: Kurukshetra: A 32-year-old man belonging to a Sikh family in Haryana s Kurukshetra allegedly died under mysterious circumstances in Maharashtra s Pune. The deceased, Sukhdev Singh, a resident of Mohanpur village in Kurukshetra, worked as a cook at a hotel in Pune. He had been working at the hotel for the last over 10 years and had recently visited his family in Kurukshetra. Sukhdev s sister, Baljit Kaur, said, My brother worked at a hotel in Pune. We were told that Sukhdev was unwell and was being sent back to Kurukshetra by train on November 11. We reached Kurukshetra railway station, but he did not arrive. We continued searching for him over the next few days, but on November 18, we learnt from a relative that Sukhdev had died and his body had been buried. Baljit said the cause of Sukhdev s death is not clear. She alleged the owner of the hotel where Sukhdev worked concealed information about his death. He should have handed over my brother s body to us so that we could perform his last rites. We suspect that he was murdered and buried. We request the government to help us bring his body back, conduct a postmortem examination and take action against those responsible for his death and for concealing the facts, she said. Baljit said the owner of the hotel initially told her that Sukhdev was ill and later said he died in a road accident. She said the relative who informed her sister of Sukhdev s death sent some photos which showed the body being buried in a pit. Baljit said after Sukhdev s death, his body was buried in a pit dug with a JCB near Chalisgaon Ghati railway station, around 400 km from the hotel where he worked. Sukhdev s family approached Haryana Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (HSGMC) president Jagdish Singh Jhinda on Saturday and requested his intervention in bringing back Sukhdev s body to Kurukshetra.Jhinda said burying Sukhdev s body without taking the family into confidence is against the dignity and sentiments of the Sikh religion. He demanded that the body be exhumed, a videotaped post-mortem be conducted, and the body be handed over to the family for cremation. The committee will write to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, and the Maharashtra government for justice, Jhinda said. headline: Criticise decisions, not constitutional institutions: CJI | Hindustan Times
content: Shimla, Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on Sunday said that citizens in a democracy have the right to criticise the decisions of constitutional bodies but should avoid targeting the institutions themselves.Interacting with students on the sidelines of the 10th convocation of the Central University of Himachal Pradesh at Dharamshala, where he was the chief guest, the Chief Justice observed that people often fail to distinguish between a decision and the institution behind it.According to him, this tendency risks undermining public confidence in institutions essential to sustaining democracy, a university statement said.While citizens in a democracy have the right to criticise the decisions of constitutional bodies, they should avoid targeting the institutions themselves, he said.In his convocation address on Sunday, Justice Surya Kant drew on the Himalayan landscape around him to urge the graduating students to be patient in pursuing their goals, reminding them that the road to any destination in the mountains is seldom straight and that no one climbs a mountain alone.The convocation was held at the auditorium of Government Degree College, Dharamshala. Degrees were conferred on 702 students and 32 gold medals were presented, 23 of them to women.The 702 graduates included 584 postgraduates, 29 undergraduates and 48 PhD scholars, besides diploma holders. The university newsletter and five books by faculty members were released on the occasion.Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu told the students that a degree is not only recognition of a student's hard work but also represents their responsibility towards society and the nation.Emphasising that any country's greatest strength lies in its educated, aware and responsible citizens, he said education is not merely about securing employment; it is a means of developing critical thinking, understanding, research, innovation and bringing positive changes to society.In an era of rapid advancements in artificial intelligence, robotics, biotechnology, data science and digital technology, the education system must prepare young people not only to seek employment but also to generate employment, undertake research and promote innovation, he was quoted as saying in the statement.Governor Kavinder Gupta called upon the university to work towards emerging as a centre of impactful research on Himalayan challenges, including climate change, disaster management, water conservation, biodiversity and rural development, stressing that universities must connect academic excellence with the needs of society."Knowledge empowers us, values give us direction and determination enables us to achieve our goals. Your degree may earn you recognition, but your character and values will earn you lasting respect," he said, urging students to remain committed to integrity, humility and lifelong learning.Highlighting the ecological and cultural significance of the Himalayas, the Governor said development must be pursued in harmony with nature.He urged the university to promote focused research on Himalayan ecology, disaster preparedness, water resources, tribal communities, natural farming and tourism, so that academic pursuits contribute to sustainable development in the region.Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court, Justice Gurmeet Singh Sandhawalia, and Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri were among those who attended the ceremony.The Vice Chancellor of the university, Sat Prakash Bansal, said the university's vision was 'local to global'.He highlighted its debut in the 701-800 band of the Times Higher Education World University Rankings and its 239th place in Southern Asia in the QS Asia University Rankings, and said its h-index had risen from 22 to 86 and its patents from one to 70.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: Himachal’s fiscal deficit projected to rise to 4.99% of GSDP in FY27 | Hindustan Times
content: Himachal Pradesh’s fiscal deficit is projected to rise to ₹13,836.84 crore, or 4.99% of the gross state domestic product (GSDP), in 2026-27 (FY27), against the budget estimate of ₹9,698.03 crore (3.49% of the GSDP), primarily due to the discontinuation of the revenue deficit grant (RDG) and increased revenue expenditure.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Saturday placed this information before the House on Form-5 under Rule-7 of the HP Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Rules, 2005, for financial year FY27.The report attributes the widening deficit largely to the 16th Finance Commission’s decision not to recommend a revenue deficit grant to the state from FY27 to financial year 2030-31 (FY31). The state had received ₹3,257 crore under this head in 2025-26.The withdrawal of the grant, coupled with recurring expenditure and the financial burden arising from natural disasters, has put additional pressure on the state’s finances, the report added.“Being a hill state/special category state, HP was significantly dependent on RDGs to meet its chronic revenue deficit. The 16th Finance Commission has not recommended an RDG for its award period from FY27 to FY31, which was ₹3,257 crore in the previous fiscal,” read the Form 5 statement.The state’s revenue expenditure is estimated to increase by ₹5,237.09 crore to ₹52,175.39 crore in FY27. The increase is attributed to higher expenditure on pensions, social security pensions, subsidies, grants-in-aid, the state’s share under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), HIMCARE and court-ordered payments.Revenue receipts, meanwhile, are projected to increase by ₹3,371.16 crore to ₹43,732.46 crore. However, the increase in expenditure is expected to outpace the growth in receipts, pushing the revenue deficit up by ₹1,865.93 crore, from ₹6,577.01 crore to ₹8,442.93 crore.While the tax revenue is expected to remain at the level of budget estimates, non-tax revenue is expected to increase by ₹839.89 crore mainly due to increase of receipt from sale of power.The centrally sponsored schemes grants are expected to increase by ₹2,229.59 crore. The government has also projected an increase of ₹4,724.47 crore in capital receipts, largely on account of interest-free loans under the Centre’s capital investment scheme. Capital expenditure is estimated to rise by ₹2,304.43 crore to ₹10,292.30 crore, with spending planned on infrastructure development, water supply, railways, roads, schools and hospitals, besides compensation payments in compliance with court orders.To contain the fiscal stress, the government has proposed measures to augment tax and non-tax revenue, including through cesses and e-auctioning of toll barriers. It also plans to mobilise central assistance, explore externally aided projects, utilise permissible borrowings for development works, rationalise institutions and curb unproductive expenditure.

headline: Kangra district proposal triggers differences in Himachal Congress
content: The proposal to create new districts in Himachal Pradesh has exposed differences within the ruling Congress, with ministers and legislators from Kangra, Shimla and Mandi taking different positions on the proposed administrative reorganisation. The disagreement has centred particularly on Kangra, the state’s largest district, where some Congress legislators have supported carving out new districts while others have opposed any division. The issue was discussed at a Congress Legislature Party meeting in Dharamsala, where differences among Kangra legislators reportedly led to heated exchanges. Ayurveda Minister Yadvinder Goma, Palampur MLA Ashish Butail and Fatehpur MLA Bhawani Pathania have supported examining the creation of new districts, citing administrative convenience and the difficulties faced by residents of geographically distant areas. On the other side, Nagrota Bagwan MLA Raghubir Singh Bali has opposed dividing Kangra, maintaining that the district’s historical and cultural identity should be preserved. Jwalamukhi MLA Sanjay Rattan has also expressed reservations about the proposal. Kangra has 15 Assembly constituencies and is the largest district in Himachal Pradesh. The demand for its reorganisation includes proposals for separate administrative districts around Palampur, Dehra and Nurpur. Supporters of the proposal argue that residents in several areas have to travel considerable distances for administrative work and that separate district headquarters could improve access to government services. Goma has supported the proposal to examine a separate district covering Jaisinghpur, Palampur, Sulah and Baijnath. Butail has also advocated a separate Palampur district, arguing that the region has geographical and administrative reasons to seek district status. Both have indicated that their positions would be presented before the government-appointed commission examining the matter. Bali, however, has maintained that administrative facilities can be improved without dividing Kangra. He has opposed the proposal on the grounds that the district’s identity should remain intact. The differences have also involved discussions over which areas should be included in any proposed new district. A Congress insider, speaking on condition of anonymity, said legislators had different views on the proposal. “There are leaders supporting new districts and others opposing the division of Kangra. Every legislator is presenting the concerns of his constituency. The party has not arrived at a common position,” the insider said.

headline: Key Palampur-Hamirpur link neglected for decades
content: The 70-km-long Palampur-Hamirpur state highway, one of the busiest roads in the region, is in a state of neglect, with commuters facing perennial traffic congestion and safety risks on its narrow and winding stretches.The highway connects Palampur with Hamirpur, Bilaspur, Una, Shimla, Chandigarh and New Delhi. Despite a manifold increase in traffic over the past three decades, the road has not been widened. There is an urgent need to upgrade it to accommodate the growing volume of vehicles and ensure safer travel.With the opening of the Kiratpur-Manali four-lane highway, the Palampur-Hamirpur route has assumed greater significance. It has emerged as one of the shortest routes for residents of Palampur, Baijnath and neighbouring towns travelling towards Chandigarh and New Delhi.The distance between Palampur and Chandigarh has reduced by around 60 km via the Palampur-Hamirpur-Ghumarwin-Kiratpur route, bringing down the journey time from around six hours to four-and-a-half hours. However, the narrow highway causes inconvenience to commuters and increases the risk of accidents.The stretch between Bhawarna and Hamirpur is riddled with potholes, making driving difficult. Despite repeated complaints, the Executive Engineers of the PWD’s Palampur and Hamirpur circles have failed to ensure proper repairs to the road.Successive state governments have failed to take concrete steps to widen the road or secure its upgradation under the National Highway programme. In 2017, the Union Government had declared the road a national highway but subsequently withdrew the notification.BM Thakur, Superintending Engineer of the Himachal Pradesh Public Works Department (HPPWD), told The Tribune that the department had already submitted a Detailed Project Report (DPR) to the Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, seeking Rs 187 crore for upgrading the 70-km stretch into a two-lane road.Palampur MLA Ashish Butail and Sullah MLA Vipin Singh Parmar have also stressed the need to widen the strategically important highway in view of the increasing traffic volume. They said the state government should once again take up the matter with Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari to expedite the project.The state government had earlier submitted the necessary documents to the Centre for declaring the road a national highway, but the proposal was still pending.

headline: PGIMER Chandigarh Secures Third Rank Among India's Best Multi-Speciality Hospitals
content: Chandigarh, November 22, 2026: In a significant national recognition of its excellence in healthcare delivery, the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh, has secured the prestigious *third rank among the Best Multi-Speciality Hospitals in India* in the THE WEEK–HANSA Research Survey. The award was presented at THE WEEK Health Summit 2026, held today at The Ambassador, New Delhi, under the theme 'India Heals | India Innovates'. Dr Ashok Kumar, Medical Superintendent, PGIMER, Chandigarh, received the coveted recognition from the Chief Guest Dr Jitendra Singh, Minister Of State (Independent Charge), Ministry Of Science And Technology, Government Of India. The achievement marks an important milestone in PGIMER's continued journey of excellence and further strengthens its position among the country's leading tertiary healthcare institutions. The ranking is a recognition of the Institute's sustained commitment to delivering comprehensive, quality and affordable healthcare, backed by advanced clinical expertise, cutting-edge technology, research-driven practices and a strong patient-centric approach. Over the decades, PGIMER has evolved into a major national referral centre, catering to patients not only from Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Chandigarh and neighbouring regions but also from across the country. Its multidisciplinary clinical services, highly specialised departments, advanced diagnostic and therapeutic facilities, and commitment to medical education and research have contributed significantly to its standing in the national healthcare landscape. The recognition is particularly significant as it acknowledges the collective contribution of the Institute's faculty, doctors, nursing professionals, healthcare workers, researchers, technical teams and administrative and support staff, whose dedicated efforts ensure the delivery of specialised healthcare services to millions of patients. PGIMER has consistently worked towards strengthening its healthcare infrastructure, expanding specialised services, embracing technological advancements and promoting innovation in clinical care. Its continued emphasis on accessibility, affordability, patient safety and compassionate healthcare remains central to its institutional philosophy.
